name: Ludvika stadslopp
description: Ludvika Stadslopp is an annual running festival that brings together elite runners and recreational runners in Ludvika. The start and finish are at Charlie Normans Square, centrally located between the railway station and the marina. The event is characterized by large crowds, many participants, and a wide range of activities for all ages. Together with partners and volunteers, it creates a wonderful atmosphere of health, exercise, and community.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Charlie Normans Square in Ludvika
A route through the central parts of the town, near the railway station and marina
Large numbers of participants and crowd support create a festive atmosphere
additional: The event has over 1,100 registered participants and offers activities for both young and old. Thanks go to the participants, spectators, volunteers, and partners who make this well-run and popular running festival possible. Information about the start location and event format comes from previous editions and has not been confirmed for 2027.

name: Cityvarvet
description: Cityvarvet is a shorter 4.2-kilometre race that starts at Götaplatsen in central Gothenburg and runs through the city’s tree-lined avenues and cheering crowds before finishing at Slottsskogsvallen. The race is perfect for anyone who finds the Göteborgsvarvet half marathon too long, is a beginner, or wants to experience the festival atmosphere without running the full distance. The course offers a festive running experience, with music and cheer stations along the way. After finishing, participants can access Runners Zone, where they can recover and cheer on the winners of Göteborgsvarvet.
course_highlights: 4.2 kilometres along Gothenburg’s main avenue, Avenyn, and through Slottsskogen
Two water stations with water and sports drink
Music and entertainment stations along the course
additional: Maximum of 1,500 registered participants. Race bib collection takes place at Göteborgsvarvet Expo at Friidrottens Hus from Thursday 20 May to Saturday 22 May. Start at Götaplatsen and finish at Slottsskogsvallen. Access to Runners Zone after finishing, with drinks and snacks. Group registration with invoice payment is available for sports teams and school classes. Participants are recommended to collect their race bib well before the start. Maximum capacity: 1,500 participants. Two water stations with water and sports drink. Registration is open until 12:00 on race day unless the race fills up earlier. Race bibs are collected at Göteborgsvarvet Expo at Friidrottens Hus.

name: Luleå Stadsmara
description: Luleå Stadsmara is a classic recreational race held at the university campus in Porsön, Luleå. The race is aimed particularly at upper secondary school students and offers a spectator-friendly 10 km course that passes through Mjölkudden, the city centre, Lulsundet and Björkskatan before returning to the university. After finishing, participants receive fruit and drinks and have the chance to win great raffle prizes. Timing is done with a chip, and results are reported live online.
course_highlights: Start at the university campus in Porsön
The course passes through Mjölkudden, the city centre, Lulsundet and Björkskatan
A spectator-friendly course, with fruit and drinks after the finish
additional: Race bibs are collected inside Stil Sportcenter, Universitetsvägen 11C, 977 54 Luleå. Registration is through PE teachers. Chip timing and net time. Live results online. Race bibs are collected at the reception of StiL Sportcenter, and timing is done with a chip. Late registration is stated to cost an extra 50 kr.

name: Uka Pain
description: Uka Pain is a series of challenging trail races in Älvdalen, offering distances from 12 km up to 100 miles. The races feature spectacular scenery, high mountain peaks and technical trails, making them one of Sweden’s major autumn running experiences. The start and finish are at Hotell Älvdalen, which also serves as the hub for the race and support. The longest distance, 100 miles, features a unique course consisting of three laps of the 50 km course, with spectacular views from several mountain peaks.
course_highlights: The course passes three of Älvdalen’s highest peaks: Hykjeberg, Skärklitt and Väsaberget
Technical trails and varied terrain, with approximately 1,500 metres of elevation gain on the 52 km course
Start and finish at Hotell Älvdalen, with spa and sauna access available to 100-mile participants
additional: Start and finish at Hotell Älvdalen. Bib pickup at The Running Company near Hotell Älvdalen. Drop bags are permitted for the 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile races, with a maximum size of 60x40x40 cm. Mandatory equipment requirements apply to the 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile races. A bus is provided for 100-mile participants from Hotell Älvdalen to the start at Boggberget. Maximum time limits: 28 km – 10 hours, 50 km – 12 hours, 100 km – 22 hours, 100 miles – 34 hours. A T-shirt is included for registrations made by 30 April. A finisher’s medal is exclusive to the 100-mile race. Spa and sauna access for 100-mile participants. The race takes place on 28–29 May 2027. Bibs can be collected at The Running Company, Dalgatan 81F. Bring your own cup for the aid stations; a participant T-shirt is included for those who register by 30 April 2027.

name: VirsboRUN
description: VirsboRUN is a trail race featuring a varied and exciting course in an untouched nature reserve, partly through Hälleskogsbrännan, the site of a 2014 forest fire. The race offers several distances, from 5.3 km up to a challenging half marathon of 21.2 km, with 101 metres of elevation gain per lap. There is also a free children’s race of approximately 800 metres, suitable for the whole family. The start and finish are at Skräddartorpet, where participants can enjoy medals, freshly grilled hamburgers and a wonderful atmosphere. Everyone is welcome to take part and experience the beautiful, challenging terrain, whatever their age or experience.
course_highlights: Trail race in an untouched nature reserve, with sections through Hälleskogsbrännan, the site of a 2014 forest fire
5.3 km loop with 101 metres of elevation gain per lap
Children’s race of approximately 800 metres, starting and finishing at Skräddartorpet
additional: Start and finish at Skräddartorpet. Warm-up with music and a course presentation before the start. Maximum of four laps (21.2 km), with a time limit of 3 hours. An extra water station is located at approximately the halfway point. A relay option is available for families with children. Race numbers are handed out at the start. The children’s race is not officially timed, and all participants receive a medal and a surprise bag. Freshly grilled hamburgers are available in the finish area after the race. A free children’s race of approximately 800 metres is offered.

name: Å-Varvet
description: Å-Varvet is a classic running race in Eskilstuna, offering a scenic and varied course along the water and through the city’s parks. The race is popular with both elite runners and recreational runners, with a great atmosphere and crowd support along the entire route. It’s a perfect event for anyone looking to challenge themselves in beautiful surroundings while enjoying Eskilstuna’s charm.
course_highlights: The course runs along Eskilstuna’s waterways and through its parks
Varied terrain with both asphalt and gravel
Crowd support along the entire course
additional: The distance is 10,549 metres.

name: Schjongs5ern
location: AKA Arena, Hønefoss idrettspark, Hønefoss, Norway
description: Schjonsfemmern is a friendly running event at Femmern, with distances for all levels, from 5 km to children’s races. The event offers scenic, accurately measured courses combining nature trails and asphalt along the beautiful Storelva, with the highest point in Søndre Park. It takes place by the ice hockey arena in Hønefoss Idrettspark and offers a unique atmosphere for both beginners and experienced runners. All participants receive a medal, and there are cash prizes for the 5 km race as well as many prize draws. After the race, participants can easily find photos of themselves through a photo service.
course_highlights: Fast, officially measured course combining nature trails and asphalt
Runs along the beautiful Storelva, with the highest point in Søndre Park
The children’s race starts and finishes at the venue, and all children receive a medal
additional: Race bibs are distributed at the finish area through a self-service system. The 5 km race has electronic timing, with the timing chip integrated into the race bib; the children’s races are not timed. Participants can choose to run the 5 km without timing. Cash prizes are awarded for the 5 km race (women and men). Everyone receives a finisher’s medal at the finish. Results are published on RaceDays. To comply with GDPR, photos from the children’s races are not published. The start and finish are at AKA Arena in Hønefoss Idrettspark. The 5 km can be run with or without electronic timing. The children’s races are untimed, and all children receive a medal.

description: Ulriken Opp is a popular uphill race in Bergen that takes you to the top of Ulriken, the highest of the seven mountains surrounding the city, with spectacular views of Bergen and the North Sea. The race is suitable for all levels, from competitive runners to recreational runners and families, and offers three distances: the Grieg Oppstemten Opp competitive category, the Drevelin Montana Classic recreational and fitness category, and CaniCross, for running with a dog. All start from Montana and finish at the summit of Ulriken, at 605 metres above sea level. The event offers a social and challenging experience, with a mass start and refreshments available in the finish area.
course_highlights: 1.75 km course with 420 metres of elevation gain from Montana to the summit of Ulriken
Start at Montana gravel field, via Johan Blyttsvei and Oppstemten
Finish at Ulriksmasten, at 605 metres above sea level, with views of Bergen and the North Sea
additional: All categories start together from Montana. The competitive category starts at 11:30, the recreational and fitness category at 10:30, and CaniCross at 10:00. The finish area by Skyskraperen Restaurant and Café offers refreshments and outdoor seating for 250 people. Training races are held before the main race, with prizes and an opportunity to socialise. Three categories: Grieg Oppstemten Opp (competitive), Drevelin Montana Classic (recreational and fitness), and CaniCross. CaniCross has a limited number of places. Parking at Bergen Hostel Montana is listed at 55 kr; public transport is recommended.

name: Bjørndalenmila
description: Bjørndalenmila is a World Athletics-certified road race with a measured course that meets international standards. The race offers officially certified results, making it possible to set a personal best. The course is fast and easy to run, making it perfect for runners who want to test their fitness, whether their goal is a new personal best or an enjoyable race experience.
course_highlights: World Athletics-certified, measured course
Fast, easy-to-run asphalt course
Officially certified results for personal bests

description: Namsosløpet is a long-standing race in Namdalen, with 3.5 km and 8 km routes, as well as a certified 21 km half marathon. The race is suitable for everyone, whether you want to walk, jog or run, and takes place in beautiful surroundings on a mix of paved and gravel roads. The start and finish are in central Namsos, and the event has been held for many years. Welcome to an enjoyable running experience in Trøndelag!
course_highlights: Routes of 3.5 km, 8 km and 21 km (half marathon)
Start and finish in central Namsos
Routes on paved and gravel roads in scenic surroundings
additional: Race bibs can be collected in the start area on Friday, June 5, from 17:00–20:00 and Saturday, June 6, from 10:00–14:00. Mass start: 3.5 km at 14:00 and 8 km at 14:10. Free parking throughout the town on race day. Businesses can request a code and pay the entry fee for their employees. All prices exclude the license fee.

description: Nordlo Sentrumsløpet Haugesund is a fast, officially measured road race starting and finishing at Rådhusplassen in Haugesund. The event offers a 10 km race consisting of two 5 km laps, as well as a new 5 km race on the same route. It is suitable for all levels, from beginners to elite runners, and creates a festive atmosphere in the city centre with closed roads and lively crowds. A children’s race is also held for the youngest participants, and there are opportunities to socialise after the race.
course_highlights: The 10 km route passes through the pedestrian street in Haraldsgaten, around the city park and along Salhusvegen to Karmsund videregående skole
The 5 km route follows the same course as the 10 km race, but covers one lap
Start and finish at Rådhusplassen, with roads closed to traffic
additional: The children’s race starts at 11:00 and covers approximately 500 m for ages 0–12. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. The 5 km race starts at 12:00, the elite 10 km at 13:00 and the main 10 km field at 13:20. Pacers are available, and electronic timing includes gun time and split times. A water and squash station is provided halfway around the course. AfterRUN, with food and drinks for sale, takes place after the race. Race numbers can be collected in advance at Anton Sport Oasen or on race day at Rådhusplassen. Changing facilities and bag storage are available at the start/finish. Roads are closed to traffic during the race. The course is stated to be certified by World Athletics with an AIMS-B certificate. Roads are closed to traffic during the race.

name: Saudafjellet Maraton 2027
description: Saudafjellet Marathon 2027 takes place on Saturday, May 22, in Sauda, Rogaland. This unique race offers spectacular scenery across Saudafjellet, one of Norway’s most impressive mountain passes. Participants can choose between the marathon, half marathon, or Gruvemila, and every distance offers a memorable experience in beautiful surroundings. The race starts at 12:00, and everyone is welcome to enjoy a challenging and wonderful day of running.
course_highlights: Run across Saudafjellet, a spectacular mountain pass
Choose between the marathon, half marathon, and Gruvemila
Scenic surroundings in Sauda, Rogaland
additional: Tickets are sold through EQ Timing via the Aett platform. The event runs from 12:00 to 15:00. Aett offers simple registration and ticket sales administration, with the option to pay at the door. The start time is listed as 12:00. Registration is through EQ Timing, and the organizer has announced an early bird offer.

name: KK-mila
description: KKmila is a friendly race in Oslo offering two distances, 5 km and 10 km, on a flat, easy-to-run course that showcases the city at its best. Thousands of participants come together for a running festival full of good vibes, a sense of achievement and energy. The course follows the waterfront, passes through parks and urban areas, and visits iconic locations such as Aker Brygge and Bjørvika, offering a varied and memorable route. The event also focuses on community and supporting charity through its partnership with Right To Play.
course_highlights: Flat, easy-to-run course along the waterfront and through the city’s parks
Passes well-known areas such as Frognerkilen, Tjuvholmen, Aker Brygge and Bjørvika
Varied, memorable route with a maritime feel and modern architecture
additional: The 5 km starts at 12:00 and the 10 km at 14:00. The race offers pacers, timing, changing rooms, showers and toilets. Participants receive a goodie bag and this year’s medal. Bag storage and a warm-up before the start are available. The event also includes a social after-run dinner for businesses and groups. The race supports the charity Right To Play, and one lucky winner will be drawn to receive a trip to KKcamp in Portugal. The Heia class is untimed, and participants are ranked alphabetically. The listed course starts and finish locations are from 2026 and therefore cannot be confirmed for 2027.

name: 4625løpet 2027
description: The 4625 Run takes place on Flekkerøy, a gem at the edge of the open sea just outside Kristiansand. The race offers varied terrain with many beautiful viewpoints and is suitable for both beginners and elite runners. The course passes through idyllic Southern Norwegian gardens, over the iconic bridge at Skibbusundet, and along the archipelago with views of Oksøy Lighthouse. After crossing the finish line, runners can look forward to a medal, recognition and well-earned refreshments.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with Kodak-friendly viewpoints
Run across the bridge at Skibbusundet, one of the island’s most photographed spots
Views of Oksøy Lighthouse and the beautiful archipelago
additional: The children’s race starts at 10:15 and 10:30, with courses of approximately 300 metres and 1 km. Toilets and changing rooms are available at Flekkerøyhallen, and bag storage is provided in the start area. Electronic timing is used for the 4625 Run, with a minimum age of 11. A water and sports drink station is located about halfway along the course at Geitodden. All participants receive a medal and pizza from Pizzabakeren after the race. Parking is available at the sports facility. Race numbers are distributed on race day from 09:00 and must be worn visibly. Separate children’s race. The main race starts at 11:00.

name: SpareBank 1 Vartdalsstranda Halvmaraton 2027
location: Vartdal skule, Vartdal, Ørsta, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
distance_verbose: Halvmaraton, 10 km, 7 km, 5 km, 0.5 km, 0.1 km
description: SpareBank1 Vartdalsstranda Half Marathon is an inclusive race organized by the non-profit organization Team Joggis, with 100% of the entry fee going to the Norwegian Cancer Society. The race takes place on the fourth Saturday in May and runs through the beautiful valleys of Vartdal, surrounded by high mountains, making for a spectacular and memorable running experience. Participants can choose from several distances, from the half marathon and 10 km to a recreational run and the children’s race, Mini Joggis. The event combines the joy of running with support for a good cause and has strong local involvement.
course_highlights: The race runs through the beautiful valleys of Vartdal and Nordre Vartdal, surrounded by high mountains
The half marathon has 3 water stations along the route (4 km, 10 km, 20 km)
The 10 km race has a water station at 4 km
additional: The recreational category has a flexible start time between 09:00 and 11:00. There is a group warm-up with Mova Ørsta and Bjørnis before the start. Changing facilities and showers are available at Vartdal School. A kiosk serves grilled food and other refreshments. Registration for Mini Joggis and the recreational run takes place at the race office on race day. All participants are entered into prize draws, but must be present at the awards ceremony to win. The half-marathon course has three water stations, and the 10 km course has one at 4 km. Changing facilities and showers are available at Vartdal School. Mini Joggis is 100 or 500 metres, and registration for the children’s race and recreational run takes place at the race office on race day. According to the organizer’s website, 100% of the entry fee goes to the Norwegian Cancer Society.

name: Askøy-På-Langs 2027
organizer: Askøy Turlag, Askøy Orienteringslag og Ask Friidrett
description: Askøy På Langs is a spectacular running and walking event that runs from south to north across Askøy. Participants can choose between three distances: a half distance of 16 km, a full distance of 37.3 km, or an extreme marathon distance. The course offers varied terrain, including the island’s highest point and dense forests, with the start in Kleppestø and the finish at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. The event offers both walking and running categories, and start times are carefully planned to avoid conflicts between runners and walkers. There is also increased toilet capacity and photographers along the way to capture the experience.
course_highlights: Varied terrain over the island’s highest point
Course from Kleppestø to Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort
Start times arranged to avoid conflicts between runners and walkers
additional: The full-distance race starts at Kleppestø quay at 08:00, while the half distance (16 km) starts from Træet School at 12:00. All distances finish at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. Basic first-aid supplies are available at the start/finish and at the food stations. Toilet capacity has been increased at Kleppestø quay and Træet. A photographer will be present along the course at a marked location. The full distance starts at 08:00 and the half distance at 12:00. All distances finish at Herdla Museum at Herdla Fort. The event is run on a voluntary, non-commercial basis.

name: Bėgimo varžybos Pavelo Fedorenkos ir Kupiškio r. Kūno kultūros ir sporto centro prizams laimėti
organizer: Kupiškio r. kūno kultūros ir sporto centras
description: The running competition for the prizes of Pavel Fedorenka and the Kupiškis District Physical Education and Sports Centre invites participants to register and compete. The event is held in Kupiškis to promote sporting activity and community spirit. It is a great opportunity to test your abilities and enjoy running in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: The event is open to all age groups
Compete for prizes from Pavel Fedorenka and the Kupiškis District Physical Education and Sports Centre
Location: Kupiškis, Lithuania
additional: The event will take place on May 29, 2027. Registration is available online and via social media.

name: Botaniczna Piątka Gdynia – edycja wiosenna 2026
description: Botaniczna Piątka Gdynia – Spring Edition 2026 is a cross-country race held in the picturesque Marszewo Forest Botanical Garden in Gdynia. The event is part of the Botaniczna Piątka race series, which has been promoting running and the beauty of natural routes in Poland since 2014. The race attracts running enthusiasts who value being close to nature and the beauty of their surroundings. It’s a great opportunity to spend time outdoors among the greenery and enjoy a unique atmosphere.

name: Bieg Lwa
description: The Lion Run is an annual half marathon held in Tarnowo Podgórne, attracting both elite runners and amateurs. The event is known for its excellent organization, appealing course, and enthusiastic crowds. The festival also features children’s races and a variety of accompanying events, such as cheering competitions and concerts. The Lion Run is a great opportunity for sporting competition and family fun in beautiful surroundings.

name: Bieg Poznaniaka
organizer: Stowarzyszenie na Rzecz Edukacji Dzieci i Młodzieży z Autyzmem „Aperio”
description: Bieg Poznaniaka dla Przedszkolaka is a family running event taking place on May 23, 2026, in the scenic Wielkopolski National Park and on the grounds of the Museum of Agriculture in Szreniawa. The program includes main races of 11 km and 5.5 km, a Nordic Walking march, and children’s and youth races over various distances. The event is charitable, with all proceeds going to support children with autism. Organizers provide electronic timekeeping, commemorative medals, and numerous activities for participants and their families, including free museum admission and outdoor games for children.

name: Nowomiejska Dycha
organizer: Urząd Miejski w Nowym Mieście Lubawskim
description: Nowomiejska Dycha is a special night-time street race taking place on 23 May 2026 in Nowe Miasto Lubawskie. The course runs along the town’s atmospheric, historic streets, offering participants a unique experience and the chance to compete for attractive prizes. The programme includes two races: a 5 km race at 18:00 and a 10 km race at 20:00. Both start and finish at Nowomiejski Market Square. Participants can look forward to generous race packs, post-race meals and a great time in charming surroundings.

name: Phoenix RUN
organizer: Klub Biegowy Phoenix Contact Wielkopolska i Opalenicki Klub Biegacza
description: Phoenix RUN is a unique sporting event held in a picturesque forest near the Smolarnia forester’s lodge, close to Nowy Tomyśl. It is the second edition of the race, organized by the Phoenix Contact Wielkopolska Running Club, bringing together running and Nordic walking enthusiasts. The event offers a range of distances for adults and children, encouraging active time with family and friends. Participants can look forward to generous race packs, commemorative medals and attractive prizes, as well as a chance to socialize and enjoy the chillout zone.

name: XV Biegiem po Wichrowskich Lasach
description: The 15th Run Through the Wichrowo Forests is an annual running event organized by the Wichrowo Forest District, attracting people who enjoy spending active time outdoors in nature. The main event is a 10 km race through scenic forest areas. There are also races for children and young people, people with intellectual disabilities, and a Nordic walking event. The start and finish are located at the Wichrowo Forest District office, and participants can take part in a familiarization run on the course.

name: XXVIII Bieg Święców
description: The 28th Święców Run in Sławno is an annual running event taking place on May 23, 2026. The 10 km main race follows city streets, including asphalt roads, basalt paving and asphalt bike paths. The course is secured and marked, with water stations along the route. The event also includes races for children and young people at the athletics stadium, over distances from 50 to 600 metres. The organisers promote community togetherness and a healthy lifestyle.

name: V Ultra Nordic Walking World Records
Stadionloppet
description: Stadionloppet is a family-friendly running event held at Stockholm Olympic Stadium. The main race is 5 km long and takes place on a scenic two-lap course created by Kalle Berglund. The event is marked by a wonderful sense of community, where children, young people and adults can all take part and cheer one another on. The start, lap point and finish are at the beautiful stadium, offering a unique running experience in a setting where the buzz of the city meets greenery and birdsong.
course_highlights: 5 km two-lap course around Stockholm Olympic Stadium
Course created by Kalle Berglund, a former world-class runner
Start, lap point and finish at Stockholm Olympic Stadium
additional: All members of Djurgården Friidrott run for free and receive a registration code when they join. Several shorter distances are available for children and young people. Members can also take part as volunteers and be part of the event. Start times and categories are preliminary and may change. Stadiongirot, a cycling race held in collaboration with Djurgården Cykel, also takes place on the same day. Members of Djurgården Friidrott can run for free with a registration code. Distance and category details for 2027 are preliminary and may change. Free trial training on the course is held ahead of the race.

name: Lustraløpet
price_range: Aktiv klasse: 250 kr + eventuell lisens; trimklasse: 150 kr; familie i trimklassen: 300 kr

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Påmeldingsavgift aktiv klasse: kr. 250,-+ ev. lisens om du ikkje har heilårslisens.

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Påmeldingsavgift trimklasse familie kr. 300,- ( familie = føresette med born under 18 år)

description: Lustraløpet is a traditional 10 km road race on asphalt, starting at Neshøgdi and finishing at Luster oppvekstsenter. The race is held annually and is known for its beautiful scenery and excellent prizes made by local producers and artists. Great emphasis is placed on volunteer effort to ensure a successful event. In addition to the competitive class, there is a recreational class for those who want a social and scenic outing without timing.
course_highlights: 10 km road race on asphalt
Starts at Neshøgdi and finishes at Luster oppvekstsenter
Scenic surroundings and prizes featuring local art
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Nes/by the start no later than 13:45. Free shuttle buses run between Luster and Nes, but travelling by your own transport is recommended due to summer traffic. Changing rooms with showers are available in the finish area. The recreational class starts between 11:00 and 13:30. All participants receive free betasuppe (soup) with flatbread and cordial at the finish. A kiosk sells ice cream, soft drinks, lapper (Norwegian pancakes), betasuppe, cordial and hot dogs. Cash prizes are awarded for the sprint prize, best time and course record. The competitive class is for participants aged 13 and over. Free shuttle buses run between Luster and Nes, changing rooms with showers are available at the finish, and participants are served betasuppe with flatbread and cordial. Prices are based on the published information for 2026 and may change before the 2027 race.

name: Åsaneløpet 2027
price_range: 150–400 kr, i tillegg til lisens fra 13 år
description: Åsaneløpet is a traditional fun run in the heart of Åsane, Bergen, inviting the whole family to take part. The race offers 5 km and 10 km distances, as well as a children’s race where every child receives a medal and the first 800 participants receive a T-shirt. The event offers a fun race-day atmosphere with a warm-up, awards ceremony, and activities such as a bouncy castle and face painting, and is suitable for both young and adult runners.
course_highlights: Run in the heart of Åsane with a lead bicycle riding ahead of the runners
100-metre children’s race for the youngest participants, with a medal for everyone
Group warm-up with MOVA before the start
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts (children only) can be collected from 11:00 on race day outside Building A at Thon Senter Åsane. The warm-up for the children’s race with MOVA starts at 11:45. The children’s race (approx. 100 m) starts at 12:00. Group warm-up with MOVA at 12:50. The 5 km and 10 km races start at 13:00, with a lead bicycle riding ahead of the runners. Awards and activities such as a bouncy castle, face painting, and athletics trials take place after the race. Children below 3rd grade run 100 metres. There is a water station at the turnaround point on the 10 km route. All children receive a medal, and the first 800 participants receive a T-shirt.

name: Bėgam už Marijampolę - 2026
description: Bėgam už Marijampolę is a traditional annual running event held in Marijampolė, bringing together participants of all ages. It is not only a competition but also an outdoor gathering for local residents that encourages an active lifestyle and a sense of community. The event features an updated running course where participants can test their endurance in a beautiful Lithuanian city. It also includes the “Einam už Marijampolę” walking tour, with 8 km and 14 km distances and free registration.
course_highlights: Updated running course in Marijampolė
Walking tour with 8 km and 14 km distances
Outdoor event that encourages a sense of community
additional: The “Einam už Marijampolę” walking tour takes place alongside the running event, and registration for the tour is free. The event brings together more than 1,000 participants, from the youngest to the oldest. Organized by the Marijampolė Athletics Sports Club. Event date: May 30, 2027; participant numbers and race distances are not specified.

name: Spatzenberg-Lauf
description: The Spatzenberg Run is a traditional fun run in Löhne, following a hilly circular course around and over the Spatzenberg in the nature reserve. The route runs mostly on paved paths and roads and offers an attractive running opportunity for all age groups. In addition to the 9 km main race, there are shorter 6 km and 3 km races for schoolchildren. The event is organised by Turn- und Rasensportverein Löhne 1910 e.V., running group, and takes place at the Obernfeld sports field.
course_highlights: Hilly circular course around and over the Spatzenberg (nature reserve)
Route on paved paths and roads
Distances: 9 km, 6 km and 3 km schoolchildren’s race
additional: Timing is provided by a disposable chip attached to the back of the race bib. Race materials can be collected from 9:00 on the event day at the Obernfeld sports field. Late entries are possible on the event day until 10:15, while race bibs are available. Payment by SEPA direct debit for online registration or in cash when collecting race materials. Hilly course around the Spatzenberg, registration online or on the event day, timing with a disposable chip, water at the finish station

name: 12 Bieg Elegant na 5
description: The 12th Elegant na 5 Run is an annual running event held in Mosina, scheduled for May 24 in 2026. The event offers a variety of distances for children, young people and people with disabilities, as well as a 5 km main race that runs through the streets of the Mosina municipality. The start and finish are at Plac 20 Października, and the main race begins at 11:15. Participants can choose a basic or extended package with a T-shirt, making the event appealing to a wide range of runners.

name: BoryRun
description: BoryRun 2026 is the largest running festival in the Lower Silesian Forests, taking place on May 24, 2026, in Osiecznica. The event combines sport, health, and mindful time offline, promoting intergenerational connection and the joy of movement without the pressure of competition. The routes pass through the scenic Lower Silesian Forests and the historic setting of Kliczków Castle, offering a chance to connect with the region’s nature and history. Children can take part in the special Boryrun Active race, featuring activities that build fitness and self-confidence.

name: Gontyniec Ultra Trail
description: Gontyniec Ultra Trail is a mountain trail race held on the picturesque Gontyniec Hill in Chodzież, the highest elevation in the Greater Poland Lake District. The courses run mainly along forest trails marked with red and yellow signs, offering runners a variety of distances and elevation gains. Organized by the Gontyniec Ultra Trail Foundation, the event attracts cross-country and ultrarunning enthusiasts from across Poland, offering unique challenges over distances from 12 to 52 km. This iconic event combines sporting competition with the beauty of nature and the history of the region.

name: Prusice Biegają - etap 2
description: The 13th edition of Prusice Biegają is a sporting event held on Żmigrodzka Street, next to the Prusice Fitness Center in Prusice. The course runs along the streets of Prusice and through Pietrowice Małe, offering participants scenic and runner-friendly conditions. The event is a great opportunity to spend time actively and compete within the local running community.

name: VI Niechanowska Dyszka i Piątka
description: The 6th Niechanowo 10K and 5K is an annual race held in the picturesque Planty Park in Niechanowo. The event offers two popular race distances: 10 km and 5 km, attracting both recreational and more experienced runners. It is an athletics event and a great opportunity to spend time outdoors in a friendly atmosphere. The organizers provide professional timekeeping and technical support.

name: XII Bieg z książką
description: The 12th Run with a Book, ON THE TRAIL TO THE FINISH, is an open running event organized by the Nicolaus Copernicus University Alumni Program and the NCUM Marathon Club. It is dedicated to the Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń community and to fans of running and reading. The race takes place on the university campus in Bielany, Toruń, and its route follows forest paths and lanes through the campus woodland. Participants must complete the course while holding a book weighing at least 100 grams, highlighting the event’s unique combination of sport and the promotion of reading. The race is sponsored by Robert Małecki, a crime fiction author and NCUM alumnus, who takes part in the race and meets participants after the competition.

name: Blodomloppet (Umeå)

price_tiers.distance: Promenad 5 km, löpning 5 km och 10 km

description: Blodomloppet in Umeå is a recreational event that raises awareness of the vital importance of blood donation and welcomes everyone to walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km. The event is open to participants of all ages and abilities, including children and teams, and ends with a shared picnic. It is a social and healthy activity that promotes community and wellbeing while supporting a good cause. Blodomloppet is part of Sweden’s largest recreational running event, with a strong focus on blood donation and health.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km courses in Umeå
The children’s race, Lilla Blodomloppet
Shared picnic after the race
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts can be collected at IFK Umeå’s club premises on 21–22 May and 24 May, and at Väven on 25 May. Teams of at least 5 people receive a picnic bag. Blood donors receive a discount of SEK 40 per person. Registration changes are free of charge until 21 May; after that, changes require an in-person visit and cost SEK 50. An order ID is required to collect race bibs. Blood donors receive a discount of SEK 40 per person. The last day to register a team and receive the picnic bag offer is 18 May. Individual registration is stated to be available until 25 May.

name: Jentebølgen - Kristiansand
description: Jentebølgen in Kristiansand is an inclusive public health run taking place on 24 May 2027, with the start and finish at Tresse. The course is approximately 5 km long and suitable for everyone, whether you want to walk, jog or run. The event focuses on community, a sense of achievement and mental health, and supports Mental Helse Ungdom with NOK 10 per race entry sold. It is a colourful and lively experience with entertainment, medals for all participants, and the option to take part as a company or sports club.
course_highlights: Approximately 5 km course starting and finishing at Tresse, Kristiansand
Accessible course that also allows strollers
Colourful Color Run with costumes, a mini-concert and medals for everyone
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the event site two hours before the start, but collecting them in advance is recommended to avoid queues. Stands open one hour before the race, and entertainment begins 30–45 minutes before the start. Jackets and bags can be left in a tent by the event office; storage is at your own risk. Companions can participate for free upon showing a companion certificate. There is no official timing, but participants can use their own watch. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. Race numbers can be collected at the event site on race day.

name: 01. Godelheimer See Marathon
description: The 1st Godelheim Lake Marathon/Ultra in Höxter takes place on May 25, 2026, and is a premiere with DUV scoring. The event gives runners the opportunity to experience a new route around Godelheim Lake. The race is aimed at marathon and ultramarathon runners and promises a varied and challenging course in a natural setting. The organizer is the 100 Marathon Club Deutschland, a club for experienced marathon runners.

name: Vårruset Jönköping
organizer: Marathongruppen med Hässelby SK och Spårvägens FK
description: Vårruset in Jönköping is part of Sweden’s largest fitness tour for women, where participants can run, jog or walk 2.5 or 5 km on a certified course. The event is all about the joy of movement and togetherness, with a wonderful atmosphere among women. Everyone who finishes receives a medal and a finish-line bag, and teams of five are treated to a picnic after the finish. It’s a festive spring evening with entertainment and encouragement along the course and at the event area by Lake Rocksjön in Knektaparken.
course_highlights: Certified 5 km course
Two distances: 2.5 km and 5 km
Event area by Lake Rocksjön in Knektaparken
additional: You can opt out of timekeeping when registering, which means your result will not be published in the results list. Teams of five are treated to a picnic after the finish. The recommended age is 13 for the 5 km and 11 for the 2.5 km, with younger participants permitted when accompanied by an adult. Registration is binding and can be completed up to one hour before the first start on race day. All participants who finish receive a medal and a finish-line bag. Teams of five receive a picnic after the finish.

organizer: Strands IF Friidrott i samarbete med GeBlod Gävleborg

description: Blodomloppet in Hudiksvall is a fun run that raises awareness of the vital importance of blood donation. You can walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km, either on your own or together with colleagues and friends. The event is part of Sweden’s largest fun run series, with a strong focus on health and social connection, and traditionally ends with a large picnic. Blodomloppet is open to everyone and promotes a healthy lifestyle while supporting youth activities in the organizing clubs.
course_highlights: Timed 5 km and 10 km courses
Lilla Blodomloppet for children
Water stations along the course
additional: The event offers discounted team registration and an Excel template for large groups. Changing facilities, toilets, storage, water stations and medical assistance are available on site. After the event, participants can enjoy a large picnic. The main races start at 18:30. The event is organized by Strands IF Friidrott together with GeBlod Gävleborg. Timed 5 km and 10 km races are available. Lilla Blodomloppet is available for children.

name: Jentebølgen - Stavanger
description: Jentebølgen in Stavanger is an inclusive public health run organised in cooperation with Mental Helse Ungdom. The course is between 5 and 6 kilometres long, and participants can walk, jog or run on accessible terrain. The event offers a colourful and lively experience, with entertainment, a mini-concert before the start and a medal for everyone who finishes. Jentebølgen is more than a race—it is a place for people of all ages to connect through achievement, joy and community.
course_highlights: The course is 5–6 km long and accessible
Color Run with colourful costumes and colour along the course
Mini-concert featuring young artists before the start
additional: Race numbers can be collected at the venue two hours before the start, or in advance to avoid queues. Stands open one hour before the race starts. Jackets and bags can be left in a tent by the event office; storage is at your own risk. Companions participate for free upon presentation of a companion certificate. All participants receive a medal. Companies and sports clubs can register groups using dedicated group tickets. All participants receive a medal. Race numbers can be collected at the venue on race day. The venue for the 2027 event has not yet been announced.

name: Bolechowo na Sportowo
organizer: Centrum Rozwoju Kultury Fizycznej AKWEN w Czerwonaku
description: Bolechowo Sporty, or Active Czerwonak at Night, is a recurring, free sporting event organized by the Centre for the Development of Physical Culture in Czerwonak. The event takes place in the evening and combines physical activity with bringing the local community together. It is a long-standing tradition that attracts participants who want to spend time outdoors, running or walking in a friendly atmosphere.
additional: The event is free and takes place from 19:30 to 22:00. This evening sporting event is part of the Czerwonak Grand Prix series. There is no information about participant limits, fees, or start waves. Previous events have taken place in the evening; available results from one edition indicate a distance of 5 km.

name: Vårruset Karlstad
organizer: Vårruset i samarbete med IF Göta Karlstad
description: Vårruset in Karlstad is a popular spring running event offering a lovely, friendly running experience for women of all ages. The race follows a 5 km course, with both timed and untimed participation options. After the finish, teams of five are treated to a picnic, creating a pleasant opportunity to socialize. The event area is located between Sundstagymnasiet and Sundstabadet, and the organizer encourages participants to travel to the start in an environmentally friendly way.
course_highlights: 5 km course, timed or untimed
Start and finish in the area between Sundstagymnasiet and Sundstabadet
Picnic after the finish for teams of 5
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Intersport Bergvik in the days before the event and at the venue from 15:00 on race day. Race information is sent out about one week before the event. There is a supervised area where participants can leave their warm-up clothes before the start. The organizer recommends cycling or taking public transport to the event area. City buses are free upon presentation of a race bib or race information. Teams consist of 5 people and must be complete no later than one month before the event to receive picnic vouchers. Changing rooms are available at Sundsta Sports Hall. Teams registered with five people receive a picnic after the finish. Individual participants receive a medal, a finish-line bag, and a race bib.

name: Gladsheim Finspångs Stadslopp

price_tiers.distance: Gladsheim Finspångs Stadslopp (7 km) och AktivRundan (3,8 km)

description: Gladsheim Finspång City Race is an annual fun run through beautiful Finspång, starting and finishing in Bruksparken. The race offers a 7-kilometre course with smooth, even surfaces, ideal for both runners and recreational participants. For a shorter challenge, there is AktivRundan, approximately 3.8 kilometres with no timing, and children can take part in XL Bygg Lilla Slottsrundan, a 1.7-kilometre route through an easy-to-run park setting. All participants receive a medal and energy products, and there are great prizes to be won. The race is open to everyone, whether they walk, jog or run.
course_highlights: 7 km course with smooth, even surfaces through central Finspång
AktivRundan: 3.8 km without timing for walkers and joggers
XL Bygg Lilla Slottsrundan: 1.7 km for children through an easy-to-run park setting
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Stora Coop Finspång/Viberga on Tuesday, 26 May, between 15:00 and 19:00. Late registration is available at the bib collection point and at the start and finish area from 15:00 on race day. Timing uses a chip on the race bib tab; without it, no time will be recorded. The children’s race has four start times between 17:00 and 18:00, depending on age group. All participants receive a medal, energy products and a water bottle sponsored by local businesses. The children’s race prize-giving takes place on the stage in Bruksparken at 18:15. The race’s official website currently provides information about the 2026 edition; prices and practical details for 2027 have not been specified.

description: Blodomloppet in Uppsala is a recreational race that highlights the life-saving importance of blood donation and welcomes participants to walk, jog or run the 5 km and 10 km distances. The race is open to everyone, whether taking part alone or with colleagues and friends. There are also special races, including Lilla Blodomloppet and Specialomloppet, for different ages and abilities. Blodomloppet is a social and healthy activity that ends with a shared picnic and helps promote blood donation and youth sports in the region.
course_highlights: The 10 km course is officially measured and runs through Uppsala
The 5 km and 2.5 km courses are popular but not officially measured
Option to participate as a team of 5
additional: Team registration for 5 people is available. An Excel template for large registrations can be downloaded. The 10 km course is officially measured, while the 5 km and 2.5 km distances are approximate. Dogs are welcome to participate. A shared picnic is offered after the race. Water stations are located along the course. Changing facilities and toilets are available. Medical services are on site. Race bibs are distributed before the start. The race highlights the importance of blood donation.

name: Jentebølgen - Bergen
description: Jentebølgen Bergen 2027 brings together girls and women of all ages for an afternoon filled with a sense of achievement, community, and a great atmosphere. The event takes place on 26 May 2027 in Bergen and invites you to enjoy running and energy with friends, colleagues, or family. The entry fee includes insurance and the ticket fee, creating a unique sense of community on the starting line.
course_highlights: A course of between 5 and 6 km
Participants can walk, jog, or run
A handicap-accessible course
additional: The entry fee includes insurance and the ticket fee. The event runs from 17:30 to 20:00. Participants are encouraged to join with friends, colleagues, or family for a social and energetic running experience. There is no timing, and all participants receive a medal. The entry fee includes insurance and the ticket fee. The venue has not yet been announced.

name: Bėgimas „Kutaliai – Kaltinėnai“
description: The “Kutaliai–Kaltinėnai” run is a traditional cross-country race held to commemorate the 141st anniversary of the birth of Aleksandras Stulginskis, President of the Republic of Lithuania, and the Day of the Constituent Seimas. The race takes place over hilly terrain, encouraging physical activity and respect for sport. The start is in Kutaliai village, and the finish is at the stadium of Aleksandras Stulginskis Gymnasium in Kaltinėnai, Šilalė District. The event is for athletes from city and district schools and anyone else who meets the health requirements.

name: Sternchenlauf
description: The Sternchenlauf in Schloß Holte-Stukenbrock is a traditional fun run held annually on the Wednesday before Corpus Christi. The event offers various races for all age groups, from races for toddlers and children to 5 km and 10 km races, as well as walking. The course follows a varied 2.5 km loop with forest trails, gravel and asphalt, lined with enthusiastic spectators. In addition to individual categories, there are team and relay categories, making the race especially appealing to groups.
course_highlights: A varied 2.5 km loop with forest trails, gravel and asphalt
Flat course with clear signage
Out-and-back courses for the toddler, children’s and schoolchildren’s races on Falkenstraße
additional: Start times: toddler race 17:00, children’s race 17:15, 1.0 km schoolchildren’s race 17:30, 2.5 km schoolchildren’s race 17:45, 5 km race 18:30, 10 km race and 5 km walk 19:30. The walk starts at the same time as the 10 km race, at the back of the field. Participant limit: approximately 2,000; relays are limited to 50. Event shirts can be purchased during registration or on site. Changing rooms and showers are available. Start and finish at the Waldstadion Schwarz-Weiß Sende e.V. Registration is available for individual and group races. The 5 km race is fully booked; remaining places will be available on site from 16:00 on the day of the event. The event is part of the region’s running events and offers a welcoming, family atmosphere.

name: B2Run Hannover
description: The B2Run Hannover on May 27, 2026, is a company run over a largely flat route of around 6.5 km along the Maschsee, finishing spectacularly in the Heinz von Heiden Arena. The event is aimed at companies, organizations, and individual participants from Hannover and the surrounding area, and promotes team spirit, motivation, and a sense of community. It offers a professional supporting program with hosting and music, and is ideal for beginners, walkers, and experienced runners. The focus is on fun, togetherness, and team building, not on personal bests.

name: Steglitzer Volkslauf
description: The Steglitz Fun Run is a long-standing running event taking place on 27 May 2026 at Stadion Lichterfelde in Berlin-Lichterfelde. Organized by TuS Lichterfelde von 1887 e.V., the event offers a sporting opportunity for runners of all ages. It is known for its friendly atmosphere and well-organized event. The races start and finish at Stadion Lichterfelde, providing an attractive setting for participants and spectators.

description:
The course winds around S:t Hans Backar in Lund. In the ultra classes, the goal is to run as many laps as possible in 6 hours. The 10 km runners complete 4 laps and the 5 km runners complete 2 laps. Extreme One runners complete one lap.

One lap is 2.55 km with 140 metres of elevation gain. This means 10.2 km and 560 m of elevation gain for the 10 km, and 5.1 km and 280 m of elevation gain for the 5 km. Each lap in the ultra classes is extended with a flat section where runners go out and back along the same route so they can cheer each other on. The ultra-class lap is 4.38 km in total.
course_highlights: The course runs through S:t Hans Backar: technical trail with clear climbs and descents
One lap is 2.55 km with 140 m of elevation gain (10 km = ~10.2 km, 560 m of elevation gain; 5 km = ~5.1 km, 280 m of elevation gain)
The ultra lap is 4.38 km, including an out-and-back section where runners can cheer each other on; ultra-class runners complete as many laps as possible in 6 hours
additional:
The ultra starts at 14:00; the other classes start from 17:45.
Registration is at

description: Blodomloppet in Örebro is a fun run that raises awareness of the vital importance of blood donation and welcomes everyone to walk, jog or run with friends, family or colleagues. The event offers several distances, including 5 km, 10 km, Specialomloppet and Lilla Blodomloppet for children. It is a social, healthy activity that also promotes team spirit and wellbeing, with the option to take part in teams of five. After the race, participants often gather for a picnic, and the event area is well equipped for an enjoyable day for the whole family.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km courses for women and men
Specialomloppet, approximately 2.1 km
Lilla Blodomloppet: approximately 750 m or 2.1 km for children aged 1–12
additional: You can register individually or as a team of five, with the option to fill vacant places later. Discounts are available for blood donors and ICA Stammis members (SEK 40), but not during late registration. There is no age limit for the 5 km and 10 km distances, but participants should be able to complete the course on their own or accompanied by an adult. Lilla Blodomloppet is for children aged 1–12, and adults may accompany them as long as they do not disturb others. A large picnic is offered to participants after the race. You can use your wellness allowance when registering. The race takes place at Trängens IP. You can register individually or as a team of five. Participants receive, among other things, a T-shirt, race bib and medal; prices vary depending on the distance and registration date.

name: Vårruset
organizer: Marathongruppen, tillsammans med Hässelby SK, Spårvägens FK och lokal arrangör KFUM Örebro Friidrott

description: Vårruset in Örebro is a popular spring running event offering distances of 2.5 km and 5 km on a course measured for accuracy. The race is open to all ages, with a recommended minimum age of 7 for the shorter distance when accompanied by an adult, and 11 for the longer distance. Participants receive a medal, a race bag, a race number, and the option of timekeeping for the 5 km. Teams that register are offered a shared picnic after the finish, creating a lovely social spring evening at Gustavsviksbadet. The event is all about community and enjoyment, with activities and a music quiz for participants.
course_highlights: Course measured for accuracy: 5 km
Start and finish at Gustavsviksbadet
Water station and toilets at the event area
additional: Race-number collection takes place at Intersport Marieberg in the days leading up to the race. Picnic for teams of 5 after the finish. The event area is at Gustavsvik Camping, where parking is limited; participants are encouraged to travel in an environmentally friendly way. Changing at home is recommended. A water station and toilets are available on site. Participants can leave warm-up clothes in a bag marked with their name and race number. Race information is sent by email approximately two weeks before the event. Timekeeping is available as an optional extra for the 5 km. For the 2.5 km, the recommended minimum age is 11, or 7 when accompanied by an adult; for the 5 km, the recommended minimum age is 13, or 11 when accompanied by an adult. Information for Örebro 2027 has not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Leśna Piątka Pikuś
description: Leśna Piątka Pikuś is a cross-country race held in the picturesque forest of the Karnieszewice Forest District in Koszalin. The 10 km route passes through charming woodland, with numerous uphill and downhill sections and a stretch alongside a deep ravine, making the race challenging and full of excitement. Every participant who completes the distance will receive a commemorative medal. The start and finish are at the car park by the educational trail, providing easy access and convenient logistics.

name: Eksjö Stadslopp
description: Eksjö Stadslopp is a community race that welcomes runners of all ages and ability levels. The race takes you through the beautiful wooden town of Eksjö and offers a wonderful running experience filled with energy, community and joy. Proceeds from the race go to Eksjö Södra IK’s children’s and youth activities, so taking part also supports a good cause. The start and finish are at Stora Torget in Eksjö, and the event has a friendly, inclusive atmosphere.
course_highlights: The race goes through one of Sweden’s most beautiful wooden towns
The course is available in several distances, including 10 km and 5 km fun runs
Start and finish at Stora Torget in Eksjö
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Snäckan beside the swimming pool. Changing facilities are available at Prästängshallen until 21:30 on race day. Start times vary by class, with children’s races starting from 18:00 onwards; the men’s and women’s 10 km races start at 19:30, and the 5 km fun run starts at 19:50. Group registration is available by email, with invoicing. Results are published on the club’s website after the race. The race programme also includes a 1,000-metre youth race and a 600-metre children’s race. Proceeds support Eksjö Södra IK’s children’s and youth activities.

name: Lindahls Helsingborg Night Run
description: Lindahls Helsingborg Night Run is a festive evening race that starts as the sun sets at Gröningen in Helsingborg. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km on a fast, flat course along the city’s beautiful waterfront promenade, with sea views. The race is all about joy, community and a spectator-friendly atmosphere with music and a festive vibe. It’s a race for everyone, whether you want to run fast or enjoy running in the evening light.
course_highlights: Fast, flat course with only 2 metres of elevation change per lap
The course follows Helsingborg’s waterfront promenade, with sea views
The 10 km race consists of two laps, passing through Gröningen, where the crowd provides extra energy
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Löplabbet Helsingborg in the days before the race and at the venue from 20:00. Bag storage is available from 20:00 in the start and finish area. Löplabbet Pacers will be on hand to pace runners to several finish times in both the 5 km and 10 km races. An After Run party with food and drinks from partners takes place immediately after finishing. Maximum of 1500 participants to ensure high quality. Time limit: 90 minutes. Entry transfers are possible for a fee until 17 May 2026. Distance options are 5 km and 10 km.

name: adidas Shake Out Run
description: The adidas Shake Out Run is a 5 km race starting and finishing at Stockholm Olympic Stadium. It’s a perfect warm-up for participants running the Stockholm Marathon the following day, as well as an opportunity for other runners to experience the unique marathon atmosphere during the event weekend. The first 1,000 people to register will receive an adidas T-shirt in their chosen size to run in, distributed at the event. After the race, people who register later can also collect T-shirts in the remaining sizes.
course_highlights: 5 km distance, starting and finishing at Stockholm Olympic Stadium
The race serves as a warm-up for the Stockholm Marathon
A unique marathon atmosphere during the event weekend
additional: Age limit: 13 years (11 years when accompanied by a parent or guardian). Late registration is available online until 1 hour before the first start. Payment options include online banking, Visa, MasterCard, Swish, and invoice via Klarna. The event is organised by the athletics clubs Hässelby SK and Spårvägens FK. The age limit is 13 years, or 11 years when accompanied by a parent or guardian. Late registration can be completed online until one hour before the first start.

name: 3. Benno Viirandi nimeline rahvajooks
description: The 3rd Benno Viirand Memorial Fun Run is a family-oriented running and Nordic walking event held in Mustla. The race follows a 5 km course, starting near the Vambola bus stop in Soe village and finishing at the Tarvastu Gymnasium stadium. The event aims to honour the memory of the legendary runner Benno Viirand and promote running as a healthy way to spend time. In addition to the main race, free children’s races are held at the stadium. Participants are provided with race numbers and can register in advance or in person on race day.

name: Abendlauf Wilstedt bei Nacht
description: The Wilstedt Night Run takes place on 29 May 2026, transforming the village of Wilstedt into an atmospheric race course. The event is family-friendly and open to everyone, from beginners to experienced runners. The new course offers lovely views of the village at night. Cheering spectators and an evening fireworks display add to the atmosphere.
course_highlights: New course through Wilstedt with lovely views of the village
Atmospheric setting with cheering spectators along the course
Floodlit swimming at Heidebad Wilstedt after the run until 22:30
additional: The start and finish are at the Wilstedt sports grounds. The event begins with the mini run at 20:15, followed by the jogging and walking starts. Late entries are available on the event day from 18:30 to 20:00 and cost 9 euros. T-shirts or functional shirts are only available to participants who register in advance and will be handed out on the event day. After the run, floodlit swimming at Heidebad Wilstedt is free until 22:30. Fireworks bring the event to a close at around 22:45. Nordic walking poles are not allowed on the course. Child and running strollers are permitted only for the hiking/walking event. Shower and changing facilities are available on a limited basis. New course through Wilstedt, family-friendly, evening event, registration until 17 May, including a mini run, fireworks and musical entertainment.

name: Lauf Rund um Burg
description: The 37th Run Around the Castle is part of the Cross and Forest Run Series and takes place around Burg in Dithmarschen. The event gives runners the opportunity to run scenic routes of 4.8 km and 10 km. The race is distinguished by its natural surroundings and varied course. Participants can look forward to a friendly atmosphere and a well-organized event.

name: Mühlhäuser Röblinglauf
description: The Mühlhäuser Röblinglauf is a charity run with the unique concept “Sport meets Music,” supporting the Mitteldeutschland Children’s Hospice. The event offers various races for children, teenagers, companies and individual runners, as well as walkers. Alongside the sporting event, there is musical entertainment and a KinderGarten concert, making the run a special experience for participants and spectators. Race materials can be collected the day before, and an AfterRöblinglauf Party takes place after the run.

name: Nacht von Hasbergen
description: The Night of Hasbergen is a traditional road race held on Friday, May 29, 2026, in Hasbergen. The event offers exciting races for all ages, from the Bambini run and relay race to the 10 km main race. The races take place on a new course that was changed because of construction work. The event begins with an opening ceremony and a show for the Bambini runners and concludes with awards ceremonies for the various races.

name: adidas Stockholm Marathon
description: The adidas Stockholm Marathon is a classic marathon that takes place this year on 30 May 2026 and attracts both elite and recreational runners. The race is 42,195 metres long, measured according to current regulations, and follows a new course through central Stockholm. The event is organised by athletics clubs Hässelby SK and Spårvägens FK, and the organisers highlight extensive runner services along the course. The race starts at Stockholm Olympic Stadium and offers seeding opportunities through events including adidas Premiärmilen and adidas Premiärhalvan.
course_highlights: 42,195 metres, measured according to the Swedish Athletics Association and IAAF
New course through central Stockholm (including Sveavägen and Kungsgatan), passing through the city
World-class runner services along the entire course
additional: Start and finish area: Lidingövägen outside the clock tower at Stockholm Olympic Stadium. The race starts in two waves, at 12:00 and 12:10. The marathon time limit is 6.5 hours, and there are four checkpoints with cut-off times along the course. Seeding: the deadline for submitting a time for seeding is 3 May 2026; adidas Premiärmilen and adidas Premiärhalvan count towards seeding. adidas Premiärmilen (10 km) takes place in Norra Djurgården, has a total elevation gain of 117 m, mixed surfaces and a provisional start time of 11:00; the time limit is 2 hours and the contact for Premiärmilen is info@premiarmilen.se. The event is organised by Hässelby SK and Spårvägens FK, and the website is provided by Marathongruppen i Stockholm AB. The event is sold out for 30 May 2026. The course runs through central Stockholm and finishes at Stockholm Olympic Stadium; runners can also take part in related Adidas events such as Premiärmilen, Premiärhalvan and Shake Out Run.

name: Backyard Ultra Vänge
description: The loop is a real gem, if we may say so ourselves—a slice of Uppland at its best. The race hub is High Chaparral Park, with its large green spaces: a natural race base in the heart of the community of Vänge. Backyard Ultra Vänge will draw spectators along the course, which awaits you dressed in lovely spring attire. We have taken care to create a varied and somewhat challenging course. The result is an experience where something is always happening and the running never gets monotonous. Large parts of the race take place on the slightly bumpy trail on the outskirts of the community. You’ll feel as if you’re flying over soft ground beneath big trees and past colossal rocks. Several national-team runners began their running careers here, and many prominent floorball players have sweated through hard training sessions. An oasis in the forest—with a glimpse of Highway 72. A road tunnel takes you beneath the highway and into the unique Uppland rowing village of Vänge-Ekeby. The village, which has been a listed building since 1998, has medieval origins and a preserved village layout. Vänge Hembygdsförening has given the village an active cultural life and attracted many visitors. The course winds through this fantastic setting. Take the opportunity to enjoy the atmosphere and a glimpse of society as it once was. Then it’s back beneath the highway and into the forest on small trails. Before you know it, you’re back in the community and looping around High Chaparral. Take a short rest and perhaps enjoy some of the energizing snacks on offer. Then you’re off again. Wonderful!

name: Skatås ryggar
location: IFK Göteborg Orienterings klubb-anläggning, Skatås, Göteborg, Sweden
description: Skatås Ryggar is Gothenburg’s largest trail race, offering a fantastic trail-running experience on winding paths in the nature reserves around Skatås, the Delsjö area and Knipeflågsbergen. The race has several distances to suit everyone, from youth categories to a challenging half marathon over five ridges. The start and finish are at IFK Göteborg Orienteering’s clubhouse, and the courses are clearly marked to provide a safe and enjoyable running experience in a wilderness setting. All participants receive a wooden medal and have access to aid stations and good food after the race.
course_highlights: The course crosses five, four or two ridges in the Skatås and Delsjö area nature reserves
The longest course is 21.1 km and includes challenging terrain with rock slabs and winding paths
There are aid stations at four locations along the longest course, with sports drink and water
additional: Race bibs must be collected at the event venue before the start. The timing chip is attached to the bib and must be worn throughout the race. A bag-drop service is available for car keys and other belongings. After the race, hot soup and bread are served to all participants, while homemade baked goods and drinks are available for purchase. Medical staff will be on site. Parking is available near the event area, and the nearest public transport stop is Töpelsgatan. The courses are marked with fluorescent red tape and clear arrows at junctions. Runners are responsible for following the correct course at junctions. The event venue is IFK Göteborg Orienteering’s clubhouse in Skatås. There are youth categories and a kids’ trail race, aid stations and food after the finish; parking is free.

name: Seskarö Trailrun 2026
location: Seskarö Havsbad & Camping, Seskarö, Haparanda Municipality, Sweden
distance_verbose: 12 km, 7 km, 3000 meter, 2 km, 1 km, 0.5 km
description: Seskarö Trailrun 2026 is northern Sweden’s most fun race, offering courses for everyone, regardless of experience or age. It’s a competition and an experience for the whole family, with a focus on the joy of running. The courses wind through Seskarö’s fantastic trails and the beautiful natural surroundings of the Haparanda Archipelago, with varied terrain including forest, gravel, cobblestones and sand. Several distances are available, from 500 metres for the youngest participants to 12 km for those looking for a greater challenge on technical terrain.
course_highlights: The course follows existing trails and combinations of trails, with varied surfaces including forest, gravel, cobblestones and sand
Technically challenging sections with jumps over logs and rocks, as well as sandy and cobblestone sections
Detailed course maps for 12 km (clockwise), 7 km (clockwise) and 3 km (counterclockwise) are available on site
additional: Race bibs can be collected on Friday 29/5 from 17:00 to 20:00 and on Saturday 30/5 from 08:00 at Seskarö Havsbad & Camping. Race numbers must be collected at least 30 minutes before the start. All participants receive a Seskarö Trailrun participant medal. Showers and toilets are available. Proceeds from the entry fee go towards maintaining and developing the Seskarö Trails outdoor recreation area. The race is held at Seskarö Havsbad & Camping. Proceeds go towards maintaining and developing the Seskarö Trails outdoor recreation area.

name: Highland Charity Backyard Ultra
organizer: Highland Trail Club och Höglandskyrkan i Sävsjö
description: Highland Charity Backyard Ultra is a welcoming race in the deepest forests of Småland, featuring a scenic, hilly 6.7 km backyard loop and a 3.7 km loop suitable for children and recreational runners. The event is organized by Highland Trail Club and Höglandskyrkan in Sävsjö, with a focus on community and charity; all proceeds go to charitable causes. The number of laps is limited to 15, creating a challenging but fun experience for all participants.
course_highlights: Hilly 6.7 km backyard loop in the forests of Småland
3.7 km loop suitable for children and recreational runners
Nature-focused race with a charitable purpose
additional: The event runs from Saturday at 09:00 to Sunday at 00:00. The number of laps is limited to 15. All proceeds from the event go to charitable causes. Backyard laps start on the hour. Sources state that the 2026 edition started on Saturday at 09:00; information about the 2027 start time is unavailable.

name: Blue Mountain Trail Run
price_range: 150-450 kr beroende på distans och anmälningstid

price_tiers.distance: 15 km - Alvars stig by Nordväggen AB
6 km - Östra Ånnabodasjön by ICA Glansen

description:
Blue Mountain TrailRun is a trail race in Kilsbergen, 20 kilometres west of Örebro. There are four courses of 6, 10, 15 and 21 km, all starting and finishing at First Camp Ånnaboda.

The courses follow Bergslagsleden and the MTB trails around Ånnaboda: narrow trails, roots and rocks, boardwalks over streams, moss-covered spruce forest and views of forest lakes. The 21 km Blankhult course has 527 metres of elevation gain and is the race’s long loop for those looking for technical trails and hills. The 15 km Alvars stig is the middle-distance course, with trails all the way. The 10 km Trolldalsvägen is the classic 10-kilometre course. The 6 km Östra Ånnabodasjön course goes around the lake on mostly easy-running trails and is suitable as a first trail race.

Men’s and women’s categories on all courses, no time limit, electronic timing and a medal for everyone who finishes. The runner who breaks the course record on the 21 km course receives SEK 5,000. The fifth edition takes place in 2027. The race has been organised by Garphyttans IF Orientering since 2023.
course_highlights: Technical trails and hilly terrain along stage 9 of Bergslagsleden
Passes several forest lakes, including Norra Ånnabodasjön and Stora Dammsjön
Climb to Sånnabodahöjden, with sweeping views over Närkeslätten
additional: Race bibs can be collected at the race office from 09.00. Registration opens on 1 December 2026. The registration deadline is 22 May 2027. Late registration is available on race day from 09.00 to 09.15, subject to availability. Start times: 6 km at 09.43, 21 km at 10.00, 15 km at 10.35 and 10 km at 11.00. Aid stations with water, sports drink and snacks are located approximately every five kilometres. Trail shoes are recommended. Burgers, coffee and refreshments are available in the finish area. Swim in Södra Ånnabodasjön after the race. 21 km course records: 1:16:41 (men) and 1:29:16 (women).

name: Småland Adventure Race
description: A warm welcome to Småland Adventure Race 2027. After three fantastic years, we’re ready to take on a new challenge and aim for a race that’s at least as good as the last one. Småland Adventure Race is a multisport competition in which teams of 2–4 people use a map and compass to visit all checkpoints (CPs) as quickly as possible. CPs usually consist of a small physical orienteering marker and are marked with circles on the maps. The course will include a number of transition areas (TAs) where teams switch between disciplines. The race will mainly involve running, mountain biking and paddling, along with other adventures. In the three previous races, participants have paddled on air mattresses, climbed, tackled a high ropes course, gone SUPing and run a maze orienteering course. Some checkpoints have been at the top of climbing nets and others in the middle of a slackline, but most are in more accessible locations. We can promise many hours of wonderful adventure! We offer a long and a short class. Provisionally, teams in the long class will be out for 22–26 hours, and teams in the short class for 11–13 hours. In 2027, we’re also offering a Bike and Run class, a recreational class where you’ll be out for just 5–7 hours and take on a few fewer adventures—but still have a great time.
