name: Oslo Løpsfestival, Østmarka halvmaraton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Dagsbillett SOLO Deltakere kr 332,50 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3%) -30%

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Dagsbillett SOLO Deltakere kr 475,00 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3%)

description: Østmarka Half Marathon is part of the Oslo Running Festival and offers an exceptional nature experience through some of the most beautiful areas of Oslomarka. The race follows scenic forest roads through varied terrain and past idyllic lakes, and is suitable both for those looking to run a good time and for those who want to enjoy a fantastic day outdoors in the forest. This is the first-ever half marathon in the Oslo Running Festival, with a mass start on August 8 at 11:00 at Rustadsaga Sportsstue in Oslo.
course_highlights: Course through beautiful areas of Oslomarka
Scenic forest roads and varied terrain
Idyllic lakes and nature experiences all the way to the finish
additional: Race bibs can be collected from Löplabbet Oslo sentrum from April 7. The same race bib is used throughout the series. A new race bib can be purchased for 75 kr. Courses will only be marked for the mass start. GPX files and Strava links for the course are available to download. Registration is binding, with no refunds or transfer of race bibs. The race can be completed during the festival period from July 30 to August 8; the mass start is on August 8 at 11:00. Early-bird prices are listed and may increase on January 1.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a simple, fast race event at Ås School in Eidsvoll, featuring a flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop. The event offers seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon, and helps runners achieve fast times with a dedicated nutrition table along the course. Race bibs are collected using self-service at the venue, which has free parking, changing rooms and toilets. The race is known for its great atmosphere and the many runners who set personal records; it is a tradition to ring the bell at the finish to celebrate a new PB.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop
Dedicated nutrition table passed on every lap
Venue at Ås School with free parking, changing rooms and toilets
additional: Race bibs are collected using self-service approximately two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The race has a dedicated nutrition table where runners can leave their own bottles and gels. At selected races, ninth-graders from Feiring School staff an official drinks station, which also raises money for their school trip. It is a tradition to ring the bell at the finish area to celebrate a new personal record. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Registration is via RaceDays; half-marathon runners can arrange their own drinks and nutrition.

name: Perseløpet ¤6 - 2027
description: Perseløpet is a race in Eidsvoll, starting and finishing at Ås School in Hammerås. The event features a flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop and offers seven distances from 3 km to 100 km, designed for fast times. Participants can set up their own nutrition table, which they pass each lap, giving them easy access to their own supplies without the need for aid-station logistics. The event has a friendly atmosphere where personal bests are celebrated by ringing the bell near the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, officially measured 2,633-metre loop
Seven distances from 3 km to 100 km
Own nutrition table passed each lap
additional: Race bibs are self-service pickup at Ås School from around two hours before the start. Free parking, changing facilities and toilets are available at the venue. At selected races, ninth graders from Feiring School staff an official drinks station, which also raises money for their school trip. The weather forecast is updated four times daily using satellite data for the area around Ås School. Runners can have their own nutrition table.

name: VI Ilgų nuotolių bėgiko Piotro Silkino jubiliejinis 85-mečio bėgimas
location: Kretingos Vasaros estrada, Maironio g. 15, Kretinga, Lithuania
description: The 85th-birthday run of long-distance runner Piotr Silkin is a traditional race held at Kretinga Summer Amphitheatre. The competition follows a lap format, with marathon participants completing one 2.2 km lap and twelve 3.3 km laps. The event celebrates longtime runner Piotr Silkin and attracts running enthusiasts from various places. Participants can enjoy both athletic competition and a welcoming community atmosphere.
course_highlights: The marathon course consists of 1 lap of 2.2 km and 12 laps of 3.3 km each
The competition takes place at Kretinga Summer Amphitheatre
The lap format lets spectators follow the race and support the participants
additional: Various distances and age groups will be offered at the event; results will be published, and registration is online.

name: Brunnenlauf
location: Iburg-Stadion, Bad Driburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Bad Driburg Brunnenlauf is an annual running event organized by TV "Jahn" Bad Driburg e.V., welcoming runners of all ages. The challenging course runs along the Sachsenring, through the spa gardens and the town, and finishes at Iburg Stadium. The event emphasizes fairness and sportsmanship and uses timing with a reusable chip. Registration is online only; late entries are not possible.
course_highlights: Challenging out-and-back course with hills
The course runs along the Sachsenring, through the spa gardens and the town
Finish at Iburg Stadium, Bad Driburg
additional: Timing is provided exclusively with the reusable race result chip, worn on the foot using a chip strap. The chip deposit is 10€ and is refunded when the chip is returned. Late entries are not possible. Participants may be disqualified for violations of fairness and good conduct. Online registration only; no late entries. Participation from age 18; children and school students participate free of charge.

name: Diekseelauf
description: The Sparkassen Diekseelauf is a traditional fun run around Lake Dieksee in Bad Malente-Gremsmühlen. The event takes place on August 9, 2026, and offers runners an attractive course with modern transponder timing. Participants can conveniently view and download their results and certificates online. The race is organized by TSV Malente and is open to runners of all ability levels.

name: v-office-Europalauf
description: The 39th vOffice Europalauf on 9 August 2026 is an international race connecting the Baltic seaside resorts of Neustadt, Pelzerhaken and Rettin over the half-marathon distance. The course offers a wonderful view across Neustädter Bucht and returns to Neustadt along the beach promenade, parallel to the beach. In addition to the half-marathon, there are races over 10 km, 5 km and 2.5 km, as well as a Bambini run. The event is a popular sporting occasion in the region and is organised by TSV Neustadt.

name: Stomperudkarusellen- løp nr 3
location: Stomperud Stadion, Lørenvegen 2, Sørum, Lillestrøm, Norway
price_range: Enkeltløp: 220 kr for voksne og 110 kr for barn, med lisens i tillegg
description: Stomperudkarusellen is a long-established series of races organized by Sørum IL since 1981. The series consists of four races with varying distances from 800 meters to 9 kilometers, including shorter options for children and young people. The races take place in scenic surroundings, with the start and finish at Stomperud Stadion and nearby areas. Participants use the same race number throughout the series, and the event is open to both adults and children. Children who are members of Sørum IL can take part for free when they register.
course_highlights: Race 3: Lysløypa, 6 km with a shorter option
Start and finish at Stomperud Stadion, Lørenvegen 2, Sørum
Varied terrain with gravel roads, trails, and an athletics track for shorter distances
additional: Participants use the same race number in all races in the series. Children who are members of Sørum IL can take part for free if they register no later than one week before race day. The races have shorter options for the youngest participants. Start locations vary between Sørum Skole and Stomperud Stadion depending on the race. Race no. 3 meets at Stomperud Stadion, Lørenvegen 2, Sørum. The prices listed by the organizer apply to 2026.

name: Stomperudkarusellen 2027. Bare løp 3 (Lysløypa)
description: Stomperudkarusellen is a long-running race series organized by Sørum IL since 1981. The series consists of four races over varying distances, including Lysløypa, a 6 km race that is part of this year’s Race 3. The races are suitable for both adults and children, with shorter options for the youngest participants. Participants use the same bib number for all the races, which take place at Stomperud Stadion and in the surrounding areas of Sørum.
course_highlights: Race 3 Lysløypa: 6 km, with a shorter 500 m option
Traditional routes in the local area around Stomperud Stadion
Shorter distances for children and young people
additional: Participants use the same bib number for all races in the series. Children who are members of Sørum IL can participate for free if they register no later than one week before race day. The races offer shorter options for the youngest participants. The events take place at Stomperud Stadion and in the surrounding areas, which have a well-maintained network of walking trails and running routes. The prices and race dates listed on the organizer’s website apply to 2026 and do not confirm the 2027 edition. In 2026, the same bib number is used for all races in the series.

name: Sommerkarusell Ålesund - 3. løp
location: Vestenden av Lillevatnet, Spjelkavik, Ålesund, Norway
description: The Summer Series in Ålesund is a long-running race series organized by Ålesundløpene. The races take place in scenic surroundings by Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet in Vasstranda, on relatively flat, paved courses measured by Kondis. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km distances, starting from the western end of Lillevatnet in Spjelkavik. The series has its own prizes and awards a medal to those who take part in multiple races, attracting both recreational runners and competitive runners.
course_highlights: The courses run along Lillevatnet and Brusdalsvatnet in Vasstranda
Relatively flat paved courses with little traffic
Measured 5 km and 10 km distances
additional: The 10 km starts at 18:00 and the 5 km at 18:05. The races have their own prizes, with gift prizes awarded after each race. Participants who complete 2 or 3 races in the series receive a medal at the final race. Course records for both the 5 km and 10 km distances are documented. The participation record is 132 finishers. Distances: 5 km and 10 km. Registration is through EQ Timing. Participants who complete two or three races receive a medal at the final race.

name: Kohila pikamaajooksude sari 2026 VI etapp 1000m
description: The Kohila Long-Distance Running Series 2026, Stage VI (1000 m), takes place at the Kohila Sports Centre stadium and is open to everyone interested in running. The series includes different distances and age groups, with participants earning points and winners determined by age group. The entry fee is €8, or €5 for young people and pensioners. Registration is primarily available in advance, and on-site registration is possible until 18:30. The series winners will be awarded after the final race. To place among the prize winners, participants must take part in at least four stages.

name: Filter Temposari (5. etapp)
description: Filter Temposari is Estonia’s oldest and most prestigious time-trial series, offering the chance to test yourself in cycling, running or roller skating. The stages take place at various locations in Tallinn and the surrounding area, featuring individual-start speed races. The races are short and intense, suitable for both recreational and advanced participants. The series also includes the Kullapada prize programme, which rewards consistent participation in every stage over the same distance.

name: 14. ETAPP / Järve terviserada
description: 14th STAGE / The Järve health trail is a 10-stage relay race around Lake Viljandi, held on varied terrain and a health trail with different surface types. Teams consist of 10 members, with an equal number of women and men, who take turns running the different stages. The start and finish are at Viljandi City Stadium, and runners are taken to the stages on buses provided by the organizers. The race is part of the tradition of the Suurjooks ümber Viljandi järve and offers a sporting experience for schools, companies, and sports clubs.

name: Jonavos bėgimo taurė - 2026, 4 etapas
description: The Jonava Running Cup is a traditional running series held in Jonava District to promote sport and physical activity. The competition is open to all runners, who can compete in different stages and age groups. Participants earn points at each stage toward the overall standings, while the courses run through various locations in Jonava District, offering an interesting and varied running experience. Registration is online, and race numbers are collected at the start venue on race day.
course_highlights: Stages take place in various locations in Jonava District: Šilai–Jaugeliškiai, Ragožiai, Juškonys, Salupiai–Bartoniai, Jonava
The start time for each stage is 19:30
Race numbers can be collected at the start venue on race day from 18:30 to 19:20
additional: Participants register separately for each stage. Participation is free. The courses may cross roads open to traffic, so participants must follow traffic rules. Registration deadlines vary by stage; race numbers are collected at the start venue on race day. Registration is online, the races take place in various locations in Jonava District, and participants are divided into age groups.

name: 31. Joosu Järvejooksu sarja 5. etapp
location: Viljandi Lake Health and Ski Trail, Viljandi, Estonia
description: The 5th stage of the Joosu Lake Run series is a running race organized by the Joosu sports club. It takes place on the health and ski trail around Lake Viljandi. The race gives participants the opportunity to enjoy beautiful lake views and varied terrain. It is a great opportunity for both recreational and experienced runners to take part in a friendly and supportive environment.
course_highlights: Health and ski trail around Lake Viljandi
Beautiful lake views along the route
Varied terrain suitable for runners

name: Vetlanda Citylopp

price_tiers.distance: Dam, herr och motion (5 km och 10 km)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Dam-, herr- och motionsklassen (10 km och 5 km)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Kids F8/P8 - F12/P12 (1 km till 1,7 km) och Funkis (1 km)

tiers.label: tier_1

description: Vetlanda Citylopp is a welcoming urban race for all ages and ability levels. The start and finish are on Storgatan in the heart of Vetlanda, and participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km on a fast, spectator-friendly loop course. Younger participants can choose shorter distances from 400 metres up to 1.7 km. The event is a community celebration, with activities and food service in the square, where runners and spectators alike can enjoy a great day together.
course_highlights: Fast loop course in central Vetlanda
Start and finish on Storgatan in the heart of town
Spectator-friendly, with activities and food service in the square
additional: Race bib collection and on-the-day registration take place at Stortorget from 12:00 on race day. On-the-day registration is available until 30 minutes before the start of each class. Timing is provided by a chip in the race bib, and results are published live and on the OK Njudung website. Changing rooms and showers are available at Hövdingen sports hall near the start/finish. Previous editions have included children’s and youth classes as well as a Funkis class. Race-day bib collection, on-the-day registration and activities have previously been held at Stortorget.

name: BAMM
description: BAMM supported by OMM is a two-day ultramarathon in an Arctic mountain environment, where participants compete in pairs using mountain navigation across vast areas of unmarked terrain. The event offers several classes with different levels of difficulty and distances, making it accessible to both beginners and experienced adventurers. During the competition, participants experience spectacular mountain scenery and challenging navigation, with an overnight stay in the mountains. BAMM is a unique opportunity to combine physical challenge with a nature experience in one of Sweden’s most scenic environments.
course_highlights: Mountain navigation across unmarked terrain
Two-day competition with an overnight stay in the mountains
Arctic mountain environment with vast areas to navigate
additional: Participants compete in pairs (men’s, women’s or mixed teams). Transfers are available from Kiruna Airport to Hotell Riksgränsen and back, with times adapted to flight departures. Riksgränsen railway station is close to the hotel. Accommodation, equipment rental, food and practical information are available via the organiser’s website. The competition is held in teams of two. Mandatory equipment is part of the preparations; for BAMM 30, tents and sleeping bags are transported to the shared overnight camp. OMM is the main sponsor.

name: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt 7. løp
description: HTB Valestrandsmarka Rundt is an annual recreational race organised by Osterøy I.L. Friidrett. The race takes place in Valestrand and covers a distance of 4.4 km. It is a social and inclusive event, with evening start times for walkers and the main field. Traditionally, sveler, cordial and prizes are served, and course records are rewarded with cash prizes from HTB.
course_highlights: A 4.4 km course in Valestrand
Start times: 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field
Course records are rewarded with NOK 3,000
additional: Start times are 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field. Times in the walking field are recorded as 30 minutes or more. Traditionally, sveler from Toro, cordial from Saftsuse and prizes from Extra Valestrand are provided. The race is part of a series of races held throughout the year, including a Christmas race and a New Year’s race. Registration takes place at Furubakken sports ground, and payment can be made via Vipps 121337 or to account 3632.54.56676. In 2026, the start times were 18:45 and 19:00, with payment via Vipps. Participants received sveler, cordial and prizes.

name: 8. Wisent-RUN
location: Wisentgehege Springe, Springe, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Wisent-RUN is a popular race at Wisentgehege Springe, taking place for the eighth time on August 7, 2026. The event offers various race distances, including children’s races and timed competitions, set in a natural environment. With a family-friendly atmosphere and free admission to Wisentgehege from 15:00, the race is a sporting highlight for all ages. The event is organised by VfV Concordia Alvesrode e.V. and is known for its friendly atmosphere and dedicated volunteers.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Köhlerhütte in Wisentgehege Springe
Race routes through the natural surroundings of Wisentgehege
Children’s races with timing and an awards ceremony
additional: Free admission to Wisentgehege from 15:00. The 500 m children’s race “Frischlingsrennen” is untimed and open to children born in 2021 or later. The 1 km children’s race is timed and includes an awards ceremony for children born from 2016 to 2021. Ample parking is available. The event is open to everyone, with free admission for visitors. It offers an opportunity to explore the wildlife at Wisentgehege while getting active.

name: 24. Dammer Stadtlauf
description: The 24th Damme City Run is an evening road race through the center of Damme, organized by OSC Damme in cooperation with the City of Damme. The program includes three starts: a schoolchildren’s race, a general race for all participants, and the main evening race. After a two-year pandemic-related break, the race returns with an expected field of over 500 runners. The event is characterized by an open, local atmosphere, with on-site registration available, as runners fill the streets of the town center.
course_highlights: Evening road race through Damme city center
Three starts: schoolchildren’s race, general race, and main race
The course stays in the city center, with a lively atmosphere
additional: On-site registration is available, encouraging open, local participation. August weather is typically sunny, with temperatures between 14 and 25 °C. The event includes several categories, including children’s races and the main race, on a route through the city, with a relaxed, welcoming atmosphere.

name: 24. Knesebecker Einhornlauf
description: The Knesebecker Unicorn Run is a traditional running event in the Isenhagen region, held annually in August. The event gives runners of various ability levels the opportunity to test themselves on varied courses. Online registration is conveniently available via the RaceResult platform, where all results and certificates can also be accessed. The race takes place in the beautiful surroundings of Wittingen and attracts numerous running enthusiasts from the region.
course_highlights: 10 km course
Nordic walking option
Event held on the school grounds in Knesebeck
additional: Registration is online via RaceResult. Results and certificates are also available via RaceResult. The race takes place on Friday evening. Participant numbers are limited to 100; registration and results are available online; the event is held on the school grounds in Knesebeck.

name: 17. VSB Dresdner Nachtlauf
description: The VSB Dresden Night Run offers a beautifully illuminated route with views of the Dresden skyline. Torches and glow sticks create a special atmosphere. The 11.5 km route follows the Elbe to the Blue Wonder and returns along the Neustadt side of the river, while the 6.2 km route also runs along the Elbe and crosses the Albert Bridge to the finish. Alongside the sporting experience, there are children’s races and a special team competition for clubs and organizations. The event takes place at Heinz-Steyer-Stadion and is a highlight of the region’s running calendar.

name: 35. Speller Sparkassen-Sommernachtslauf
description: The 35th Speller Sparkassen Summer Night Run is a traditional race in Spelle, organized by SC Spelle-Venhaus. The event offers runners an attractive course in the beautiful surroundings of Wählehof. The race is suitable for all ages and ability levels and takes place in a relaxed atmosphere. Participants can look forward to a well-organized event with a friendly, family atmosphere.

name: Tavelsjö Halvmarathon
location: Tavelsjö Church, Tavelsjö, Umeå Municipality, Sweden
description: Tavelsjö Half Marathon is a family-friendly running event offering races for both adults and children. The half marathon starts and finishes at Tavelsjö Church and is a popular goal for summer training. Children can take part in a Mini race, and there is also a timed youth race, making the event a celebration for the whole family. All participants receive a medal and a treat after crossing the finish line, and there are also prize drawings.
course_highlights: Half marathon starting and finishing at Tavelsjö Church
Timed 2.2 km youth race
Mini race for children, popular with the whole family
additional: The youth race starts at 10:00 and is open to young people aged 8–17. Parents are welcome to help children who need support during the youth race. All participants receive a medal and a treat after crossing the finish line. Gift cards are available to purchase as gifts and are delivered within one week of ordering.

name: Midnattsloppet Stockholm
description: Midnattsloppet Stockholm is a classic night race held on 14 August 2027, with an evening start. The race offers 10 km and 5 km distances, taking participants through the lively streets of Södermalm in a festive atmosphere filled with music, cheers and camaraderie. In addition to the main races, there is also a costume category and children’s races, making the event a festival for all ages. Midnattsloppet is known for its uniquely late start time and the special atmosphere created among runners, spectators and race staff.
course_highlights: The original course around Södermalm in Stockholm
An evening start with a unique night-race atmosphere
A festive atmosphere with music and cheers from spectators along the course
additional: Start times vary by race: the Mini Race (300 m) starts between 11:45 and 15:30, the 2 km children’s races start at 18:30 and 18:50, the 10 km starts at 21:10, the 5 km starts at 21:40, and the costume category starts at 22:00. Corporate races and team competitions are offered to strengthen camaraderie and workplace health. Midnattsloppet is organised by Midnattsloppet Nordic AB, a wholly owned company of Hammarby IF Friidrott, and the surplus goes back to the sports clubs.

name: 6 sjöar
description: 6 Lakes is a race through the beautiful forests just outside Uppsala. You’ll run mainly on small forest roads, with shorter sections of trail. All distances loop around at least one lake, while the full marathon takes you around 6 lakes. With the environment in mind, we provide free bus transport for runners from Uppsala Central Station to the start in Fjällnora, and back after the race. The race is also free of disposable cups; instead, every runner receives a reusable cup.

name: ÅRC x Copperhill loop!
description:
Welcome to our exciting Åre Run Club x Copperhill loop!

On August 14, runners of all levels will gather to conquer the Copperhill hill. You can choose your own distance—5, 10, 15 or 20 km—and decide for yourself how many laps you want to do before crossing the finish line! We believe everyone should be able to take part and enjoy this amazing experience together. Join us for an unforgettable running celebration, whether you’re a beginner or an experienced runner. Let’s create magical running memories together!

name: Bringebærløpet 2027
description: The Raspberry Run in Vollen is a family-friendly race offering distances for all ages and ability levels. The start and finish are at Vollenhallen, and the course runs through a scenic area, with only minor changes from previous years. The youngest runners complete a lap of approximately 1 km on the roller-ski track, while older participants run 2.5 km or 5 km. The event focuses on participation and enjoyable sporting experiences, and participants can also attend the Raspberry Festival held in conjunction with the race.
course_highlights: The course follows the roller-ski track at Arnestad through scenic surroundings
A race of approximately 1 km for the youngest participants
A 2.5 km and 5 km race course with a mass start
additional: Schedule: 11:00 bib number collection opens; 13:00 mass start for 5 km; 13:30 mass start for 2.5 km; 14:00 start of the 1 km children’s race, with multiple starts; 15:00 awards ceremony for competition classes aged 11 and up. The listed distances and start/finish area apply to the 2026 edition; details for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Grue Backyard 2027
description: Grue Backyard is a unique endurance race featuring 6.7 km loops through technical forest terrain. The race starts a new wave every hour, continuing until only one runner remains standing. Participants can complete one loop to earn a medal or push further for the finisher cap and the win. The event also includes the Grue Half Marathon, known as one of Norway's fastest half marathon courses, and the Gruemila 10 km race.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loops through technical forest terrain
New start every hour until one runner remains
Flat and fast 21.1 km half marathon course
additional: The race features hourly starts for the backyard loops, with medals awarded for completing one loop and a finisher cap for those who continue until the end. Previous editions have had up to 12 rounds, and participants who completed at least seven rounds have been able to receive a Grue Backyard Ultra Finisher T-shirt. This information is from previous editions and does not confirm details for 2027.

name: Ringeriksmaraton
description: Ringeriksmaraton is an annual running festival that began in 1995 and has grown to become Norway’s largest marathon relay. The race runs through the beautiful municipalities of Hole, Ringerike and Jevnaker, and offers distances and categories for everyone, including 8-person and 4-person relays, a pair marathon, half marathon and marathon. The event attracts recreational runners from all over the country and offers a sociable, active experience in beautiful surroundings. Children’s Ringeriksmaraton is also a popular part of the event, making it a family-friendly occasion.
course_highlights: The course runs through the municipalities of Hole, Ringerike and Jevnaker
Beautiful natural scenery, including Norway’s largest apple orchard
Varied terrain with asphalt, footpaths, forest roads and residential areas
additional: A mass start for all categories at Vik at 11:00, with an early start at 10:00 for runners using technical aids or with a finish time over 5 hours. Drink stations with squash and water at each relay exchange, as well as a muesli bar with salt at exchanges 3 and 6 for the half marathon and marathon. Toilets are available at several locations, but there are no shower facilities at Jevnakerhallen due to renovation. Løperbanken makes it possible to find a team if you are missing teammates. Race numbers and relay batons are handed out together. Registration is final, with no refund if you withdraw. Course maps, GPX files and practical information are available on the organizer’s website.

name: Bergen Skogsmaraton - Maratonkarusellen
description: Bergen Forest Marathon is an annual forest race held in Hordnesskogen, with the start and finish at the parking lot. The race features a loop of approximately 5.3 km, run multiple times depending on the distance: 8 laps for the marathon, 4 for the half marathon, and 2 for the 10 km. The event is suitable for both experienced runners and recreational runners, offering a wonderful nature experience in the forest and good facilities, including changing rooms, water stations, and food in the finish area. The focus is on enjoyment and quality for all participants.
course_highlights: Loop course in Hordnesskogen, starting and finishing at the parking lot
Each lap is approximately 5.3 km long
Two water stations, passed three times per lap
additional: Race headquarters opens at 08:00 for race-number collection and bag drop. Start times: 10 km at 09:00, marathon at 10:00, half marathon at 11:00. Food and drink for everyone who finishes. Changing rooms and toilets are at Bjarghallen, approximately 250 metres from the start. Parking is available at Bjarghallen, but capacity is limited; public transport or carpooling is recommended. Clothing can be stored in a tent in the start area at your own risk. Late registration is possible up to the start, subject to availability. The start and finish are at the parking lot in Hordnesskogen. Bjarghallen is approximately 250 metres from the start. Registration is through EQ Timing, and late registration is possible up to the start if places are available.

name: Level-løp
description: Level Løp is a trail race for everyone, held in beautiful surroundings in Hommersåk. The race offers distances of 5 km, 10 km and 23 km, as well as a 1000-metre children's race, with varied terrain and elevation changes suited to both recreational and experienced runners. The race starts at Riska Church and features scenic trails, forest and challenging climbs. After finishing, participants can enjoy hot food and drinks, and prizes are awarded to the top men and women in all main distances.
course_highlights: Trail race through the varied and beautiful terrain of Hommersåk
23 km with 1100 metres of elevation gain, 10 km with 246 metres, and 5 km with 87 metres
Aid stations on the 10 km and 23 km distances
additional: Bib collection is on Friday, 14 August, from 15:00 to 19:00 at Amboltveien 9, and on race day from 08:00 at the start area. Registration at the start area is open from 08:00 to 12:45 on race day. The children's race is divided into age-based waves. Hot food and drinks are provided for all participants in the 23 km race. A kiosk offers hot food, snacks and drinks. Parking is at Riska Church, not at the start area. Toilets and changing rooms are available at the start/finish. Live results with finish times are available. Prizes are awarded on an ongoing basis after runners finish. One prize is drawn at random from the bib numbers. Parking is at Riska Church. The stated start times are 09:00 for 23 km, 10:00 for 10 km, 10:20 for 5 km and 13:30 for the children's race. The 10 km and 23 km races are for participants born in 2012 or earlier.

name: Skånevik Skyrace
description: Skånevik Skyrace is a spectacular mountain race on a challenging 24-kilometre circular course with 1,600 metres of elevation gain across varied and technical terrain. The race offers fantastic views of fjords and mountains, combining raw nature with the joy of running for both recreational runners and elite athletes. The start and finish are in Skånevik town centre, where activities create a lively atmosphere both on the course and in town. The event features official timing, several drink stations, and a wide range of participant amenities, including access to a pool, sauna and massage after the race.
course_highlights: 24 km circular course with 1,600 metres of elevation gain
Steep climbs and technical terrain with flowing trail sections
Fantastic panoramic views from Håfjellet (932 m above sea level) and Nepo (610 m above sea level)
additional: Start and finish at Skånevik Fjordhotell, with a Base Camp for race-number collection, information, music, food and a great atmosphere. Three drink stations along the course and several timing checkpoints. Free access to Sjøkanten Trivsel, including a pool, sauna and massage after the race. Minimum age: 16; runners must pass Juraskar by 3:00 p.m. Accommodation is available at Skånevik Fjordhotell and nearby Airbnb properties, camping and boat moorings. Registration for 2027 is sold out, but places may become available in May 2027. The 2027 edition is sold out; any available places may be released in May 2027. Minimum age: 16, and runners must pass Juraskar by 3:00 p.m. Participants receive food and drinks at 3–4 drink stations, a medal and a buff.

name: Kniveåsen Rundt
location: Pumpehuset ved Solumstrand renseanlegg, Drammen, Norway
description: Kniveåsen Rundt is a forest race around Kniveåsen in Drammen that welcomes everyone to participate. The race is free and suitable for both recreational and experienced runners looking for an outdoor experience in forest terrain. The event has an inclusive atmosphere and is held annually, offering great opportunities to enjoy running in beautiful surroundings.
course_highlights: Forest race around Kniveåsen in Drammen
Natural terrain with varied surfaces
Suitable for all levels
additional: The race is free to enter. Results from previous years and event videos are available on the website. The race is open to everyone. Registration is linked from the official website.

name: Budor løpefest 2027
description: Budor Running Festival 2027 takes place on Saturday, August 14, at Budor Gjestegård and offers 5 km, 10 km, and half-marathon distances. The race offers an inclusive atmosphere for both experienced runners and beginners, with the start and finish at Gjestegården. The courses pass through scenic surroundings on trails and gravel roads, offering a spectacular running experience with beautiful panoramic views. The event also includes a free children’s race, Koiedalen Rundt, with a medal for participants. Prizes are awarded to the three fastest runners in each category in the 5 km, 10 km, and 21 km races.
course_highlights: The courses run mainly on trails and gravel roads through scenic surroundings
Start and finish at Budor Gjestegård, with panoramic views
The half marathon has only 250 places and offers a memorable running experience
additional: Race numbers can be collected between 09:00 and 10:30 at Gjestegården. The half marathon starts at 10:00, the 10 km at 10:30, and the 5 km at 10:40. Toilets and a few showers are available in the basement of Gjestegården, and swimming is possible in Koiedalsvannet near the finish area. The children’s race, Koiedalen Rundt, starts at 13:00 and is free. You can sell your place by contacting the organizer by email. All distances start and finish at Budor Gjestegård. Published schedule: half marathon at 10:00, 10 km at 10:30, and 5 km at 10:40. Race numbers can be collected at Gjestegården. The half marathon has 250 places, and the children’s race, Koiedalen Rundt, is free.

name: Backyard ultra Golsfjellet

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Backyard Deltakere kr 750,00 + Adm. gebyr (25 NOK + 3% transaksjonsgebyr)

description: Backyard Ultra Golsfjellet is a unique trail race with no asphalt, offering participants a full experience of fresh mountain air and scenic surroundings. The race is based at Oset Fjellhotell, which is exclusively booked for the event and filled with runners, supporters, and a great backyard atmosphere throughout the weekend. This is more than just a race; it is also a social weekend experience focused on food and spending time together, with all meals for runners prepared by the hotel’s renowned kitchen. The race is suitable for anyone looking for a challenging and social experience in the mountains.
course_highlights: The race takes place entirely on mountain terrain with no asphalt
Start and finish at Oset Fjellhotell, exclusively booked for the event
Delicious refreshments and food prepared by Oset Fjellhotell’s kitchen during breaks
additional: Race bibs and ankle chips can be collected at Oset Fjellhotell on Friday, August 14, from 19:00 to 21:00 and Saturday, August 15, from 07:30 to 08:30. The entire hotel is booked for the event, and a 20% discount is available for a two-night stay with discount code BYOSET. A pasta party is held on Friday evening and a gala dinner on Saturday evening, but neither is included in registration. A hotel buffet on Saturday evening is available to participants for 495 kr when reserved. Food and drink are central to the race, with easy access to refreshments during breaks. Accommodation and some meals are not included in the entry fee. The 2027 registration is listed with an Early Bird price.

name: Saudehornet Rett Opp 2027
location: Havna i Ørsta sentrum, Ørsta, Norway
description: Saudehornet Rett Opp is an annual uphill race in Ørsta that starts at the harbour in the town centre and climbs to the summit of Saudehornet, 1,303 metres above sea level. The course is 5.7 km long with a challenging climb, attracting amateurs, recreational runners and some professional athletes. The race has a rich history, including John Tvedt’s record run in 2007. It is a challenging and spectacular summit route that can also be hiked when there is no snow on the mountain.
course_highlights: 5.7 km course with 1,303 metres of elevation gain
Starts at the harbour in central Ørsta and finishes at the summit of Saudehornet
Challenging uphill race suitable for recreational and professional runners
additional: The route can be tried as a moderately challenging summit hike when there is no snow. Participants are mainly amateurs and recreational runners, but some professional athletes also take part. The event includes a recreational class and a separate children’s race to Skåla.

name: Lääne-Virumaa jooksusari 2026 - 27. Viru-Nigula Rahvajooks
description: The Lääne-Virumaa Running Series 2026 offers a varied series of running and walking events, bringing together fitness enthusiasts and recreational athletes from spring to autumn. The 27th Viru-Nigula People’s Run takes place on the Viru-Nigula running track and in the long-jump pit. It is part of a long-running series that encourages participation across different age groups and distances. The series aims to promote healthy lifestyles and offer participants the chance to test their abilities. The events are well organized, with chip timing, ensuring participants an enjoyable and motivating running experience.

name: Schierker Sommerlauf
description: The Schierker Sommerlauf is a traditional race in the Harz Mountains, taking place for the 24th time on 8 August 2026. The event offers varied distances from 1 km to 16 km, running through the impressive landscape around Schierke. Runners can enjoy breathtaking views, a unique atmosphere and great support in the finish area at the Schierker Feuersteinarena. The race is part of the new Harzer Laufcup 2026 and is open to runners of all abilities.
course_highlights: Run on paved forest roads, with two laps for the 8 km main race
Breathtaking views of the Brocken and the Harz landscape
Start and finish at the Schierker Feuersteinarena, with a great atmosphere
additional: The start and finish are at the Schierker Feuersteinarena, which has changing rooms and showers. The course runs along paved forest roads. There is a refreshment point at the newly built toboggan run. Registration is online, with personalised race numbers for those who register in advance. Use of the showers is included in the entry fee. The event is part of the Harzer Laufcup 2026. Courses on paved forest roads, online registration, personalised race numbers, refreshments included, electronic timing, certificates and trophies for the winners.

name: 100MeilenBerlin - Der Mauerweglauf
description: The 100MeilenBerlin – The Wall Trail Run is a historically significant ultramarathon that follows the route of the former Berlin Wall around western Berlin. The course of approximately 161 kilometers runs mostly on paved paths, but also includes trail-like and sometimes uneven sections. The start and finish are at Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn-Sportpark in Berlin-Prenzlauer Berg. The race commemorates the victims of the division of Germany and is held annually, with the running direction alternating.

name: 2. Backyard Ultra-Marathon Tharandter Wald
description: The 2nd Backyard Ultra Marathon in the Tharandt Forest is organized by SC Freital e.V. and takes place in one of Saxony’s most beautiful forest regions. The course is a 6.7 km loop, mostly on forest trails, run alternately clockwise and counterclockwise. The start and finish area is at the Jugendfreizeithof Grillenburg. A total of 100 starting places are available, and registration is via RaceResult.

name: Botaniczna Piątka edycja letnia
description: Botaniczna Piątka Bydgoszcz – Summer Edition is a cross-country race organized by running enthusiasts since 2014. The event takes place on scenic routes that showcase the beauty of the locations. The organizers’ goal is to popularize running and provide participants with a unique sporting and scenic experience. Join this friendly and dynamic running event.

name: XII Rozłaziński Bieg po radość z życia
XXXIII Bieg im. Marszałka Józefa Piłsudskiego
Olsokløpet 2027
location: Ålvundeid, Sunndal, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
description: Olsokløpet is an annual race held in Ålvundeid, Møre og Romsdal. The race covers a distance of 9.7 km and starts at 13:00. Prizes are awarded to the top three women and men, as well as to category winners, who receive a modest prize. The event also includes activities for children in the form of a track and field fun run, and food sales with grilling organized by Ålvundeid Bygdekvinnelag.
course_highlights: The race takes place in Ålvundeid, Møre og Romsdal
Distance of 9.7 km
Activities for children and a track and field fun run
additional: Prizes are awarded for 1st, 2nd and 3rd place, as well as to category winners. The top three women and men receive 1,000, 500 and 300 kroner, respectively. Food sales and grilling from 11:00 to 15:00. Previous editions have included prizes for the top three and category winners, as well as activities for children and food sales/grilling. This information applies to previous editions and may differ in 2027.

name: Rubjerg Knude løbet 2027
distance_verbose: Halvmarathon, Halvmarathon, 15 km, 10 km, 5 km, 2.5 km

name: Volkslauf Rund um den Beerster See
location: Kurpark am Kanal, Bad Bederkesa, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Volkslauf Rund um den Beerster See is a running event for participants of all ages and abilities, held on the third Sunday in August in Bad Bederkesa. The course passes through a natural setting and offers a motivating challenge for both competitive runners and recreational athletes. The event promotes community and the joy of being active, making it a special experience for both race participants and recreational runners. The start and finish are in Kurpark am Kanal, and timing is by transponder.
course_highlights: Scenic course around Beerster See
Start and finish in Kurpark am Kanal
Free drinks on the opposite side of the lake and at the finish
additional: Race packs are distributed in the Amtsscheune opposite the castle. Showers are available at the Moortherme upon presentation of your race number. Timing is by transponder, which must be returned after the race. The cut-off time for the main races is 1 hour 45 minutes. The event takes place in all weather conditions. Course distances: 7.6 km; hiking, walking and Nordic walking: 1.1 km, 0.5 km and 14.6 km. Race packs are distributed in the Amtsscheune. The event takes place in all weather conditions. Timing is by transponder.

name: Wohldenberger Waldlauf
description: The 21st Wohldenberger Forest Run on August 16, 2026, offers runners of all ability levels varied courses through the Wohldenberg Forest. For more than two decades, this event has been one of the most popular in the Hildesheim region, attracting 200 to 300 participants each year. The route follows natural forest trails with changing surfaces and hilly sections, making it a true trail-running experience. There are suitable distances for beginners, families, walkers, and ambitious runners, from short children’s races to the challenging half marathon.

name: Wolfsburg Staffellauf powered by VfL Wob e.V.
description: The Wolfsburg Relay Race, organized by VfL Wolfsburg e.V., is a special team experience that brings together runners of all ages and backgrounds. On August 16, 2026, the second edition of this relay marathon will take place, giving teams from schools, clubs, and companies the chance to experience team spirit through sport. The course runs through the green city forest, with the start and finish at VW-Bad, where music will also create a lively atmosphere. Children’s relay teams are supported by Förderkreis Leichtathletik VfL Wolfsburg e.V., making participation especially appealing.

name: Marceliński Bieg Letni 2026
description: Marceliński Summer Run 2026 is a cross-country race organized in Poznań by running enthusiasts from the Biegi.Wlkp. group. The event takes place on scenic routes that highlight the location’s aesthetic appeal. Since 2014, the organizers have focused on promoting cross-country running in Greater Poland, offering participants a unique running experience amid beautiful natural surroundings.

name: XXI Bieg Lesoków
description: The 21st Lesoków Run is an annual race held in Szemud as part of the Kaszuby Biegają series. The event offers two routes, 5 and 10 km long, through the picturesque Kashubian countryside, encouraging participants to enjoy the outdoors. It attracts runners of different ages and experience levels, promoting a healthy lifestyle and local running culture.

name: Blodomloppet (Jönköping)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Lilla Blodomloppet för barn upp till 12 år kostar 100 kr och kan anmälas till denna avgift ända fram tills dagen loppet går.

description: Blodomloppet in Jönköping is a recreational event that raises awareness of the vital importance of blood donation and welcomes participants to walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km. There is also a children’s race, Lilla Blodomloppet, for children up to 12 years old, with shorter courses. The event is a social and health-promoting activity where teams and individual participants can take part, and each team receives a picnic bag as part of the entry fee. Blodomloppet is part of Sweden’s largest recreational race series, with a strong focus on health and the importance of blood donation.
course_highlights: Timed 5 km and 10 km runs
Untimed 5 km walk
Lilla Blodomloppet for children up to 12 years old, with 400/800 m courses
additional: Teams can consist of 3–5 participants, and vacant places can be filled at no extra cost until 5 August by email. Registered blood donors receive a 40 kr discount when registering. A picnic bag from ICA is included with team registration and can be ordered separately for 250 kr each. Wellness allowances can be used via Wellnet, Epassi or Benify. Lilla Blodomloppet is for children up to 12 years old, with shorter 400/800-metre courses. The event raises awareness of the need for blood donation. Participants can form teams, and the event usually ends with a picnic.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://blodomloppet.se/vara-lopp/jonkoping/): 2027-08-17 — "Välkommen till Blodomloppet 2027! ... 17 augusti 2027" (was estimated 2027-08-10)

name: Convinistafetten
location: Stora Skuggan, Norra Djurgården, Stockholm, Sweden
description: Convinistafetten is Sweden’s largest relay race, held annually in Stora Skuggan, Norra Djurgården, Stockholm. Each team consists of five participants, each running 5 kilometres, and there is also a walking category where the team walks together. The event is a fun, energetic evening that promotes team building and company camaraderie. After the race, all teams are treated to a picnic with food, drinks, fruit and coffee on the grass. Convinistafetten has a long tradition dating back to 1986 and attracts over 3,000 teams every year.
course_highlights: Each team runs five legs of 5 km each
Start and finish by the transition zone in Stora Skuggan
A picnic with food and drinks is included after the race
additional: Relay teams start in three different waves, with the first start at approximately 17:30. The walking category starts at approximately 17:40. The team captain receives all the race bibs by mail. The final runner collects the picnic box from the picnic tent. It is possible to book extra picnic boxes and private tent packages to enhance the experience. Title sponsor Convini treats teams to a picnic after they finish.

name: Vestfold løpskarusell - 6. løp - Revetal

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 1200 kr. for ikke medlemmer frem til 31.12.26.

description: Vestfold Running Series 2027 is a series of 8 great races in the Tønsberg region, offering the joy of running, community and a great atmosphere for all levels. Each race has two distances and starts at 18:00, with electronic timing via EQ Timing. Participants can choose to run individual races or buy a season pass for all the races at a discounted price. The courses take runners through varied and beautiful surroundings in Vestfold. Course descriptions are shared in a Facebook group and when registering for the season.
course_highlights: Two distances at each race, typically around 3 km and a double lap
Courses cover varied terrain, including residential areas, lit trails and gravel roads
Start and finish at central locations such as the Sport1 store in Revetal
additional: Season-pass participants collect their race number at the first race. Participants running an individual race collect theirs from the race office 10 minutes before the start. Race numbers must be kept for the entire series. Electronic timing via EQ Timing. Course descriptions and profiles are shared in the Facebook group and when registering for the season. Start at 18:00. Season passes and registration for individual races are available.

name: Sørdalskarusellen - Fløymyrløpet
description: Flømyrløpet is the seventh race in Sørdalskarusellen and has been held since 2001. The start and finish are at Skurvbrua on Nordseterveien, 6 km above Lillehammer. The race offers a tough, wet trail run over challenging terrain, including marshy sections and trails. There are two distances: a long course of 5.4 km and a short course of 2.81 km. The short course follows the long course up to Flømyra and then descends to the finish. The race offers a mass start and a virtual option, and is a traditional part of Sørdalskarusellen, with an awards ceremony after the race.
course_highlights: A challenging 5.4 km trail run with wet and marshy sections
Start and finish at Skurvbrua, 6 km from Lillehammer city centre
The course follows a ski-trail route up to Flømyra shooting range, then returns via trails and roads
additional: All mass starts are at 18:30. The virtual race takes place August 15–18. The low-price registration deadline is 13:00 on race day, and the final registration deadline is 18:00 the same day. The awards ceremony is at approximately 19:15. The under-12 class uses the short course. It is possible to run the short course without timing. The course was adjusted in 2023 to avoid the worst of the marsh. Participants must enter their time on My Page under the Self Timing tab. Flømyrløpet is part of Sørdalskarusellen, a series of ten recreational races in the Lillehammer area. There is a long course of approximately 5.4 km and a short course of approximately 2.8 km. The information from the organisers applies to previous editions, so details for 2027 may differ.

name: 15. ETAPP / Vabaõhumuuseum
description: The Health Run and Walk is a multi-stage running and walking event held in various parts of Tallinn, including the Estonian Open Air Museum. Each stage offers a chance to enjoy beautiful nature trails and the benefits of recreational sport. The Estonian Open Air Museum stage is 4.2 km long and is well suited to both runners and walkers who want to spend active time outdoors. The event is a tradition and is open to everyone interested in recreational sport.

name: Blodomløpet 2027
organizer: Røde Kors Blodprogram, i samarbeid med Blodbanken Ahus og lokale friidrettslag
description: Blodomløpet is a fun run organized by the Norwegian Red Cross Blood Programme in cooperation with local blood banks and athletics clubs. The event focuses on raising awareness of blood donation and promoting a healthy lifestyle. Participants can walk, jog or run 500 metres, 5 km or 10 km, and proceeds from registration go to local athletics clubs that support children and young people. Inspired by Sweden’s largest fun run, the event aims to help create a healthier Norway without blood shortages.
course_highlights: Choice of 500-metre, 5 km and 10 km distances
The courses are clearly marked and include both paved and gravel surfaces
Proceeds go to local athletics clubs that support children and young people
additional: Registration is binding and entitles participants to a place in the event and a one-time licence where required. Participants may enter individually or as part of a team (maximum 5 participants). Photos and videos will be taken during the event and may be used for documentation and marketing. By registering, participants enter into an agreement with the organizing clubs and partners.

name: Liikumissari 8.Järvamaa Järvede jooksud VII etapp /Käru järve jooks
location: Käru, Türi Parish, Järva County, Estonia

name: Hagbloms Nattloppet
description: Hagbloms Nattloppet in Kalmar is a unique running experience that invites you to walk, jog or run 5 km in a wonderful atmosphere, with music, lighting and surprises along the course. The start and finish are at Stortorget, where runners also pass through on each lap. All participants receive a special medal and, if they register in advance, a unique T-shirt, as well as a drink, fruit and a piece of chocolate. The race is open to both men and women, and there is also a walking class without timing. The event is organised by Högby IF with support from Hagbloms and other sponsors.
course_highlights: 5 km course with the start, lap point and finish at Stortorget in Kalmar
Run at your own pace with music and lighting along the way
A special medal for everyone who finishes
additional: Race number pickup and late registration take place at the Högby tent at Stortorget on Thursday 20 August from 15:00 to 17:00 and Friday 21 August from 18:00. Payment can be made by card, cash or Swish. Everyone registered by 16 August receives the Nattloppet’s unique T-shirt. Prizes are drawn, including gift cards from Kallskänken. A walking class without timing is available. Open to walkers, joggers and competitive runners. Everyone who finishes receives a medal; participants who register in advance also receive the race’s unique T-shirt.

name: Askes Fjällmaraton
location: Torget, Idre Fjäll, Idre, Älvdalen Municipality, Dalarna County, Sweden

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 50 kr som oavkortat går till Viggo Foundation

description: Askes Fjällmaraton is a child-friendly 1 km mountain race held on Friday evening at Idre Fjäll. The course is well marked and suitable for all children born in 2015 or later. There is no timekeeping, but all participants receive a medal and a treat at the finish. Registration is easy online or on site using Swish, and the entire entry fee goes directly to the Viggo Foundation, which supports neuro-adaptive sports for children and young people.
course_highlights: 1 km course with clear markings
Start and finish at Torget, Idre Fjäll
Child-friendly race with no timekeeping
additional: Registration is available online until 15 minutes before the start or on site at bib collection using Swish. All proceeds go to the Viggo Foundation. After the race, every child receives a medal and a treat. The Fjällmaratonklubben for children aged 4–12 also offers fun activities on Saturday. Intended for children; sources give different age limits. Registration is available online until 15 minutes before the start or on site at bib collection. Proceeds go directly to the Viggo Foundation.

name: Schleswiger Treppenlauf
description: The Schleswig Stair Run takes place for the 13th time in 2026 and features a new, attractive course starting and finishing at the Polierteich. Participants complete 10 laps with a total of approximately 940 steps, mostly on firm sand. The event offers both individual and duo competitions, with ample parking available at Stadtfeld. It is a sporting challenge in Schleswig, organised by the Spiridon Schleswig running club.
course_highlights: 10 laps with approximately 940 steps
Mostly firm sand underfoot
Start and finish at the Polierteich
additional: Start and finish at the Polierteich; ample parking at Stadtfeld; event runs from 18:30 to 21:00; individual and duo competitions available; mostly firm sand underfoot. Registration is open; parking at Stadtfeld; running time from 18:30 to 21:00.

name: 11. Lichterlauf Tangermünde
description: The Tangermünde Lights Run is an atmospheric race right by the Elbe in the historic imperial town of Tangermünde. On August 21, 2026, runners of all ages and ability levels can take part in races of various distances, including a children’s race, a 5 km fun run, a 10 km main race, and a team relay. The course runs along the picturesque Elbe promenade and offers a special atmosphere, followed by an after-run party in Tangermünde. The race is a community sporting event that puts fun, exercise, and team spirit first.

name: 19. Barßeler Hafenfestlauf
description: The 19th Barßeler Hafenfestlauf takes place on August 21, 2026, near Barßel Harbor. The event offers races for various age groups, including Bambini races, student races, a 5-kilometer race, Nordic walking, and a 10-kilometer main race. The course follows paved roads and is suitable for all age groups. The event is organized by Sport- und Turnverein Barßel and offers a family-friendly atmosphere with an accompanying program and refreshments.

name: Buntekuhlauf
description: The Buntekuhlauf in Lübeck-Buntekuh is a long-standing running event taking place for the 18th time on 21 August 2026. It offers various races for all ages and ability levels, from short runs on the sports field to longer routes on sidewalks. The races take place on traffic-free sidewalks and sports-field grounds, creating a safe and pleasant atmosphere for all participants. SC Buntekuh e.V. organizes the event with the aim of making exercise fun for everyone.

name: Volkslauf Um die Taakener Ähren
description: The “Um die Taakener Ähren” fun run is a popular, family-friendly running event in Taaken, taking place on August 21, 2026. The event offers various races for all age groups, from a toddlers’ run and races for schoolchildren and joggers to the competitive 10 km main race and a relay race. The course runs through Taaken and its idyllic fields of grain, with fun and community at its heart. All participants receive pastries at the finish, and the winners are awarded traditional winner’s loaves. The village provides food and drink stalls to create a welcoming atmosphere.

name: Mottenburger Meile
description: The Mottenburger Meile is a traditional cult race on the Elbe in Hamburg, held annually on the Friday after the Hamburg school holidays. The precisely measured out-and-back course is 7.5 km, equivalent to a Prussian land mile. The race starts and finishes on the banks of the Elbe below Halbmondweg/Elbchaussee and offers a romantic atmosphere with evening lighting. In addition to the sporting competition, the race supports the Hamburger Spendenparlament and remembers the Jewish victims of the Holocaust with a Stolperstein.

name: Ultravasan
description: Ultravasan 90 is a trail race starting in Berga by, Sälen, offering runners the classic Vasaloppet route through scenic summer landscapes. The race starts at dawn at 05:00 and follows the historic checkpoints to the finish in Mora, with views of pine forests, waterways, trails and traditional mountain farm settings. The race is 92 km long, has Swedish Championship status in 2026 and is part of Vasaloppstrippeln; the maximum number of participants is 2,500, and the minimum age is 17.
course_highlights: Dawn start at 05:00 in Berga by—watch the sun rise over the marshes around Smågan
Seven Vasaloppet checkpoints along the course, with drinks, energy, toilets and medical care
Scenic stretches through open pine forests, winding waterways, well-trodden trails and picturesque traditional mountain farm settings
additional: Race bibs and chips can be collected in Mora or Sälen in the days before the race, or at the start venue. Start pens open at 04:30, and your time starts when you cross the start line. Baggage transport to Mora is available, and you can send a change-of-clothes bag to Evertsberg. There are refreshment stations approximately every five kilometres, as well as toilets and medical care at all checkpoints. Maximum 2,500 participants; training grants of SEK 60,000 are awarded to the winner in each of the women’s and men’s categories. Ultravasan consists of two longer ultramarathon distances: Ultravasan 90 (Sälen–Mora, approximately 92 km) and Ultravasan 45 (Oxberg–Mora, approximately 45 km). Both finish in Mora and are part of Vasaloppet’s Summer Week.

name: Vasastafetten
description: Vasastafetten is a cross-country relay race held as a festival, where hundreds of teams made up of clubs, companies, families and groups of friends share the classic route from Sälen to Mora. It is the oldest event of the summer and offers a challenging course covering a total of 92 kilometres, divided into ten legs ranging from 4.5 to 15 kilometres. The race starts in Berga by in Sälen and welcomes both elite runners and recreational runners aged 8 and over. The entry fee includes bus transport for participants on the first two legs, and the organiser sends the team captain the race pack with bib numbers and information well in advance of the race.
course_highlights: Cross-country race between Sälen and Mora
Ten legs ranging from 4.5 to 15 km
Start in Berga by, Sälen, and finish in Mora
additional: The race pack with bib numbers and an information letter is sent to the team captain approximately two weeks before the race. The timing chip must be collected on race day at the Vasaloppet start in Sälen between 06:30 and 08:00. A bus ticket to the start for leg 1 must be booked, and runners on leg 2 must take the organiser's bus to Smågan. For legs 2 to 10, teams are responsible for their own transport to and from the changeover points.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://vasaloppet.se/lopning/vasastafetten-lopning/): 2027-08-21 — "Vasastafetten 2027 Datum 21 augusti" (was estimated 2027-08-14)

name: Midnattsloppet Göteborg
description: Midnattsloppet Göteborg is a festive, high-energy night race that winds through the city’s lively streets and along Avenyn, starting and finishing at Gustaf Adolfs torg. The race offers two distances, 5.2 km and 10 km, giving participants a unique experience with music, spectators and the joy of running late into the evening. Midnattsloppet is more than just a race—it’s a celebration and a memorable experience that brings together runners of all ages and abilities. In addition to individual races, there are team and corporate competitions that encourage togetherness and the joy of being active.
course_highlights: Two-lap course through central Gothenburg and along Avenyn
Start and finish at Gustaf Adolfs torg
Festive atmosphere with music and spectators along the course
additional: Start times: the 10 km starts at 21:15, the 5.2 km starts at 22:54, the costume start for the 10 km is at 21:48 and for the 5.2 km at 23:00. The time limit for the 10 km is 90 minutes from the last start group. At the 5 km lap point, runners arriving after 22:36 will not be allowed to continue for the second lap. A race pack and T-shirt are included with registration. You can use your wellness allowance through Benifex, Epassi and Benefits. Companies can purchase value codes for team and corporate competitions. The first start for the 10 km is at 21:15 and for the 5.2 km at 22:54. The 5.2 km entry fee includes, among other things, a T-shirt, timing, water along the course, refreshments after finishing and a digital diploma. A medal can be purchased separately.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://midnattsloppet.com/midnattsloppet-goteborg/): 2027-08-21 — "Datum: 21 augusti 2027 Distans: 10 km Första start: kl. 21.15" (was estimated 2027-09-04)
pipeline_log.evidence_quote: Datum: 21 augusti 2027 Distans: 10 km Första start: kl. 21.15

name: Hjorthagen Ultra Trail 100
description: Hjorthagen Ultra Trail 100 is an ultrarunning event in the scenic surroundings of Lill-Jansskogen in Stockholm, offering distances of 30, 50 and 100 miles. The race combines physical endurance with community in an intimate setting with a maximum of 100 participants. The course is an 11.8-kilometre loop with aid stations serving food and drink at set times. Runners finish both day and night, with generous time limits for each distance. The start and finish are at Stora Skuggans väg 22, with good transport links and nearby facilities.
course_highlights: 11.8-kilometre loop course in Lill-Jansskogen
Scenic surroundings with magical forest sections
Aid station with food and drink from Umara served at set times
additional: Maximum 100 participants. Time limits are 32 hours for 100 miles, 16 hours for 50 miles and 9 hours for 30 miles. The 30-mile finish cutoff is 23:00 on Saturday, the 50-mile cutoff is 06:00, and the 100-mile cutoff is 17:00 on Sunday. The start and finish area has parking, toilets, a tent, a restaurant, a 4-H farm and a café. Drinks are provided by Umara. Volunteer opportunities are available. The information states that parking is available at the venue and that it is close to the metro and buses.

name: Fjällvindenterrängen
description: Fjällvindenterrängen is a classic 10-kilometre mountain trail race from Laisaliden to Hemavan. The race takes you through beautiful mountain terrain along Drottningleden and finishes with a run through the ski area, crossing the finish line at the base station of Centrumliften. The race starts at 12:30 with a group warm-up and is limited to 200 participants to ensure a good experience. After the finish, energy, drinks and fruit are provided, and food and fika can be purchased at Anders Bistro. A family evening to get ready for the race is held the night before at Arena Hemavan.
course_highlights: 10 km of mountain terrain along Drottningleden
Crossing Mortsbäcken, followed by a steep, technical downhill section
The final stretch runs through the ski area, descending to the finish
additional: A bus to the start is included, departing at 11:30 from the Centrumhuset car park in Hemavan. There is a water station after approximately 5–6 km. Timing chips are handed out at the start and must be returned after the finish. The prize ceremony takes place at approximately 13:30 in the finish area. Warm-up clothes can be left at the start to be transported to the finish. Toilets are available in Centrumhuset, but there are no showers. There is an outdoor toilet at the start. Start at 12:30 with a group warm-up. Limited to 200 participants; the entry fee includes bus transport to the start and energy at the finish.

name: Tough Viking
description: Tough Viking Kungl. Djurgården is a spectacular obstacle course race that takes you through Stockholm’s beautiful and historic surroundings. The course offers a varied mix of fast running sections, technical obstacles, strength challenges, and water elements. The race is spectator-friendly and suits both beginners and experienced OCR runners looking to combine speed, nature, and an authentic race atmosphere. The start and finish are located on Djurgårdsbrunnsvägen near the Maritime Museum, with a well-organized event area and services.
course_highlights: The course winds through the lush parks and historic landmarks of Royal Djurgården
Varied terrain with fast running sections and technical obstacles
Includes strength challenges and water elements
additional: Start times are selected during registration and sent by SMS before race day. Race bibs and timing chips are collected at the black Tough Viking tents by the Maritime Museum. The chip must be worn around the right ankle. A group warm-up is held 10 minutes before each start. Shoes with metal spikes are prohibited and will result in disqualification. Participants can compete individually or in teams (at least four people per team). Bag storage is available on site. The Open class has a minimum age of 12; participants under 18 need a guardian’s signature. There are four hydration stations along the course. Missing obstacles results in five penalty laps. Parking is limited, and public transport is recommended; changing tents are available, but there are no showers.

name: Rinkebyloppet 2026
location: Ursvikssidan av gångbron, Rinkeby, Stockholm, Sweden
description: Rinkebyloppet is an annual running race that starts on the Ursvik side of the pedestrian bridge in Rinkeby, crosses the bridge and follows Rinkeby Allé to the finish at Rinkeby Square. The race is a welcome tradition that also marks the start of the popular Rinkeby Festival. This year, there is also a class for participants with disabilities who use wheelchairs, following the same course and reaching the same finish as the other runners. Rinkebyloppet welcomes all runners and is part of the active and inclusive Rinkeby Run collaboration.
course_highlights: Start on the Ursvik side of the pedestrian bridge
Run across the bridge and along Rinkeby Allé
Finish at Rinkeby Square, marking the start of the Rinkeby Festival
additional: A new wheelchair class for participants with disabilities follows the same course and has the same finish as the runners. A wheelchair class is offered on the same course, with the same finish as the runners.

name: TMC (Tromsø Mountain Challenge) HalvUltra 25km
description: Tromsø Mountain Challenge is a weekend featuring four trail races in Tromsø’s unique mountain landscape, spread over two days. The HalvUltra 25 km starts at TUIL Arena and follows a demanding course through Tromsdalen, up Djupdalen to Bønntøva (760 m above sea level), and down Fjøyfjellet to Fjellstua before finishing at TUIL Arena. The race combines spectacular scenery with challenging terrain and attracts both new and experienced runners seeking a true Arctic running challenge.
course_highlights: Start at TUIL Arena and run through Tromsdalen
Climb to Bønntøva at 760 m above sea level, the race’s highest point
Spectacular descent via Fjøyfjellet and finish at TUIL Arena
additional: Bib pickup takes place at TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen. The HalvUltra 25 km has a time limit of 6 hours. Transport to the Ultra 50 km start is available by bus from TUIL Arena at 07:45. Bag storage is available at TUIL Arena. A self-declaration form must be completed before the start for the Ultra and HalvUltra. The time limit is 6 hours. Bib pickup takes place at TUIL Arena, and HalvUltra participants must complete a self-declaration form before the start. Places are limited.

name: Vikerfjell Challenge
description: Vikerfjell Challenge is a trail race for all levels, with distances of 21 km and 11 km, plus a separate 2.5 km children’s race. The courses pass through the beautiful Vikerfjell Nature Reserve, over varied terrain including gravel roads and trails. Start and finish locations are Ringerudsetra, Tossviksetra and Skarrudsetra. The event offers fantastic scenery and a great atmosphere, and is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners.
course_highlights: The courses pass through Vikerfjell Nature Reserve
Terrain includes gravel roads, trails and varied surfaces
Start and finish locations are Ringerudsetra, Tossviksetra and Skarrudsetra
additional: The race offers distances of 21 km, 11 km and a 2.5 km children’s race. Start and finish locations are at several mountain farms in the area. The courses offer varied terrain and scenic experiences. Aid stations, toilets, showers and baggage storage are available. Parking and transport information can be found on the website. The event also includes a 2.5 km children’s race. Start and finish locations vary by distance.

name: Hornindalsrokken Skyrace
location: Horndøla bru, Volda, Møre og Romsdal, Norway
description: Hornindalsrokken Skyrace is a challenging 17.5 km mountain race with 1,300 meters of elevation gain, held annually in Volda, Møre og Romsdal. The race starts at Horndøla bru and features a mix of gravel roads, rough off-road tracks, and technical alpine trails, including a steep ascent up Rokkeråsa with scrambling sections. Participants experience varied terrain and stunning natural scenery. Mandatory safety equipment is required due to the alpine conditions. The race emphasizes safety, sportsmanship, and respect for the environment.
course_highlights: 17.5 km distance with 1,300 m of elevation gain
Steep 1.3 km ascent up Rokkeråsa with 506 m of climbing and technical scrambling
Aid station at the top of Rokkeråsa (6.4 km)
additional: Registration and bib pickup at Horndøla bru from 07:30 to 09:15. Mandatory safety briefing from 09:15 to 09:30. The start and mandatory safety briefing are at Horndøla bru. Prize ceremony at Horndøla Camping at 15:00. Bus transportation is available from the finish at Trondstad Grendahus back to Horndøla Camping. Minimum age: 15 years. Maximum 200 participants. Mandatory equipment includes trail shoes with good grip, a windproof jacket, warm clothing, a warm buff or hat, gloves, an extra wool shirt, a first aid kit, a whistle, a charged phone, water, nutrition, and a climbing harness with a locking carabiner if the direct route is used. The organizer’s website lists different dates for 2027: 21 August in the main listing and 22 August in the practical information.

name: Skåbu fjellmaraton (Jotunheimvegen Ultra)
description: Jotunheimvegen Ultra is a spectacular ultramarathon starting at Bygdin Høifjellshotell on Valdresflya and following Jotunheimvegen, with fantastic views of the peaks of Jotunheimen. The race follows a gravel road past idyllic mountain farms along Vinstervatna, and from around 38 km follows the marathon course to the finish in Skåbu town centre, with a tough final climb up Kamfossbakken. This race offers a challenging and scenic experience in high mountain terrain, with several food and drink stations along the way. Skåbu Fjellmaraton also offers several distances suitable for all levels, but Jotunheimvegen Ultra is the highlight for ultrarunners.
course_highlights: Start at Bygdin Høifjellshotell on Valdresflya, approx. 12 km from Beitostølen
The race follows Jotunheimvegen, with views of the peaks of Jotunheimen and idyllic mountain farms along Vinstervatna
Finish with a tough 3 km climb up Kamfossbakken to the finish in Skåbu town centre
additional: Race bibs not collected in Skåbu are sent by bus in the morning and can be collected at the start. Luggage can be sent by bus to the finish and collected at the event office. Six food and drink stations along the route serving sports drink, water, bananas and cola. Cut-off time at the Slangen aid station is 14:00; runners arriving later may continue at their own risk or get a ride to the finish. Timing is provided by eqtiming.no, with split times at Slangen and Kamfossbakken. The “King and Queen of Kamfossen” climbing competition takes place at the Kamfossbakken split-time point. Late registration is possible up to 1 hour before the start. Parking is at Skåbu school, not by the finish area. Toilets and showers are available at the school. There are six food and drink stations along the route, with the first after 14 km. The cut-off time at Slangen is 14:00. Bus transport between Skåbu and Bygdin can be booked as an add-on when registering.

name: Høyjord Rundt og Rundt
description: Høyjord Rundt og Rundt is a varied race suitable for all levels, with distances from 6.1 km to 77 km. The course features technically challenging terrain with approximately 470 metres of elevation gain per lap, including trails, gravel roads and beautiful viewpoints. The event also includes a children’s race with an obstacle course and an untimed recreational run, so the whole family can take part and have fun. Everyone who finishes receives a medal, and food and drinks are available in the start/finish area. The race is organised by Høyjord Idrettslag and emphasises the joy of running, community and a great atmosphere.
course_highlights: Approximately 470 metres of elevation gain per 11 km lap, with technically challenging trails
Beautiful viewpoint at approximately 7 km on the course
Snack station with snacks and drinks at 2.5 km
additional: Dogs are not allowed on the technical courses, but dogs on a leash are permitted in the recreational run. Pacing is not allowed. The children’s race takes place on the artificial turf pitch and includes an obstacle course and a separate medal. The extra service offers the option to walk or run shorter distances without timing during the week before the race. Food and drinks are available in the start/finish area, including snacks, broth, coffee, cola, hot food and fruit.
