The race has a zero-tolerance policy for littering and requires mandatory equipment according to the equipment list. Registration is via Racetracker. The children’s race includes an obstacle course. The untimed extra service is available on Thursday or Friday of race week.

name: Langhusløpet
organizer: Langhusløperne i samarbeid med Langhus IL Alliansen
description: Langhusløpet 2027 is an inclusive race for all ages and abilities, held at Haugjordet Lower Secondary School in Langhus. Participants can choose between a children’s race, 5 km and 10 km. Everyone receives a medal, and all children receive a bun. The race combines asphalt with forest roads and trails, and offers a friendly, social atmosphere focused on the joy of running and community. Bag storage is available, and race bibs can be collected both the day before and on race day.
course_highlights: 10 km course with 75% asphalt and 25% forest roads and trails
400-metre children’s race, with a medal and a bun for every child
Start and finish at Haugjordet Lower Secondary School, with bag storage available
additional: Race bibs can be collected on Friday 13 August at Löplabbet in Ski Storsenter from 10:00 to 19:00, and on race day from 9:30 to 10:45 at the race office at Haugjordet Lower Secondary School. Prizes will be awarded to the top three men and women in the 5 km and 10 km races. All participants take part at their own risk, and parents are responsible for children who participate. The minimum age is 10 for the 5 km and 13 for the 10 km. The children’s race is open to all. Race bibs can be collected on race day at Haugjordet Lower Secondary School or at Löplabbet in Ski Storsenter.

name: Tromsø Mountain Ultra 50km
description: Tromsø Mountain Challenge is a weekend featuring four trail races in Tromsø’s unique mountain landscape, including the 50 km La Sportiva Ultra, which starts from Snarbyeidet. The races offer challenging trails, spectacular mountain and plateau views, and finish with a wonderful descent through Tromsdalen to the finish at TUIL Arena. The event attracts runners from all over the world and offers a true Arctic running experience in the fresh autumn air and beautiful fall colors. This is a race for both new and experienced trail runners looking for a challenging and scenic experience.
course_highlights: Start from Snarbyeidet on runnable mountain terrain, climbing to approximately 760 m above sea level
Pass nine checkpoints along the way during the ultra race
Spectacular descent through Tromsdalen to the finish at TUIL Arena
additional: Bib pickup takes place at TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen. The cutoff time for the 50 km ultra is 9 hours, with a checkpoint at Tromsdalselva (32 km) where the cutoff is 5.5 hours. Transport to the start from TUIL Arena is by bus at 07:45. Bags can be stored at TUIL Arena and transported by bus to the finish area. A self-declaration form must be completed before the start for the Ultra and HalvUltra. The maximum time is 9 hours. The cutoff at the Tromsdalselva checkpoint, after 32 km, is 5.5 hours. The organizer provides a bus from TUIL Arena to the start at 07:45, and Ultra runners must complete a self-declaration form. The number of start places is limited.

name: Nordvest Maraton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pris: 200 kroner for mosjon utan tid

description: Nordvest Marathon is a traditional race that has been held annually since 1991 in the beautiful and varied surroundings of Hareid Municipality in Sunnmøre. The race offers distances for everyone, including the full marathon, half marathon, 5 km and an untimed recreational class. The course offers scenic experiences along Grimstadvatnet and around Snipsøyrvatnet, with a varied route combining asphalt, gravel and tartan, over gently rolling terrain. The event is known as one of Norway’s most beautiful races and attracts both experienced and recreational runners.
course_highlights: The course runs along Grimstadvatnet and around Snipsøyrvatnet
Varied surfaces: asphalt, gravel and tartan
Gently rolling terrain in scenic surroundings
additional: Prize ceremony at 15:30 at the clubhouse. Medals for all finishers. Prizes for the top third in each class, with up to three prizes. Untimed participation is available at all distances, with a preferred start time of 11:00. Members of Hareid IL receive a NOK 100 discount, and those with an annual licence receive a NOK 50 discount. Registration is open on a rolling basis via RaceResult until the race starts. Start and finish are at Hareid Stadium. The recreational class is untimed.

name: Dalheim Rundt
description: Dalheim Rundt is a family-friendly trail race that starts and finishes at TUIL Arena in Tromsø. The course follows the network of trails and the floodlit ski trail through beautiful Tromsdalen, with a water station at Dalheim. This race is part of Tromsø Mountain Challenge, which offers spectacular nature experiences in rugged Northern Norwegian terrain, with challenging trails and great views. The event takes place in late August, when Northern Norway displays its finest autumn colours.
course_highlights: Start and finish at TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen
The course follows the network of trails and the floodlit ski trail through Tromsdalen to Dalheim
Water station at Dalheim amid scenic surroundings
additional: Race bibs are distributed at TUIL Arena in Tromsdalen. The number of starting places is limited, and registration is open while race bibs are available. The race is part of a weekend featuring several trail races in Tromsø, and several of the races finish with a spectacular descent through Tromsdalen to the finish at TUIL Arena. The race is part of Tromsø Mountain Challenge and the TMC Triple. The start time is listed as 12:00 on Saturday, 21 August 2027.

name: Vossaton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Barneløp (3-11år) Påmelding opnar i mai: Kr 35 – Påmelding

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Rabatt, kr 50, for medlemmer i Voss IL fram til 17.08. (gjeld ikkje for barneløp)

description: Vossaton running festival is an annual race held at Voss sports ground, starting on 21 August 2027. The event offers several distances, including a half marathon starting at Gjernes, as well as a children’s race for the youngest participants. It is an inclusive running festival, with cash prizes for the fastest times and extra prizes for course records. Participants can enjoy a varied course with several water stations along the way, and there is also an informal corporate relay with several legs.
course_highlights: Half-marathon start at Gjernes, approximately 1.5 km from the sports ground
Water stations at 5.2 km, 11.3 km, 16.4 km and the finish
Group jog to the start from the finish area before the half marathon
additional: The half marathon has a minimum age of 15. There are toilets at the start at Gjernes School. Clothing can be handed in in a separate bag or sack when collecting race numbers and will be transported back to the finish area. The corporate relay has 5–10 runners per team, with legs of approximately 2.5 km and just over 1 km. Late registration for the children’s race is possible until 15 minutes before the start. The three fastest times for women and men in each race receive prizes. An extra prize is offered for a course record: NOK 1,000 in the half marathon and NOK 500 in the 5 km. Members of Voss IL receive a discount.

name: Sami Maraton

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Pris: kr 100,- Deltakere 7-13 år får kr 50,- i rabatt.

description: Sámi Marathon is mainland Norway’s northernmost marathon and is held in the centre of Tanabru in Deatnu-Tana. The race offers compact, sociable courses with several passes by the stadium, creating a great atmosphere and bringing runners close to the spectators. Distances include the marathon, half marathon, 10 km, Run4Fun and MiniMarathon, with dedicated categories for para-athletes and children. All participants receive a medal at the finish, and prizes are awarded in several categories, with additional prizes for the fastest times over each distance. The race has a strong focus on community and the joy of running in the centre of Tana.
course_highlights: The marathon consists of 4 laps and the half marathon of 2 laps on officially measured courses
The courses are compact and close to the town centre, with several passes by the stadium
Suitable for all ages, with dedicated courses for children and para-athletes
additional: Race numbers and Emit timing chips can be collected at the stadium the day before the race between 18:00 and 19:30, or from 08:30 on race day. Please arrive at least 30 minutes before the start, or 1 hour beforehand if you have not collected your race number and chip. All participants receive medals. Family discount with a maximum combined entry fee of NOK 1,500 per family. Additional prizes for the three fastest times in the 10 km, half marathon and marathon. An earlier marathon start is available for participants expecting a running time of over 5 hours. The information page lists medals for all participants and changing facilities at Tana multi-purpose hall. Distance and price information applies to the published 2027 registration; the date 21 August 2027 has not been confirmed on the source pages.

name: Romerikes Råeste 2027
description: Romerikes Råeste is an action-packed obstacle race held in Nannestad’s unique, muddy ravine landscape. The race offers two courses of different lengths and difficulty levels, suitable for children, young people, recreational runners and competitive athletes. The main course is 6 km long with more than 60 obstacles, and there is also a family-friendly children’s course called Råtassen. The event combines challenges, a sense of achievement and community, and is a spectacular outdoor event near Gardermoen.
course_highlights: 6 km main course with more than 60 obstacles
Course through a muddy ravine landscape
Children’s course for ages 3–10 with exciting obstacles
additional: Starts are in groups of approximately 20–30 participants every 5 minutes, with 10–20 in the elite classes. Start and finish at Nannestad Idrettspark. It is possible to pick up your race pack before race day to avoid queues. There is a water station on the main course, but not on the children’s/family course. Romerikes Råeste caps in children’s and adult sizes are available to order when registering. Parking costs 100 kr and is paid via Vipps. The organiser’s website describes the 2026 edition but does not confirm race details for 2027. Råtassen is for children aged 3 to 10; guardians may accompany the children without a separate ticket.

name: Anholt Rundt 2027
distance_verbose: 44.5 km, Marathon, 23 km, Halvmarathon, 10 km, 5 km

name: Lüganuse rahvajooks
description: Lüganuse Public Run is part of the Ida-Viru Running Series and takes place in Kiviõli Central Square. The event offers several distances, from a children’s race to a 9 km run, suitable for different age groups and skill levels. Participants can enjoy a friendly, community-focused atmosphere and compete in the team category. Registration is easy and the entry fee is affordable, making this a great event for both recreational and experienced runners.

name: Detmolder Residenzlauf

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Das Startgeld beträgt 11,00 Euro für Erwachsene und wird per Bankeinzug nach der Anmeldung gezahlt.

description: The Detmold Residenzlauf is a long-standing running event taking place on 15 August 2026 in Detmold. The event offers various races for children, young people and adults, including a Bambini run, school races, a 5 km fitness run and the 10 km main race. The start and finish are on the Market Square in Detmold, providing a central and lively setting. The event is supported by Stadtwerke Detmold and AÜG NETZWERK as title sponsors and is known for its family-friendly atmosphere and a range of categories.
course_highlights: Start and finish on the Market Square in Detmold
Various distances from 1.5 km to 10 km
Timing with the Raceresult timing system
additional: Race bib collection on the event day from 15:30 at the Rathaus am Markt in Detmold. Timing is provided by the Raceresult timing system; personal chips are not permitted. Free admission to the Aqualip leisure pool upon presentation of the race bib. Medals for all participating children and young people. Awards ceremony on the Market Square: school races from around 18:30, 10 km race from 20:00. Friedrich-Brakemeier Challenge Trophy for the school with the highest participation rate. Vouchers for schools, teams and groups with the most advance registrations. The race attracts numerous participants from the region and, alongside the main distances, also features children’s races and special competitions. Results and certificates are available online.

name: Exter FlexRun! 2026
location: Sparkassen Sportpark Exter, Vlotho, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Exter FlexRun on 22 August 2026 at Sparkassen Sportpark Exter offers a flexible running format for all ability levels. Participants can choose their distance and run up to four laps of 10.5 km each, covering up to the full marathon distance. There are also relay events, walking and Nordic walking courses, and a children’s run. The event takes place in a scenic setting and offers a great atmosphere, with refreshments and entertainment on site.
course_highlights: Loop courses on paved paths and mostly asphalt roads in and around Vlotho Exter
Refreshment stations at 4.0 km, 8.5 km, and in Sportpark Exter
Showers, changing rooms, and a wide range of refreshments at Sportpark Exter
additional: The start and finish for all events are at Sportpark Exter. Flexible distance choice, with up to 4 laps (10.5 km each). 4 x 10.5 km relay for teams. Walking/Nordic walking: 10.5 km and 21 km. Children’s run: 1.6 km, from age 6. Team and company rankings with awards. Courses are marked and staffed by marshals. Registration is via Race Result; the event offers showers, changing rooms, refreshments, and is family-friendly.

name: Heideköniginnenpokal
description: The Heideköniginnenpokal (HeiPo) in Amelinghausen is a traditional fun run, taking place for the 31st time in 2026 as part of the Heideblütenfest week. The challenging routes pass through scenic landscapes, including along Lopausee. The race attracts many participants and is a mainstay of regional running events.
course_highlights: Scenic stretches
Route along Lopausee
Part of the Heideblütenfest week in Amelinghausen
additional: The Amelinghausen running group meets regularly on Mondays and Wednesdays to run together. There is also a beginners’ course that gradually introduces participants to running. The event is part of a lively running-group community that takes part in many fun runs and marathons across Germany. The race takes place in August, with typical summer weather around 25°C and possible rain. There are also children’s races and other fun runs as part of the festival week.

name: Jahn-Gedenklauf
description: The Jahn Memorial Run in Lanz is a traditional running event organized by SV Jahn Lanz e.V. The event takes place at the Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn Stadium and offers various distances, which also count toward the Prignitz Cup. The start time is 10 a.m., and the run is open to runners of all ages and ability levels. The event is supported by Kreissportbund Prignitz e.V. and is a fixture in the regional sports calendar.
course_highlights: Short course: 6.6 km
Long course: 12.5 km
Outside the Prignitz Cup: 3 km
additional: Courses are not suitable for spikes; on-site registration is possible; start at the stadium

name: 4. Rammelsberger Steigerlauf
description: The Rammelsberger Steigerlauf is a challenging mountain race in the northern Harz, held at the Rammelsberg UNESCO World Heritage Site in Goslar. The event offers a range of courses with gradients of up to 30%, winding through historic mining landscapes and varied forest and mountain sections. Participants can look forward to professional timing and a unique running experience with an alpine character. Courses range from a short race for children to a marathon and trail race with up to 1,110 meters of elevation gain. The event is aimed at runners, walkers, and trail runners looking to challenge their fitness and sure-footedness.

name: Osnabrücker 6-Stunden-Lauf
organizer: Norbert Dulle, Heinz Hagen, Maik Mittmann, Holger Schulze, Florian Siebelmann, Frank Wilke
description: The Osnabrück 6-Hour Run takes place on August 22, 2026, at Rubbenbruchsee in Osnabrück and celebrates its 10th edition. The run is a charity event supporting HelpAge’s “Every Grandma Counts” campaign and is open to all runners who want to cover as many kilometers as possible within six hours. Whether you’re an ambitious runner, training for a marathon, or simply looking to run, walk, or hike together in the beautiful landscape around the lake, everyone is welcome. The event offers individual and relay entries and emphasizes community and supporting a good cause.

name: Sieber Berg- und Panoramalauf
description: The Sieber Mountain and Panorama Run returns on August 22, 2026, after a 14-year break, offering three challenging routes in the Harz Mountains with up to 900 meters of elevation gain. The event is hands-on and welcoming, and challenges runners of all abilities. There’s something for everyone, from the family-friendly 4.5 km Nature Experience Route to the 12.5 km Panorama Loop and the 27.5 km queen stage with 900 meters of elevation gain. The routes pass through impressive natural scenery with panoramic views and offer a true Harz experience. Alongside the sporting challenge, there will be a pasta buffet and a community village festival to round off the day.

name: THE HUMBLE CLUB Backyard Run IV
description: The Humble Club Backyard Run IV on August 22, 2026, on Okerinsel in Braunschweig is a unique running experience that combines a sporting challenge with social commitment. The run supports the “Boxen gegen Parkinson” project and stands for exercise, community, and social responsibility. The event starts at 10:00 a.m., with admission from 8:30 a.m., and provides participants with basic refreshments of still water and fresh fruit, as well as an exclusive finisher’s medal. Participants are asked to bring their own refreshments so they can stay properly fueled.

name: Barumer Stick and Stone Run
description: The Barumer Stick and Stone Run is a challenging obstacle race taking place on August 22, 2026, at the Barumer Forest Stadium and in the surrounding wooded, hilly landscape of the Lüneburg Heath. The course follows sandy, muddy, and partly overgrown trails, with water obstacles such as ditches and a village pond. The event offers runners a varied challenge in a natural setting and is suitable for both individual participants and groups. Participants receive a medal and refreshments at the finish area.

name: Jan Schüpp Bürgerlauf Wittmund
description: The Jan Schüpp Wittmund Citizens’ Run is a running event organized by MTV Wittmund. It starts at the stadium on Breslauer Straße in Wittmund. The route runs through the town center, past the market square and Schlossplatz, and offers a challenging and varied course. In addition to the main races, there are children’s and youth races, which are free to enter. The event is well organized with support from the police, fire department, and German Red Cross (DRK), and is popular with runners and spectators.

name: middenmang-Loop 2. Emder Vielfaltslauf
description: The middenmang-Loop is an inclusive diversity run in Emden, taking place for the third time on August 22, 2026. The run is open to all age groups and to people with and without disabilities, bringing everyone together to enjoy running. A variety of events and distances, from the Kinner-Loop for children to the 10-km middenmang-Loop for experienced runners, offer something for everyone. The run is part of the Ostfriesische Sieben race series and promotes community, physical activity, and inclusion.

name: Maraton Wigry
description: The Wigry Marathon is a unique marathon held in Wigry National Park, around scenic Lake Wigry. The approximately 42.2 km course runs mainly along forest and unpaved trails, with a small amount of asphalt, offering runners pristine air and beautiful views of the Suwałki and Sejny regions. This is not a marathon for setting personal bests, but for those who want to enjoy its remarkable nature and atmosphere. The event takes place on August 22, 2026, starting at the Monastery in Wigry and finishing at the Municipal Square in Stary Folwark.

name: ews Volks- und Spendenlauf
description: The 14th ews Volks- und Spendenlauf runs through Bad Segeberg, past scenic spots such as Kalkberg and the Great Segeberger Lake. Since 2011, the race has been a regular part of the city’s sporting calendar, combining athletic achievement with the enjoyment of exercising together and charitable engagement. The event supports selected projects each year, with donations divided among three projects in 2026. It is a community event that brings together exercise and social commitment.
course_highlights: Through Bad Segeberg
Past Kalkberg
Along the Great Segeberger Lake
additional: Team entries are only possible using a paper form, which must be sent by email to info@volkslauf-bad-segeberg.de by 02 October 2023. Race number collection takes place at the registration desk on 23 August 2026. Registration is online and requires agreement to the liability waiver and data protection terms. The focus is on enjoying exercise and charitable engagement. The race runs through Bad Segeberg and includes walking and Nordic walking. Donations support local projects. Registration is open until June 2026. Team and individual starts are possible.

name: Rotherbaum 10K Hamburg - K Rotherbaum
description: The 10K Rotherbaum is an officially measured 10-kilometer race in Hamburg, held in accordance with international competition regulations. The course is a loop registered with the German Athletics Association and AIMS, making finish times eligible for rankings. The event is open to runners of all age groups and offers a cup competition across all 10K Hamburg races, with attractive prizes. Registration is online only, and participants are asked to travel by public transport.

name: Der Alstertallauf
description: The Alstertallauf is a family-friendly race along the upper Alster hiking trail, considered Hamburg’s most beautiful running route. It welcomes running enthusiasts of all ages and recreational athletes, and offers several distances. The event takes place near the Albert-Schweitzer-Gymnasium in Hamburg and is known for its friendly atmosphere. In 2022, more than 200 runners took part, with distances ranging from 410 m to 10 km.

name: Gettorfer Staffelmarathon
description: The Gettorf Relay Marathon is a team marathon taking place on 23 August 2026 at Sportpark Gettorf. The course is a loop of approximately 4.2 km, run ten times. Teams consist of 5 to 10 people who pass the chipped relay baton in the exchange zone. Alternatively, two people can take part in the Duo Marathon and freely divide the ten laps between them. Timing is electronic, using transponders and shoe chips, and split times are recorded for each runner.

name: Bielebohlauf
description: The Bielebohlauf Oppach is a running event in the Lusatian Highlands, offering a range of distances from 400 m to 20 km. The routes follow forest, meadow, and field paths as well as small roads around the Bieleboh. The longer distances are challenging and include steep climbs. Special Bambini and children’s races are available. Refreshments and entertainment are provided at Oppach Stadium, and finishers receive certificates and online clips.

name: 1. Laufchallenge Mellendorfer TV
description: The 2026 Sparkassen Running Pass for the Hanover Region features 43 running events, making it the largest series of its kind in Germany. Participants can collect stamps at various events across the Hanover Region and discover the region as they run. Each successful participation earns a stamp, and frequent runners can qualify for attractive gold, silver or bronze rewards. Participants register directly for the individual runs, which take place at many beautiful locations and offer a variety of activities. There is also a Running Pass app with an event calendar and digital running log.

name: Die Generalprobe
description: The dress rehearsal is an urban road race in Berlin, serving as perfect preparation for the BMW BERLIN-MARATHON. On August 23, 2026, runners can test their form on a super-flat loop through the Berlin districts of Steglitz, Wilmersdorf and Zehlendorf. Events include a quarter marathon, a half marathon, and races for children and young people. The event features a lively atmosphere and a personalized medal for all finishers.

name: IV BIEG PEŁNEJ MISKI
description: Bieg Pełnej Miski is a charity running event held in Szubin, aiming to support animal shelters through the “Pełna Miska” campaign. The race has been held annually since 2023, and the next edition is scheduled for August 23, 2026. The event combines sporting competition with the goal of helping homeless animals, engaging the local community and running enthusiasts. The organizers encourage people to take part and work together to support animals.

name: Biegi wokół Bursztynowej Góry
description: The Runs Around Bursztynowa Góra are an annual running event held in picturesque Bąkowo as part of the Kaszuby Biegają series. The races attract runners from various age categories, offering appealing routes and the unique atmosphere of Kashubia. It’s a great opportunity to spend time outdoors amid beautiful nature and local culture. The organizers ensure professional event management and a welcoming atmosphere for participants.

name: XVI Festiwal Biegowy Dziki Weekend
description: The 16th Dziki Weekend Running Festival is an annual sporting event held in Police, West Pomeranian Voivodeship. Organized since 2010 by the DZIK Running Club Association, the festival is one of the most recognizable races in the region. The event promotes an active lifestyle, cross-country running, and sporting competition for children and young people, while also showcasing the natural attractions of the Wkrzańska Forest. The start and finish of all races are at the sports clearing at 99 Piaskowa Street in Police.

name: Blodomloppet
organizer: Östersunds SK och Blodcentralerna i Jämtland/Härjedalen

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Anmälningsavgift Blodomloppet 5 eller 10 km: 350 kr (t.o.m 3 augusti).

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Blodomloppet 5 eller 10 km Ungdom (födda 2009 eller senare): 200 kr

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Blodomloppet 5 eller 10 km Ungdom (födda 2009 eller senare): 100 kr

description: Blodomloppet in Östersund is a fun run that raises awareness of the vital importance of blood donation. You can walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km, either on your own or with colleagues and friends. The races start and finish in Badhusparken and offer a well-organised, inclusive atmosphere for all participants. After the race, participants often get together for a shared picnic, strengthening the sense of community. Blodomloppet is a recreational activity with an important purpose and a long tradition in Sweden.
course_highlights: The 5 km and 10 km courses are marked with red ribbons and signs
A lead cyclist shows the way, and course marshals are stationed along the route
Start and finish in Badhusparken
additional: Late registration is possible on race day via the website or in person at the information tent, with payment by Swish. The courses have been officially measured and approved by certified course measurers. The start and finish are in Badhusparken. Marshals and traffic guards are stationed along the course, and a lead cyclist shows the way. Participation is at your own risk, as no accident insurance is provided. By participating, you consent to the publication of photos from the event. The final date for team registration is 20 August; after that, picnic bags are available while supplies last. The start and finish for all races are in Badhusparken. The courses are marked and staffed by marshals and traffic guards. Registration information and fees for 2027 may be updated.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://blodomloppet.se/vara-lopp/ostersund/): 2027-08-23 — "23 augusti 2027" (was estimated 2027-08-23)

name: Blodomloppet (Sundsvall)
organizer: Sundsvalls Orienteringsklubb och Blodcentralerna i Västernorrland
description: Blodomloppet in Sundsvall is a recreational race that highlights the life-saving importance of blood donation and welcomes participants to walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km. The event takes place at Ungdomsfältet in Södra hamnen, near the marina, and offers both individual and team starts. The courses are certified by the Swedish Athletics Federation and run counterclockwise along Selångersån, with scenic bridge crossings. Blodomloppet is a social, healthy activity that concludes with a group picnic for team participants.
course_highlights: Two certified adult courses: 5 km and 10 km
The courses run counterclockwise along Selångersån, crossing Sporthallsbron (5 km) and Montörsvägsbro (10 km)
Start and finish at Ungdomsfältet in Södra hamnen, near the marina
additional: Teams consist of 3–5 participants, with the option to add team members up to and including 18 August. A picnic bag for 5 people is included with team registration. Participants in the walking category may use poles or a stroller and bring a well-behaved dog on a short leash. Late registration for individual participants is available on race day from 15:30, at an increased fee, with payment by Swish. The courses are officially measured and certified by the Swedish Athletics Federation. Registration for 2027 has not yet opened. The race highlights blood donation and promotes a healthy lifestyle.

name: Sørkedalsløpet
location: Idrettslokalet i Sørkedalen, Sørkedalen, Oslo, Norway

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Alle klasser 22 år og yngre (nedre aldersgrense 8 år) kroner 285

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: Alle klasser fra 23 år og eldre kroner 435

description: Sørkedalsløpet is a real cross-country race on forest trails in Nordmarka, organised for the whole family. You can choose between a challenging, hilly 11 km course or a shorter 3 km course, both starting and finishing at Idrettslokalet in Sørkedalen. The race offers fresh air, a great atmosphere, and homemade elk soup and buns in the finish area. It is a friendly, local weekday race suitable for runners of all ages.
course_highlights: Cross-country race on forest trails and gravel roads in Nordmarka
Hilly 11 km course and shorter 3 km course
Start and finish at Idrettslokalet in Sørkedalen
additional: Wave starts: 11 km at 18:00 and 3 km at 18:20. Race bibs can be collected at Idrettslokalet from 16:00 to 18:15. Homemade elk soup and buns are served in the finish area. Sausages, cinnamon buns, coffee, and squash are also sold to spectators. Parking is not available at the venue, but there is parking about 700 m away at Sørkedalen utfartsparkering. Bus 41 stops at the venue. Previous editions have served refreshments at the finish, including elk soup and buns.

name: B2Run Hamburg
description: The B2Run Hamburg on August 25, 2026, is a corporate run covering around 5.6 km and ending with a spectacular finish in the Volksparkstadion. The varied course is mostly flat, making it ideal for beginners, walkers, and experienced runners. The event promotes team spirit, motivation, and a sense of community, and is perfect for companies and individual entrants from Hamburg and the surrounding area. Alongside the sporting experience, the run offers a professional supporting program with commentary and music.

name: Bolechowo na Sportowo
organizer: Centrum Rozwoju Kultury Fizycznej AKWEN w Czerwonaku
description: Bolechowo na Sportowo, or Active Czerwonak at Night, is a recurring, free sporting event organized by the Czerwonak Physical Culture Development Centre. The event takes place in the evening and combines physical activity with bringing the local community together. It is a long-standing tradition that attracts participants who want to spend time outdoors, running or walking in a friendly atmosphere.
course_highlights: A 5 km distance confirmed for the 2026 edition
Evening event format in Bolechowo
Part of the Active Czerwonak at Night series
additional: The event is free and takes place in the evening, usually from 19:30 to 22:00. It is a recreational sporting event and part of the Czerwonak Grand Prix series. No information is available about participant limits, fees or required equipment. Previous editions took place in the evening; 82 participants took part in 2026.

name: Blodomloppet Västerås
price_range: 350–450 kr för 5 eller 10 km; 100–150 kr för Lilla Blodomloppet

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: därefter sker en höjning på 50 kr (400 kr) kallat ”Efteranmälan”

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 100 kr Lilla Blodomloppet Anmälan från 7/8 – 150 kr

description: Blodomloppet in Västerås is a recreational race that highlights the vital importance of blood donation and welcomes everyone to walk, jog or run 5 km or 10 km. The race is open to both individual participants and teams. Teams can consist of 3–5 people, who can take part in different distances. There is also Lilla Blodomloppet for children aged 1–12, with two shorter distances. The start and finish are at the Rocklunda area, with clearly marked courses and several marshals along the way. After the race, all participants receive a medal and a finish-line goody bag, and team participants are invited to a group picnic.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Rocklunda area, on the football pitches north of the riding arena
The courses are marked with Blodomloppet course tape, with flag marshals at strategic locations
Lilla Blodomloppet for children features two distances of approximately 1,400 m and 500 m around Rocklunda IP
additional: The race offers a warm-up in front of the stage at approximately 17:00. Lilla Blodomloppet has two start times: approximately 17:15 for 1,400 m and approximately 17:25 for 500 m. Teams can consist of 3–5 participants and include a picnic for 5 people. Race bibs and T-shirts are handed out, and there are water stations along the course. Registration is binding and cancellations are not accepted. Teams consist of 3–5 participants. The team fee covers five people and includes a picnic.

name: Norrköpings Stadslopp (Nkpg City)

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Gratis anmälan för alla barn och ungdomar.

description: NKPG City Norrköping City Race is a fast-paced and popular running event held in central Norrköping, starting and finishing on Olai Kyrkogata. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km, with a course that passes through classic surroundings, lined with cheering spectators and featuring more than ten music stations to create a wonderful atmosphere. The race welcomes both elite runners and recreational runners in a festive atmosphere, with great prizes and a large crowd. Children can also take part in the free 1 km children’s race, Lilla Lundbergsloppet, with a medal and goodie bag for every participant.
course_highlights: Start and finish on Olai Kyrkogata in central Norrköping
The course passes through classic Norrköping surroundings, lined with cheering spectators
More than ten music stations along the course to keep runners motivated
additional: Lilla Lundbergsloppet starts at 17:00 in four waves and is free for children. The children’s warm-up is led by Friskis & Svettis at 16:40. The 10 km race starts at 18:30 and the 5 km race starts at 19:30, with warm-ups 15 minutes before each start. Race numbers can be collected at XXL Ingelsta on Wednesday 26 August from 11:00 to 18:00, or on race day from 15:00 at the start and finish area. There are veteran, junior and youth categories, as well as team competitions for women, men and mixed teams. Water stations are located at 2 km and 7 km (Nodra), and at 3.5 km and 8.5 km (ICA Strömmen). After finishing, participants are offered water drilled by Finspångs Brunnsborrning. Timing is by chip, and results are published directly after the finish. ARQLY-Spurten is a race within the race on the final 85 metres, with sprint prizes. 5 km and 10 km. Lilla Lundbergsloppet is free for children.

name: GKN-stafetten 2026 (del av Trollhättan Action Week)
description: The GKN Relay is a relay race held along the Trollhättan Canal during Trollhättan Action Week. Each team consists of four participants, each running 3 kilometres on a flat course around the canal. The event is full of team spirit and energy, with live music and an evening of fun and camaraderie. Participants can pick up their race bibs and relay baton the day before to avoid queues. After the race, there is an opportunity to enjoy a picnic and entertainment at the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat course around the Trollhättan Canal
Team relay with 4 participants, 3 km per leg
Running combined with live music and a picnic at the finish
additional: Race bibs and the relay baton can be collected the day before at Odenhuset. NearYou offers a staffing pool to cover late withdrawals from teams. After the race, there is live music and the opportunity to picnic at the finish area. Race bibs and the relay baton can be collected the day before the race.

name: Höga Kusten Trail
description: Höga Kusten Trail is one of Sweden’s most popular adventure races, offering a weekend filled with spectacular nature, community and celebration in the High Coast World Heritage Site. The event features five unique distances over two days, with each course taking you across some of the High Coast’s most iconic and dramatic peaks. Combining running, jogging and fast hiking, the event is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners. Alongside the races, there are cosy pre-event evenings, after-trail parties and a mini expo featuring equipment from leading outdoor brands. Höga Kusten Trail is more than just a race—it’s a complete experience in one of Sweden’s most beautiful settings.
course_highlights: Five unique distances over two days, ranging from 14 km to 60 km
Courses pass through the High Coast World Heritage Site and offer spectacular views and nature experiences
Aid stations and course marshals along the route, plus race briefings and an equipment expo before the races
additional: The races take place over two days, with five distances. On Friday, Three Peaks 18k and Coast to Summits 28k start; on Saturday, Twin Peaks 14k, The Original 45k and The Ultimate 60k start. There is a race briefing before each distance and after-trail parties in the evenings. Buses run from FriluftsByn to the start locations. There is also a mini expo featuring equipment from Icebug and Haglöfs. You can sell your entry through the participant group on Facebook, and optional insurance can be purchased through Startklar. Registration for 2027 opens Friday, 5 March at 15:00. Distance and programme details for 2027 may change; published prices apply to 2026.

name: Istrun
description: Istrun Half Marathon is a flat and fast course (approx. 70 m elevation gain), officially measured and approved by SFIF, offering ideal conditions for setting a half marathon personal best.

name: HTB Ole Bull-løpet 2027
description: HTB Ole Bull Run is a traditional fun run organised by Osterøy IL Athletics. The race is part of a series of fun runs and running events in beautiful surroundings on Osterøy in Vestland. Participants can look forward to a well-organised race experience starting at Furubakken sports ground, with options for walkers and the main field. The event has a friendly atmosphere, with prizes and refreshments for participants.
course_highlights: The course is 4.4 km long
Starts at Furubakken sports ground, Valestrandsfossen
Start times: 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field
additional: Prizes are provided by local sponsors such as Extra Valestrand and Toro. Sveler (Norwegian pancakes) and squash are served to participants. The race is part of a series with several events throughout the year, including a Christmas run and a New Year’s run. Registration is available at the start at Furubakken sports ground or via Vipps 121337. The series lists start times of 18:45 for walkers and 19:00 for the main field. Previous editions have featured 4 km and 6 km courses, but distances for 2027 have not been announced.

name: Sognefjord Trail Run
description: Sognefjord Trail Run is a spectacular trail-running experience in beautiful Kaupanger, Vestland. Choose from the 17K, 27K, 45K Ultra or a 1 km Kids Race. The courses offer varied terrain, including forest trails, mountain sections and fantastic views of the Sognefjord. The event has an inclusive atmosphere, with well-marked courses, helpful volunteers and a social post-race gathering in central Sogndal.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with forest trails, mountains and technical sections
Fantastic views of the Sognefjord and mountain peaks such as Søre Gråbrørne
Flowing trails and challenging climbs, including up to Amlaholten and Store Haugmælen
additional: Start times: 08:00 for 45K Ultra, 11:30 for 17K, 12:00 for 27K, 15:00 for Kids Race. Bib collection and check-in Friday 16:00-21:00 in Sogndal and Saturday morning in Kaupanger. Post-race gathering with music and an awards ceremony in central Sogndal from 20:30. The courses include asphalt, gravel and trails. Kids Race for children aged 2-13 over 1 km. Food available for purchase after the finish. The 2027 edition is part of the Norge Trail Series (NTS), and registration is open.

name: Arctic Alta Ultra 2027
description: Arctic Alta Ultra is a challenging ultrarun held in Tverrelvdalen, starting and finishing at Ungdomshuset. The race offers several distances from 6 km to 100 miles, with well-marked courses and aid stations along the way. Participants can use bag-drop points on the longer distances, and the finish area has facilities including a café, changing rooms and showers. The event combines nature experiences with challenging terrain in the beautiful surroundings of Alta.
course_highlights: Aid stations on all distances, with several unmanned stations on the 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile distances
Bag-drop points for the 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile distances
Start and finish at Ungdomshuset in Tverrelvdalen, with facilities including a café and showers
additional: Participants in the 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile races must sign a runner's declaration before the start. Race manuals are available for the 16 km, 29 km, 50 km, 100 km and 100-mile distances. The start and finish address is Sønvismoen 44, 9537 Tverrelvdalen. For the 2026 edition, a café, changing rooms with showers and an awards ceremony at Ungdomshuset in Tverrelvdalen are listed. These practical details have not been confirmed for 2027.

name: Naktinis bėgimas 2026
description: Night Run 2026 invites you to feel the rhythm of the night and immerse yourself in the end-of-summer buzz in Kaunas. It’s a unique opportunity to unwind from everyday life and end the summer with an energetic run featuring music, a sea of lights, and the company of enthusiastic runners. The event takes place in Town Hall Square and Santaka Park, offering spectacular views and an unforgettable nighttime adventure. Participants compete in the 2.5 km, 5 km, and 10 km distances, and the event is intended for both amateurs and professionals.
course_highlights: Course in Town Hall Square and Santaka Park
Night run with music and a sea of lights
Races over 2.5 km, 5 km, and 10 km
additional: Participants must attach their bib with the timing chip to the front of their shirt. Registration details and race distance can be changed until 2026-08-23 for a €5 fee. A participant’s time may not be recorded if they do not complete the course within the set time limit. The use of vehicles on the course is strictly prohibited. The event will take place in Kaunas; the course features a night run with lights, music, and a lively atmosphere. Registration and further information are available on the official website.

name: Lemgoer Hanselauf

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Anmeldung am Veranstaltungstag ab 16 Uhr möglich

description: The Lemgo Hanselauf is a traditional running event held annually on the last or second-to-last Friday in August in Lemgo. The event offers 3.3 km, 6.6 km and 10 km courses along the city’s ramparts. Children and Bambinis can also take part over shorter distances, making the Hanselauf a family-friendly event. With around 1,000 participants, the Hanselauf is a sporting highlight in the region that brings together fun and community.
course_highlights: Course along Lemgo’s historic ramparts
Distances of 3.3 km, 6.6 km and 10 km
Children’s and Bambini runs over 1.5 km and 400 m
additional: Bib collection and late registration on the event day from 4 p.m. in the right-hand school wing of Engelbert-Kämpfer-Gymnasium. No timing or placings for the children’s and Bambini runs. Assemble at the start from 4:55 p.m. Participation is free. Run along the ramparts, children’s and Bambini runs, registration at Engelbert-Kämpfer-Gymnasium, late registration available on the event day.

name: Ibbenbürener Aaseelauf 2026
description: The Ibbenbüren Aasee Run is a long-standing running event taking place for the 41st time in 2026. The event offers races for children of kindergarten and primary-school age, as well as a 5 km fun run, a 5 km team run, and a 10 km main race for competitive and recreational runners. The course runs around Lake Aasee, with the start and finish at Stadion Ost in Ibbenbüren. The event is limited to 1,000 participants and is known for its family-friendly atmosphere and good on-course support.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Stadion Ost, Ibbenbüren
Loop course around Lake Aasee, with three laps in the 10 km main race
Drinks stations along the course and in the finish area
additional: Late registration is available on event day from 15:00 until 1 hour before the start of each race for a fee of €2.50. Changes to entries are also possible on event day for a fee. €1 per registration is donated to a charitable organization. Free parking is available at Stadion Ost. Race bibs can be collected on event day from 15:00. Timing is recorded using transponders on the back of the race bib. Registration is online only, with a limited number of places. Late registration costs €2.50; charitable projects can be supported.

name: Straßenlauf Rund um den Holtenauer Leuchtturm
Sparkassen-Tauchscher-Stadtlauf
description: The Sparkassen-Tauchscher City Run is a long-standing running event organized by the Leichtathletik Club Taucha e. V. in the town of Taucha on the Parthe River. The 21st edition of this city run takes place on August 28, 2026, and also includes the Saxon State Championships in the 10 km road race. The event offers runners of all age groups an attractive opportunity to compete in a lively atmosphere. Registration opens in February 2026.

name: Jönköping Marathon & Half Marathon
description: Jönköping Marathon & Half Marathon is a welcoming city race taking place on 29 August 2026, with beautiful views along Lake Vättern and through Jönköping and Huskvarna. The course has been redesigned to reduce the total elevation gain while retaining a varied profile with sections through nature, crowd support and several power zones; the marathon course finishes with a spectacular finish line right in the middle of Munksjö Bridge. The race attracts international participants and also features shorter races and a MINI children’s race, as well as offers for businesses and tent packages in the start/finish area.
course_highlights: Spectacular finish line right in the middle of Munksjö Bridge
Beautiful views along Lake Vättern and through Jönköping and Huskvarna, on a redesigned course with less elevation gain
Marathon: 42,195 m with 12 aid stations along the course plus 1 in the start/finish area, an interactive map and power zones
additional: Practical information from the website: up to five runners can be registered at a time; race bibs are not sent out. The marathon course has an interactive map and a downloadable PDF, power zones, and 12+1 aid stations. The organizer offers tent packages for businesses in the start/finish area and the option to use a wellness allowance. Distances: 21K (21,097.5 m) and 42K (42,195 m); includes a team relay and MINI Jönköping Marathon for children. Energy and aid stations along the course, chip timing, group registration for up to 5 runners, and a business village with tents in the start/finish area.

name: Stockholm Trail
description: Stockholm Trail is a trail race organised by OK Södertörn, offering a unique running experience in the beautiful Nackareservatet, just outside Stockholm City. The races follow winding forest trails and cross sunlit rock slabs, with courses suited to both beginners and experienced runners. The start and finish are at Hammarbyhöjdens IP, and the event has a welcoming atmosphere, with encouraging marshals and personal service. All proceeds from the race go directly to OK Södertörn’s activities.
course_highlights: The course runs entirely through nature, along technical forest trails and over beautiful rock slabs
Fantastic views and unique natural areas in Nackareservatet
Clearly marked courses with encouraging marshals along the way
additional: There are six different courses: 21K, 10K, 5K, 5K fun run (untimed), 2.5K kids, and Mini Trail for the very youngest participants. All participants receive a race bib with their name and a unique medal after completing the race. Showers and changing facilities are available at the venue. The course requires shoes with good grip and careful attention to roots and rocks. The 21K has a generous time limit to suit all runners.

name: Säve Trail Run
description:
Säve Trail Run 2027 

After a wonderful inaugural event in 2026, Säve Trail Run returns on 28 August 2027. We look forward to another day filled with the joy of running, community and wonderful nature experiences in Säve, north of Gothenburg. 

Säve Trail Run takes you through beautiful woodland, winding trails, soft pine-needle carpets and varied terrain. The route combines easy-running sections with technical features that give you that wonderful trail-running feel—whether you’re an experienced trail runner or trying it for the first time.

Choose the distance that suits you best: 12 km, 7 km or 2 km for children and beginners. 

The start and finish are at Säve Sportklubb, where runners, families and spectators gather for a day of exercise, joy and community.

All participants receive a medal to remember the event, and great prizes are promised for the podium finishers in each distance.

Säve Trail Run is for everyone. Whether you’re chasing a rush, want to challenge yourself or simply enjoy nature and the experience with others.

More information about Säve Trail Run 2027, including the race date, course profiles, maps and practical details, will be published on the website as it becomes available.

See you on 28 August 2027

name: Stockholm Halvmarathon
description: Stockholm Half Marathon is a popular half-marathon that runs through central Stockholm, starting and finishing at Strömbron, near the Royal Palace and the Parliament House. The course is 21,098 metres long and offers a fast, scenic route through the districts of Norrmalm, Vasastan, Kungsholmen, Gamla Stan and Södermalm. The race is an annual tradition that attracts runners from across the country and offers a unique opportunity to run through Stockholm’s historic and beautiful urban surroundings. The race starts at 15:30, and after the finish there is an after-run event in Kungsträdgården.
course_highlights: Start and finish by the Royal Palace and Strömbron
Fast course through Norrmalm, Vasastan, Kungsholmen, Gamla Stan and Södermalm
Clearly marked kilometres and police/officials at every intersection
additional: The expo and race-number pickup take place in Kungsträdgården in the days before the race. Race numbers are printed on site at the expo. The metro is the easiest way to get to the event area. After the race, there is an after-run event in Kungsträdgården. Race confirmation is sent by email from mid-August. The first start is provisionally at 15:30. Participants may start from the year they turn 17.

name: Midnattsloppet (Malmö)
description: Midnattsloppet Malmö is a festive, high-energy running experience taking place on 28 August 2027. Runners can choose between the 5 km and 10 km distances. The race starts late in the evening, creating a unique nighttime atmosphere in the heart of the city. The event is all about the joy of movement and community, with a carnival atmosphere, cheers from the crowd and music along the course. There is also the option to take part in costume races and corporate competitions, making Midnattsloppet a memorable and social experience for all participants.
course_highlights: The race runs through central Malmö’s streets in a festival-like atmosphere
Late-evening start times create a unique nighttime running experience
Music and activities along the course create a carnival atmosphere
additional: Costume races start at 21:12 for 10 km and 22:36 for 5 km. Corporate and team competitions are available to strengthen community and workplace wellbeing. The time limit for the 10 km is 90 minutes, with a cutoff after 6.6 km at 22:27. Race packs, shirts and wellness allowances via Benifex, Epassi and Benefits are available. After the race, an After Run with wraps and drinks is offered at a hotel from 23:00 to 01:00. The 10 km starts from 21:00 and the 5 km from 22:30. Costume starts are available for both distances. A team competition is available for the 10 km and gives a discount of 50 kr per person. Race packs are collected at the chosen Stadium store; a medal can be purchased as an add-on.

name: Trelleborgsloppet
description: Trelleborgsloppet is a well-known city race in Sweden’s southernmost city, Trelleborg, with a measured course offering both 5 km and 10 km running, as well as a 5 km walk or Nordic walk. The race starts at Östervångsstadion and finishes in Stadsparken, providing a lovely, spectator-friendly setting. Trelleborgsloppet is a festival for everyone, with both elite runners and recreational runners taking part, and participants can enter team competitions and prize draws for an extra chance to win. The event is marked by a sense of community and fun, with a focus on making the race enjoyable for all participants.
course_highlights: Measured city course with gun time
Starts at Östervångsstadion and finishes in Stadsparken
Course through an urban setting, with cultural landmarks and parks along the way
additional: Race bibs must be collected at Östervångsstadion no later than 45 minutes before the start, or the day before in the lobby of Söderslättshallen. Changing facilities are available at Söderslättshallen, with clothing transport to the finish. Timing uses a disposable chip (Neptron), and gun time is used. Late registration is available online until 45 minutes before the start and on site for an additional fee. A team competition is available, with extra prizes for groups of at least 8 participants. There is also a 5 km distance for walking and Nordic walking. Participants can compete individually or as part of a team.

name: Festivalloppet

late_fee.price: ordinarie anmälningsavgift + 60 kr för alla över 16 år

description: Festivalloppet is an annual running race organized in Strömsnäsbruk by SK Graal. The race offers an enjoyable competition setting for runners of different ages and ability levels, with the option to register late on race day. SK Graal is an active club that also offers training and membership benefits, such as discounts on running shoes. Festivalloppet is part of the club’s wide range of events and attracts runners from the surrounding area.
course_highlights: The course runs along the River Lagan in Strömsnäsbruk.
Previous editions have offered distances of 10 km and 4.8 km.
Children’s and youth categories have been included in previous editions.
additional: Late registration is available on race day until one hour before each start. Payment can be made in cash or by Swish. There is no late registration fee for the youngest children, youth, or the walking class. Clubs registering more than 5 participants can email a registration list and will be invoiced afterward.

name: Rynningeviken Längre 2026

tiers.label: tier_2
tiers.description: 16 augusti - 21 augusti (10.00/13.00) 695 SEK. Begränsat antal platser.

description: Rynningeviken Längre is a running race in Örebro that challenges participants to run as far as they can in three or six hours in the scenic Rynningeviken Nature Reserve. The course is a beautiful loop of approximately 2.4 km, mostly on gravel paths with a few bridges, close to the city centre. The event is a celebration of running, focusing on endurance and community, where participants can take on a unique challenge and aim for personal distance records. There is also a KidsRun for the youngest runners. The event is open to all ages and offers a wonderful day filled with the joy of running.
course_highlights: A 2,412.5-metre loop, mostly on gravel paths
Two bridges, with little elevation gain
Start/finish on cobblestones, with a shorter loop for the final 15–30 minutes
additional: Start times: 6-hour race starts at 11:00, 3-hour race starts at 14:00, KidsRun starts at 11:30. A mandatory race briefing takes place before each start. Timing is recorded using a transponder, which is loaned to participants and must be returned after the race. There is no timing for the KidsRun. At the finish, the distance is measured precisely using a measuring wheel. Water and energy supplies are available along the course, including sports drink, bars, fruit, coffee and more. Changing facilities and showers are not provided, but swimming is possible in the Svartån River. Toilets are available near the start area and after approximately 1 km on the loop. Participation is at your own risk. Group registration and discounts for young people and members of certain running clubs are available. The timed races are 3 and 6 hours long. The KidsRun is for children born in 2015 or later and covers either one full lap or a shorter 700-metre distance.

name: Kraftloppet Skellefteå Löpning 2026
description: Kraftloppet in Skellefteå is a festival for both competitive recreational athletes and casual runners looking to challenge themselves in three different events: skiing, cycling and running. The running event offers distances of 21 km and 12 km, as well as children’s races of 2.7 km and 500 m. Kraftloppet focuses on health and community, and offers the opportunity to complete a Kraftklassiker by taking part in all three events during the same calendar year.
course_highlights: Running distances of 21 km and 12 km, plus children’s races of 2.7 km and 500 m
Recreational races with both shorter and longer distances for different ages and ability levels
Part of the Kraftklassiker, which includes skiing, cycling and running in the same year
additional: The Kraftklassiker rewards participants who complete Kraftloppet skiing, Kraftloppet cycling and Kraftloppet running during the same calendar year. Registration is available via links on the registration page. Contact Bergsbyns SK by phone at +46 (0)910-861 61 or by email at info@kraftloppet.com. The organizer’s published information lists the running event on 29 August 2026; it does not confirm the date of 28 August 2027.

name: Dundret Extreme Running
description: Dundret Extreme Running is a trail race held in Gällivare, starting and finishing at Hellnerstadion. The event offers three distances: 22 km, 10 km and 2 km, all featuring varied terrain and elevation changes that challenge runners of different levels. K22 is a demanding test with 800 metres of elevation gain and beautiful views of Sarek and Kebnekaise, while K10 and K2 offer shorter but still challenging courses. The race is well organised, with safety measures, aid stations, prizes for the fastest runners and a prize draw open to all participants.
course_highlights: K22: 22 km with 800 metres of elevation gain, a mix of trails and paved roads, highest point at 823 metres above sea level
K10: 9.6 km with 240 metres of elevation gain, a mix of gravel and trails, turnaround point at Femmanvägen
K2: 2.1 km trail loop around Hellnerstadion with 60 metres of elevation gain, a fast and manageable distance
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Hellnerstadion from 08:00 to 09:30. All participants must cross the finish line or notify a race official if they withdraw. Aid stations along K22 and K10 offer water and Umara sports drink. Changing rooms and showers are available at Hellnerstadion. The prize-giving ceremony takes place at 13:00 for K10 and K22, including a mountain prize for K22. All K2 finishers receive a medal. Live results and split times will be published via a link on race day. The registration page states that registration is through MittLopp.se and that registration on race day is not possible. Current prices and distances for 2027 have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Mandalsmaraton
location: Giert Karis Plass, Bryggegata, Mandal, Norway
description: Mandalsmaraton is one of Norway’s oldest marathons, first held in 1980. The race runs through Mandal’s charming town-centre streets and scenic surroundings, including Furulunden and its idyllic beaches. The course is flat and consists of a 10 km loop, run multiple times depending on the distance. The event aims to be inclusive of everyone, whether you run, jog or walk, and offers a lively atmosphere with music and an enthusiastic crowd.
course_highlights: Flat 10 km loop with a national C certificate
The course runs through the town centre and Furulunden, with beautiful natural scenery
Three aid stations with water, sports drink, cola and bananas
additional: The start and finish are in Bryggegata by Giert Karis Plass. Pacers are available for all distances. Bag storage is offered at Kirkesenteret in Gågata, near the start area. After the finish, Hr. Redaktør invites participants to an After Run with food and drinks. Changing rooms and showers are available at Mandalshallen nearby. Free parking is available at Speidertomta and Mandal Videregående Skole. All participants must have a licence, either an annual licence or a one-time licence when registering. Red Cross medical personnel are present on the course. The start and finish are in Bryggegata by Giert Karis Plass. Aid stations are located at 4.2, 7 and 9.8 km. Changing rooms and showers are available at Mandalshallen, and bag storage is at Kirkesenteret. Strollers and dogs are not allowed on the course.

description: Porsgrunn Half Marathon is an inclusive road race for all levels, with distances including a children’s race, 5 km, 10 km and half marathon. The start and finish are at Franklintorget outside Down Town shopping centre, where there will also be entertainment, stalls and a free children’s race. The courses are officially measured, and there is a great atmosphere along the route, with entertainment for both runners and spectators. All participants receive a medal, and the event is a community celebration focused on making participation accessible to individuals, families, friends and businesses.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Franklintorget outside Down Town shopping centre
600-metre children’s race through the shopping centre
Officially measured courses with entertainment along the route
additional: Race bibs can be collected on Friday, 27 August, from 16:00 to 19:00 at Down Town shopping centre, and on race day from 09:30 outdoors at Franklintorget. The 600-metre children’s race is free, requires no registration and awards a medal to everyone. Registration is binding, but entries may be resold via EQ timing. A 35 NOK registration fee is added. Register by 8 August 2027 to have your name printed on your race bib. The event offers a 5 km, 10 km, half marathon and a free 600-metre children’s race. The course and distance information refers to details published for the 2026 edition.

name: Lyderhorn Opp
description: Lyderhorn Opp is an uphill race organized by Laksevåg Turn og Idrettslag, finishing at the summit of Lyderhorn, 396 metres above sea level. The course is approximately 3.8 km long and is suitable for both competitive and recreational runners. Participants receive a race bib and T-shirt, and everyone who finishes receives a medal and a T-shirt. Prizes are awarded to the three fastest men and women, and gift prizes are drawn among participants.
course_highlights: Approximately 3.8 km course finishing at the summit of Lyderhorn (396 metres above sea level)
Uphill race over varied terrain
Race bib and T-shirt for all participants
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts can be collected at Sport1 Vestkanten on the Friday before the race. Participants receive a 10% discount on one item of their choice at Sport1 Vestkanten when collecting their race bib. There are relatively good parking options, but walking, cycling or using public transport is recommended. First-aid personnel and defibrillators are available along the course. Gift prizes are drawn using race bib numbers during the event. The organizer's website states that the event has been cancelled and welcomes participants back in 2027.

name: Fjordkraft Bergen City Milen
description: Fjordkraft Bergen City Milen is a 10 km road race through the heart of Bergen city centre, starting and finishing at Torgallmenningen. The course offers a varied route that includes city streets, walking and cycling paths, tunnels, and scenic areas such as Småpudden and Nygårdsparken. The event is a community celebration that brings together local and visiting runners and is suitable for all levels and ages. With a long tradition dating back to 2012, the race is organised by Turn og Idrettsforeningen Viking, which emphasises community, activity, and quality.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Torgallmenningen in Bergen city centre
The course passes through Kronstadtunnelen and includes a turnaround
Passes scenic areas such as Småpudden and Nygårdsparken
additional: Race bibs and T-shirts can be collected at JUICE Galleriet. Race-bib distribution closes at 14:00 on race day. Changing rooms and clothing storage are available at Vikinghallen. The children's race, Mini-Milen, starts at 15:00. The awards ceremony is at 17:00. All participants receive a medal, drinks, and light refreshments. An administration fee of NOK 25 is charged in addition to the entry fee, along with a licence fee for the athletics federation. A children's race is also held. The official race website lists 18 September 2027, which differs from the date in the race listing.

name: Ledenløpet (Fåvang–Øyer)
distance_verbose: 27 km, 17 km, 7 km, 5 km, 3000 meter, 1 km
price_range: Gratis for 1 og 3 km; 250–500 kr for øvrige distanser
description: Ledenløpet is a race through the cultural landscape in the heart of Gudbrandsdalen, with six distances suitable for different ages and levels. The races start at various locations and finish at Nermo Hotell in Øyer. It is an inclusive event, with both timed races and free distances for children, and promotes environmental friendliness by being cup-free. Ledenløpet also offers carpooling to the start and nutrition packages tailored to runners.
course_highlights: Run through the cultural landscape of Gudbrandsdalen
Finish at Nermo Hotell for all distances
Several starting locations, with distances ranging from 1 km to 27 km
additional: Race bibs are distributed at the start, no later than 15 minutes before the race begins. Ledenløpet is cup-free, so runners must bring their own cup or bottle for the drink stations. Bus transport to the start from Nermo Hotell is available for Langleden and Mellomleden. The maximum total number of participants is 250 runners. Prizes for the top three in the men's and women's categories at each distance: a model of their choice of ON running shoes from Sport 1 Hafjell. Distances: 27 km Langleden, 17 km Mellomleden, 7 km Stuttleden, 5 km Ekstrastuttleden, 3 km and 1 km Bringebærleden. Bringebærleden for the youngest participants is untimed. The race is cup-free, so bring your own cup or bottle. Race bibs are collected at the start.

name: Kolbotnvannet Rundt
location: Kolbotn Kulturhus (Kolben), Kolbotn, Nordre Follo, Norway
organizer: Kolbotn IL Allianse og Kolbotn Run
description: Kolbotnvannet Rundt is an annual race organized by Kolbotn IL Allianse, with the start and finish at Kolbotn Kulturhus (Kolben) in Nordre Follo. The race offers a scenic loop around Kolbotnvannet and attracts both recreational and competitive runners. The event has a friendly atmosphere and also includes children’s races, making it family-friendly. Results from previous years show strong performances in both the 5 km and 10 km distances.
course_highlights: A route around Kolbotnvannet in scenic surroundings
Start and finish at Kolbotn Kulturhus (Kolben)
Suitable for both recreational and competitive runners
additional: The organizer is Kolbotn IL Allianse. The start and finish are at Kolbotn Torg, Strandliveien 4, 1410 Kolbotn. Children’s races are also held as part of the event. A 1 km race is offered for participants aged 6 and up, as well as a children’s race of approximately 500 meters. The start area is near Kolbotn station.

name: Damvegen Opp
description: Damvegen Opp is a challenging uphill race in Ålvik, with a 4.5 km course and a total elevation gain of 600 metres. The race follows a gravel road and offers a test of both fitness and willpower, rewarded with fantastic views. Participants can run, jog, walk or “gog” at their own pace, but must finish within the 2-hour cut-off time. Two aid stations along the way provide hydration, and refreshments and a medal await everyone who finishes at the top. The Red Cross is on hand to help ensure a safe experience for everyone.
course_highlights: 4.5 km course with 600 metres of elevation gain
Gravel road throughout
Two aid stations along the way and refreshments at the top
additional: The cut-off time is 2 hours. Everyone who finishes receives a medal. The Red Cross is present throughout the race for safety. The Red Cross helps ensure safety along the course, and everyone who finishes receives a medal. Previous information gives a participant limit of 50.

name: Kodalmila
location: Kodal IL Stadion, Kodal, Sandefjord, Norway
price_range: 50-300 kr (+ lisens på 5 km og 10 km)
description: Kodalmila is Vestfold’s oldest recreational race and is being held for the 47th time. The event offers several distances, including road and trail races, starting from Kodal town centre and Kodal IL Stadium. It is family-friendly, with a children’s race and shorter trail races, and is a traditional community celebration for runners of all ages. Race bibs can be collected at the clubhouse on race day, and registration is via EQ Timing.
course_highlights: 10 km road race starting at 14:00
5 km trail race starting at 14:05
2.5 km trail race and children’s race starting from Kodal IL Stadium
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Kodal IL’s clubhouse at Rismyrveien 10b on race day from 12:00. The start for the 10 km, 5 km and 2.5 km trail races is at the bus stop in Kodal town centre, while the children’s race starts at Kodal IL Stadium. Registration opens on 1 December 2024. Registration is via EQ Timing. Race bibs can be collected at Kodal IL’s clubhouse on race day.

name: Forest Run Elverum
description: Forest Run Elverum organizes obstacle trail runs and activity days in and around Elverum, with its main base at Starmoen. The course features approximately 20 obstacles of varying difficulty and is suitable for all kinds of recreational runners, from beginners to more experienced obstacle runners. The event emphasizes teamwork, togetherness, and a sense of achievement, and aims to foster good relationships between participants. Forest Run also offers team participation and tailored activities for schools, businesses, and private groups.
course_highlights: Obstacle trail run with approximately 20 obstacles
Course through woodland at Starmoen, 10 km east of Elverum town centre
Obstacles of varying difficulty, suitable for both beginners and experienced runners
additional: The course and obstacle course are rebuilt, and the facilities can be rented by schools, stag parties, birthday groups, and for team building. The focus is on teamwork and a sense of achievement, with activities for both recreational runners and more professional obstacle runners. The team also organizes group trips to other obstacle races. To register as a team, participants register individually and select the same team. Shoes with good tread are recommended; expect to get wet and muddy.

name: Stavanger Marathon
location: Mariero Station cycle path, Stavanger, Norway
description: Stavanger Marathon is a well-organized race offering distances for everyone, from a children’s race to a full marathon. The courses combine asphalt and gravel and take runners through scenic surroundings around lakes and fjords in Stavanger. The start and finish are in the city centre by Stavanger Cathedral, with a lively festival atmosphere on the last Saturday in August. The race has pacers, good facilities, and prizes for both the best times and course records.
course_highlights: The marathon course goes around three lakes and along Hafrsfjord and Gandsfjorden, with approximately 130 metres of elevation gain
80% asphalt and 20% gravel
Start and finish by Stavanger Cathedral; the 5 km starts at Mariero station
additional: Race numbers can be collected at Radisson Blu Atlantic Hotel on Friday 27 August and Saturday 28 August. The 5 km starts at Mariero station; the other distances start by Stavanger Cathedral. The half marathon is divided into 8 waves, starting 3 minutes apart. Bags can be left at Kongsgård School. Free showers are available at Stavanger Swimming Hall after the race. Prize ceremonies take place at different times for the various distances. Prizes are awarded for course records and for the best youth and teenage runners. Sports drink and bananas are available along the course and at the finish. The start is by the cycle path at Mariero station. Race numbers can be collected at Radisson Blu Atlantic Hotel. The marathon course has approximately 280 metres of elevation gain.

name: Nordre Follo Maraton
description: Nordre Follo Marathon is the municipality’s own marathon, starting and finishing in Ski town centre. The race takes place on Saturday, 28 August 2027 at 12:00 and offers several distances, including the marathon, half marathon, 10 km, 5 km and a children’s race. The course showcases the municipality from Oppegård to Kråkstad and serves as a natural tune-up race for the Oslo Marathon. Ski town centre is easily accessible by the Follobanen, which takes eleven minutes from Oslo S.
course_highlights: Course from Oppegård to Kråkstad
Start and finish in Ski town centre
A great showcase of Nordre Follo municipality
additional: The race is organised by Puls Samfunn and Ung300. Registration has not opened yet; check with the organiser for updates. The event is scheduled about a month before the Oslo Marathon as a natural tune-up race. Ski town centre is eleven minutes from Oslo S by Follobanen. Registration has not opened yet. Ski is around 11 minutes from Oslo S by Follobanen.

name: 4. Backyard Ås
description: Backyard Ås is a unique endurance race based on the backyard ultra format, where participants run a 6.7 km loop every hour on the hour. The race continues until only one runner remains, testing both physical endurance and mental strength. The course follows scenic trails in Ås, Norway, and offers a varied mix of asphalt, gravel, and forest trails. The event takes place in scenic surroundings just 30 minutes south of Oslo and is an official Backyard Ultra Association race, with results counting toward international rankings.
course_highlights: 6.7 km loop every hour on the hour
Course with approximately 50% asphalt and the rest trails and gravel for the first 9 loops
More technically challenging course with 100 metres of elevation gain per loop from loop 10 until the end of the race
additional: Two different courses are used: Course 1 (loops 1–9) is flatter, with 64 metres of elevation gain and approximately 50% asphalt, the rest trails and gravel. Course 2 (loop 10 onward) is more technically challenging, with 100 metres of elevation gain per loop. A fully equipped aid station at the start/finish offers basic nutrition and space for personal supplies. Headlamps are required for night loops. The event offers free parking and is easily accessible by train. Registration is coming soon, and places are limited. The venue is approximately 30 minutes south of Oslo.

name: 22. Ülemiste metsajooks
description: The 22nd Ülemiste Forest Run is an environmentally friendly 3 km trail run held around the Tallinn Water Treatment Plant. The race centre, start and finish are located at Järvevana tee 3. The run takes place on Saturday, 29 August 2026, starting at 11:50. Participants are provided with a marked route, sports drink and water at the finish, and medical assistance along the entire course. The event is open to all running enthusiasts and offers an enjoyable, active experience.

name: Tallinna Vee 54. jooks ümber Ülemiste järve
description: The 54th Tallinna Vesi Run Around Lake Ülemiste is a traditional running race taking place on 29 August 2026. The Run Around Lake Ülemiste is part of the Maru Lake Runs series, and this year’s race is the series’ final, fourth event. The marked course is 13.7 km long and starts and finishes at the Tallinn Water Treatment Plant at Järvevana tee 3. The event centre opens early in the morning, and race materials are distributed on site. Participants are provided with chip timing; the chip is attached to the back of the race bib.
