description: The Stadtwerke Lübeck Marathon on 18 October 2026 offers runners a varied choice of distances in the historic Hanseatic city of Lübeck. In addition to the classic marathon, the event includes a duo marathon, half marathon, relay and other shorter races suitable for all ages and ability levels. The course runs through the picturesque city and offers a sporting challenge with regional championship scoring. The event is approved by the German Athletics Association and emphasizes community and a passion for sport.
course_highlights: Marathon with Schleswig-Holstein state championship scoring
Duo marathon relay point in Travemünde on the Baltic Sea
Course through the historic Hanseatic city of Lübeck
additional: Free medal engraving is available for registrations by 31.01.2026, with name, distance and finish time. A preferred race number can be selected free of charge during the early registration phases, subject to availability. Relay event with 10 x 4.2 km. Handbike half marathon on the same course as the runners’ half marathon. Duo marathon relay point in Travemünde on the Baltic Sea. On-course refreshments include honey gels; Schleswig-Holstein state championship scoring. Registration by 30.09.2026. Various race number and medal options.

name: Berliner Morgenpost Great 10K
description: The Berliner Morgenpost Great 10K is Berlin’s fastest 10-km race, starting in front of Charlottenburg Palace. The course runs through Berlin Zoo and offers a unique running experience in the capital. In addition to the classic 10-kilometer course, there is also a 2 x 5 km relay and a 4.2 km short course from the zoo to Charlottenburg Palace. The event is suitable for all abilities and age groups and offers a large running festival for the whole family.

name: 19. Burger-Rolandlauf
description: The Burger Rolandlauf is a traditional race that normally takes place in Burg and is jointly organized by Rolandgymnasium Burg and LG Ihleläufer Burg. The course runs through the town along the Ihle, through the forest and past the Bismarckturm, finishing in the school courtyard. Alongside the sporting competition, participants can enjoy a varied supporting program with music, activities for children and refreshments. The 2026 event in Burg was cancelled due to a lack of permits; instead, a replacement event will take place in Tangerhütte City Park.

name: Frühstückslauf
description: The breakfast run in Wernigerode is a group run without timekeeping, leading from the market square up to Wernigerode Castle. The route is about 3 kilometers long, with an elevation gain of 100 meters. The run takes place as a group and is free of charge. A light snack is served afterward, making it a sociable event.

name: H/21 Halbmarathon
description: The H/21 Hannover Half Marathon is a new running event on the national events calendar, combining urban flair, modern beats and green sections of the course. The start and finish are in the heart of Hannover, and the route passes notable hotspots throughout the state capital. The event takes place in autumn and offers a special running experience in a vibrant urban setting. Join the prologue as Hannover begins a new chapter in running history.

name: Porta Volkslauf
organizer: SC Nammen / SC Porta Westfalica Nammen e.V.
description: The Porta Fun Run 2026 is a long-standing running event in Porta Westfalica and has been a fixture on the regional running calendar for more than three decades. The event attracts runners of all ages, from competitive athletes to those running for enjoyment. The route follows roads and field paths around the Nammen sports ground and through the Nammer Unterholz nature reserve, offering varied, flat sections with magnificent panoramic views of the Porta. The run is part of the Mühlenkreisserie and takes place at the local sports facility in Nammen. The warm atmosphere and sense of community make the day a special experience.

name: Sebastian Fredrich Gedenklauf (LM/LC/NLC)
description: The Sebastian Fredrich Memorial Run is a long-standing running event in Lubmin, organized by the triathlon and running group of HSG Uni Greifswald. The event offers a sporting challenge in a friendly, well-organized atmosphere, supported by many volunteers. The route passes through scenic sections and is suitable for both competitive runners and recreational athletes. The event is part of an active running and triathlon community in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania.

name: Storkower See Lauf
description: The Storkower See Run is a long-standing running event organized by Triathlonverein Fürstenwalde 1990 e.V. and approved by the Brandenburg Athletics Association. On October 11, 2026, runners of various age groups and ability levels can take part on courses of different lengths around Lake Storkow. The event offers a fair competitive atmosphere and is open to running enthusiasts of all ages. Online registration opens in January 2026, and participants are listed in an official start list.

name: Wendlandmarathon
description: The Wendlandmarathon Kolborn is a traditional road race in Lüchow, Lower Saxony, held since 1993. The event offers a wide range of distances, from the marathon and half marathon to short children’s races, appealing to both long-distance runners and families. The course is measured to AIMS/IAAF standards and has kilometre markers and aid stations. Practical facilities for participants include parking, showers, changing rooms and certificates, as well as finisher medals for children.

name: Dobromiejski Festiwal Biegów i Nordic Wa...
location: Swobodna, Gmina Dobre Miasto, Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship, Poland

name: Piwna Mila
description: The Beer Mile is a unique race over a flexible distance of 1,700 to 2,000 metres and the highlight of the third day of the Sun Festival in Wąsowo. Participants start by drinking one beer, and beer refreshment stations are placed along the course approximately every 500 metres. This sporting celebration brings together runners, spectators and families, offering a one-of-a-kind atmosphere and a special finisher’s medal.

name: XIV Biegi Przyjaźni
description: The Friendship Run is one of the events in the Kaszuby Biegają series, the largest running event in northern Poland. The race takes place in the picturesque area around Skrzeszewo, giving participants the chance to spend time actively and discover the charms of Kashubia. The running series attracts runners of different ages and skill levels, promoting a healthy lifestyle and bringing the local community together.

name: Dwumaraton Olęderski
location: Wąsowo, Kuślin, Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland

name: Bieg Październikowy
location: Łubianka, Toruń County, Kuyavian-Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland

name: Grand Prix CITY TRAIL
description: The CITY TRAIL Grand Prix is a nationwide series of 5 km cross-country races held in the beautiful woodland settings of city parks. In Poznań, the course loops around Lake Rusałka, starting on Św. Wawrzyńca Street and finishing at the city beach by the lake. The races are open to runners of all abilities, from beginners to advanced athletes, who can regularly check their results on the same course. Races take place throughout the 2026/2027 season, and participants can compete in both local and national rankings.
course_highlights: A 5 km course through woodland around Lake Rusałka
Start on Św. Wawrzyńca Street, finish at the city beach
Suitable for beginner and advanced runners
additional: The race office opens at 8:30 and closes at 10:30. A group warm-up with the CITY TRAIL Ambassadors takes place before the 10:45 start. The event also includes races for children in various age categories. The course remains the same throughout the season, allowing runners to compare results across months and years. The series also includes children’s races. The official calendar lists the dates for the 2026/2027 season but does not confirm a race in Poznań on 10 October 2027.

Rosa Sløyfe-løpet Kristiansand
organizer: Kreftforeningen og Brystkreftforeningen, i samarbeid med Springtime Group
price_range: Mini: gratis; kort og lang løype: 500 kr + administrasjonsgebyr

description: The Pink Ribbon Run in Kristiansand is an annual event held to support the breast cancer cause. The run starts and finishes at Aquarama in the city centre, and the course passes through beautiful areas around Kristiansand. Participants can choose between a short course of approximately 3.4 km or a long course of approximately 5.5 km. There is also a separate children’s race for children aged 3 to 9. All participants receive a race pack with a bib, neck warmer, bag and medal, and the event brings together thousands of people in a sea of pink for a good cause.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Aquarama in central Kristiansand
Short course of approx. 3.4 km without timing
Long course of approx. 5.5 km with timing
additional: The race pack includes a bib, neck warmer, bag and medal. The Mini children’s race is free and approximately 400 metres long, with activities in the start area. The short course is untimed, while the long course is timed. Race numbers can be collected in the start area from 2 hours before the start, or in advance to avoid queues. Participants in the short and long courses are insured through a licence with the Norwegian Athletics Association, which also supports the cause. Companies can register using separate registration forms and manage participants through My Page. The race pack contains a bib, neck warmer, bag and medal. NOK 250 of the race entry fee goes in full to the Pink Ribbon campaign.

name: Nummela BackYard Ultra
description: Nummela Backyard Ultra is an ultramarathon running event in which competitors run 6.706-kilometre laps within an hour, continuing for as long as multiple runners are able to keep going. The competition is unique because it has no predetermined finishing time or distance, and the winner is the one who runs one more lap than the others. The event is held at the Polku Hotel in Vihti and offers a challenge for runners who value perseverance and endurance. The competition originated in the United States and is also known as “Just one more Loop.”

name: Night Trail Run 30 km
description: Night Trail Run is a unique trail race in Sollentuna, focused on the experience of darkness and nature. The race offers several distances, including a challenging 30 km course where runners navigate using GPS and a map. The start and finish are at Väsby gård, and the course is marked with reflectors to create a magical atmosphere in the glow of headlamps. The race is open to runners aged 18 and over, with special rules for younger participants on the shorter distances.
course_highlights: Course marked with clear reflectors for a night-running experience
Navigation using GPS and a map on the 21 km and 30 km distances
Start and finish at Väsby gård in Sollentuna
additional: Flexible start time between 18:00 and 19:30 for the 5 km and 10 km. The 21 km and 30 km races start on Saturday, 17 October, at 16:45 and 16:00, respectively. Minimum age is 18, but participants aged 15–18 may run the 5 km and 10 km if accompanied by an adult. A proper headlamp is recommended, ideally with an extra lamp for the 30 km. The time limit for the 30 km is 4 hours and 30 minutes. Aid stations are available along the 21 km and 30 km courses. Previous organizer information states an age limit of 18 and a time limit of 4 hours and 30 minutes for the 30 km. Details for 2027 have not been confirmed in the available sources.

name: 53. Saaremaa kolme päeva jooks
description: The Saaremaa Three-Day Run is a traditional running event in Kuressaare, inviting all running enthusiasts to take part. The competition offers several distance options and age groups, with opportunities for both young people and adults. Registration takes place on site, and the entry fee is affordable, making the event accessible to a wide range of participants. The competition is part of a larger running series, which also includes season standings and an awards ceremony.

name: Vistakulle Backyard
description: Vistakulle Backyard is a running event in the Vistakulle area near Gränna, organised by Rudu Friskvård in collaboration with Bauer Activities. The race is aimed at people who are a little adventurous and interested in fitness, and places as much emphasis on the experience of nature as on performance. The event takes place on 16 May 2026 and offers a memorable course through hilly terrain close to nature.

pipeline_log.message: New race date found on official site (https://baueractivities.se/loppen/vistakulle-backyard/): 2026-10-17 — "17 Oktober 2026 07.00-19.00" (was estimated 2027-05-15)

name: Hellasloppet
description: Hellasloppet is a family-friendly running event offering a wonderful day at Hellasgården, close to the city. The races pass through the beautiful Hellas area, by lakes and hills, along lovely running trails and roads. There are races for all ages, from the very youngest children, who can run 100 metres without registering in advance, to children aged 5–8 on a flat course. The day offers the joy of running, uphill sections, music and a lovely autumn setting, with refreshments and activities for the whole family.
course_highlights: Races through the Hellas area, with lakes and hills
Lovely running trails and roads
Flat course for children aged 5–8
additional: The first race starts at 10:00, and the final start for the 10 km race is expected around 12:00. There is plenty of parking and bicycle parking by the start area. Prize ceremonies take place throughout the day. Athletics activities are available on site, with stations where you can try running, throwing and jumping. All children born in 2022 or later can run 100 m without registering in advance and will receive a medal. Refreshments are available throughout the day. The first race starts at 10:00, and the 10 km race is expected to start around 12:00. The 100-metre race for the youngest children does not require advance registration. Parking is available, and refreshments are served.

name: Växjö Marathon
description: Växjö Marathon is a fast, flat marathon course run over eight laps around the beautiful Växjösjön. The course is mostly paved, with a short section of fine gravel, and has very little elevation change—about 3 metres per lap. The event welcomes both experienced runners and beginners, and also offers relay races for teams. This is the 32nd edition of the race, which is known as Sweden’s fastest marathon course. The course is marked and has a lead cyclist and course marshals, but it is not closed to traffic during the race.
course_highlights: Eight laps around Växjösjön
Flat, fast course with about 3 m of elevation change per lap
Mostly paved, with about 300 metres of fine gravel
additional: The course is marked, with a lead cyclist and course marshals. It is not closed to traffic during the race. Relay races are also available for teams, and a children’s race is held. Sports drinks, dietary supplements, and energy and protein bars are available. The organizer is Växjö Löparklubb. The marathon relay has teams of four, with each runner completing two laps. The course is not closed to pedestrians, cyclists, or motor traffic. Sources do not confirm the details for the 2027 edition.

name: Åhus TrailRun
description: Åhus TrailRun is a challenging trail race through the coastal forests and along the sea south of Åhus in Skåne. Participants can choose from four distances: 2.5 km, 6 km, 11 km and 17 km, as well as an untimed children’s race. The courses feature gently rolling terrain with a mix of trails, sand dunes, hills and running on sand by the sea, providing a unique running experience. The race is part of Skåne Trailcup and also offers a team competition with great prizes. The event is open to everyone and has a friendly, welcoming atmosphere.
course_highlights: Gently rolling terrain with varied surfaces
A mix of trails, sand dunes and challenging hills
Running on sand along the sea
additional: Participant limit: 1,000. The children’s race is approximately 350 m long, has individual starts and is free to enter. Start times: 2.5 km and 6 km start at 12:30, 11 km and 17 km start at 12:40, and the children’s race has individual starts between 13:00 and 15:00. The time limit for the 17 km race is 2 hours and 50 minutes. Parking is limited; follow the instructions of event staff. Valuables storage is available for a fee of 20 SEK. Toilets are 200 metres from the event venue. The venue at Strandridaregården is approximately 100 metres from the sea. The children’s race is approximately 350 metres and is untimed. Prices are reported for the 2026 edition.

name: Jönköping 10K/5K
description: Jönköping 10K/5K is a race for everyone, from elite runners to recreational runners, offering a completely flat and fast course in central Jönköping, starting at Lillsjöplan. The course has been officially measured by the Swedish Athletics Association and is eligible for seeding at many races in Sweden and internationally. The race offers a great atmosphere, pacers for different finishing times, and the opportunity to take part in team competitions with friends. It’s a perfect chance to set a personal best or simply enjoy a pleasant run with colleagues or friends.
course_highlights: A completely flat and fast course in central Jönköping
The 5K runs one lap; the 10K runs two laps
A water station with UMARA sports drink along the course
additional: Pacers carrying flags for 40-, 45- and 50-minute times in the 10K. Team competition with a 10% discount when registering with two friends. Warm-up with Fitness24Seven at 10:40 in the start/finish area. Limited bag drop in the start area in the morning. Parking is available in nearby parking garages for a fee. Register three people as a team for a 10% discount on the entry fee and a chance to win prizes. Up to five runners can be registered at the same time.

name: Night Trail Run (Sollentuna) — Hundtrail / 5 km & 10 km
description: Night Trail Run Hundtrail is a unique evening race in Sollentuna where you can run with your dog over 5 or 10 kilometres. The courses are marked with reflectors, and headlamps are mandatory to create a magical nighttime experience. The race is open to runners aged 18 and over, but young people aged 15 to 18 may participate if accompanied by an adult. It is an unforgettable evening enjoyed by both two- and four-legged participants.
course_highlights: The courses are marked with reflectors
Flexible start time between 18:00 and 19:30 (until 19:00 for 10 km)
Headlamps are mandatory, and dogs must be kept on a leash
additional: A maximum of one dog per runner. Age limit: 18; participants aged 15–18 may take part accompanied by an adult. Dogs must be kept on a leash and be comfortable around other dogs and people. The race takes place in the dark, with narrow passages and frequent encounters with other dogs, so reactive dogs are not recommended. One dog per runner; dogs must be kept on a leash. Flexible start times: 18:00–19:30 for 5 km and 18:00–19:00 for 10 km. Age limit: 18; young people aged 15 and over may participate with a responsible adult.

name: Stockholms Brantaste

tiers.label: tier_1

description: Stockholms Brantaste is an intense, high-energy race that challenges you to run both up and down the steep slopes of Hammarbybacken. The course is just over 3 km long and includes three climbs, taking you up two different ski slopes. The race is suitable for both experienced runners and beginners who want to test their lactate threshold and mental toughness. The finish is at the top of Hammarbybacken, with a fantastic view of Stockholm as the backdrop.
course_highlights: Just over 3 km with three climbs
Uphill on two different ski slopes
Finish at the top of Hammarbybacken with views over Stockholm
additional: Race bib collection takes place at the Hammarby Fabriksväg event area from 09:30 on race day. The race bib is personal and must be worn on the chest with safety pins. There are water stations along the course. In the relay, teams complete 8 laps of approximately 1 km each, with 2–4 people per team. Children’s races are available for ages 7–12 (approximately 500 m) and ages 0–6 (approximately 300 m; registration via Skistar). The event area is easily accessible by public transport; parking is limited. The 2026 edition is listed as taking place on October 17; information about the 2027 race has not yet been confirmed in the available sources. The relay covers approximately 8 km for teams of 2–4 people. Brantaste Mini is approximately 500 metres for children aged 7–12, and Valles Kompislopp is approximately 300 metres for children aged 0–6. The start and finish are at Hammarbybacken; the organiser recommends public transport because there is no parking at the slope.

name: Rönninge Backyard Run 2026

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Anmälan sker på plats och kostar 75 kr

description: Rönninge Backyard Run 2026 is a unique running event celebrating its 5th anniversary. The race consists of a 6,706-metre loop starting at Bubblan in Toredal and running on asphalt and gravel. Participants run as many loops as they can manage over twelve hours, with a start every hour on the hour from 09:00 to 20:00. To continue, runners must complete each loop in under an hour, and the most enduring runner who is fastest on the final loop wins. There are women’s and men’s categories, as well as a MiniBackyard for children and young people who want to run shorter distances.
course_highlights: The loop is 6,706 metres long, with approximately 80% asphalt and 20% gravel
The course includes several longer climbs, including towards Sandbäcksvägen and the promenade
Start and finish at Bubblan in Toredal, with a final flat asphalt stretch leading to the grass field
additional: The race starts every hour on the hour from 09:00 to 20:00, with up to 12 loops over twelve hours. Runners must complete each loop in under an hour to continue. MiniBackyard starts at 14:00 and lasts for a maximum of 45 minutes. Registration for MiniBackyard takes place on site. Coffee and refreshments are served at 20:00 after the final loop. The first start is at 09:00 and the last start is at 20:00. There is also a MiniBackyard with a loop of at least 670 metres; on-site registration costs 75 kr.

name: Ivar Formos Minneløp 2027
description: Ivar Formos Minneløp is a traditional cross-country race in Oslo, offering scenic and challenging courses in Nordmarka. The race has distances for both children and adults, including a tough 17 km course that follows the terrain where Ivar Formo trained to become an Olympic champion. The start and finish are at Sognsvann Snøpark, and the courses feature beautiful trails, panoramic views of the city, and several aid stations along the way. The event is a sweaty pleasure for everyone who enjoys running in the forest, with a new 10 km course that is undulating and challenging without steep climbs or descents.
course_highlights: 17 km course starting and finishing at Sognsvann Snøpark, with panoramic views of Oslo from Vettakollen and Frønsvollen
The course passes well-known places such as Båntjern, Skjennungstua, Ullevålseter, and Lynhytta, with aid stations
New 10 km course on beautiful forest trails, with challenging, undulating terrain and no steep hills
additional: Start and finish at Sognsvann Snøpark. Timing chip included in the race bib, except for the children's race, which is untimed. Late registration is available on race day via the EQ Timing app. Registration is binding, with no refunds in case of illness or injury. Race bibs can be resold via EQ Timing. No T-shirts will be sold in 2027 due to low interest. In 2027, the race will be held for the 15th time. Late registration is available on race day via the EQ Timing app. The timing chip is included in the race bib, and the children's race is untimed. Registration is binding, and a one-off licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation is required if you do not have an annual licence.

name: Volda Bakgårdsultra 2027
description: Volda Bakgårdsultra is a social and inclusive ultramarathon based on the backyard ultra concept, where participants run 12 laps of 6.7 km, with a new start every hour on the hour. The race starts in the SpareBank 1 Hall at Volda Stadium and is suitable for all levels, from those who want to complete one lap to those aiming to finish the classic ultra distance of 50 miles (80.4 km). The event has been a success since 2025 and offers a unique running experience focused on community and personal challenge. Between laps, participants can rest in the hall, with access to a drop bag area and kiosk. Registration for 2027 opens on 16 January at 20:00 via EQ Timing.
course_highlights: 12 laps of 6.7 km, with a start every hour on the hour
The course is mostly gravel road with little elevation gain
Start and finish in the SpareBank 1 Hall, with access to a rest area and drop bag area
additional: The race has a basic aid station with water, sports drinks, fruit and salty snacks. Participants can also bring their own food and drinks and set up personal drop bags by the start/finish area. Free parking is available at Volda Stadium, and Volda town centre is within walking distance of the venue. Volda Airport Hovden is a 10-minute drive away. The hall has a kiosk selling coffee, soft drinks, chocolate and other light refreshments. Participants must have a valid licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation or purchase a one-day licence when registering. The provisional date is 16 October 2027, with a start at 08:00. Registration has not opened yet; the final date and registration information are to be confirmed in January 2027.

name: Furumomila 2027
description: Furumomila is a traditional cross-country race held for the 44th time at Furumo Idrettspark. The event offers several distances, including a 10 km cross-country race, MiniMil, a recreational walk and SpareBank1 Modum’s cross-country race. Participants can look forward to generous cash prizes, gift cards, medals and pins. This autumn adventure welcomes both recreational runners and competitive athletes.
course_highlights: 10 km cross-country race over varied terrain
Several distances: 10 km, 5 km, 1.5 km, MiniMil and a recreational walk
Start and finish at Furumo Idrettspark
additional: Race numbers can be collected in the tent by the clubhouse before the start. Showers and changing rooms are available. Parking and a shuttle bus are provided. Prizes are awarded shortly after the finish for the various distances. A one-time licence is required for those without an annual licence, in accordance with the rules of the Norwegian Athletics Federation. Previous editions have distributed race numbers by the clubhouse. Distances and practical information for 2027 have not been confirmed.

name: Hytteplanmila
description: Hytteplanmila is an annual fun run held at Svensrudmoen in October. The race features a fast, gently undulating 10-kilometre course, known as one of Norway’s fastest 10K road race routes. Participants can experience a varied course with both easy and challenging sections, including a demanding finish on Pulsbakken. The event attracts both recreational runners and elite athletes, with separate start groups for the elite field.
course_highlights: Fast, gently undulating 10-kilometre course
The race’s challenging finish on Pulsbakken
Great views over Steinssletta and historic sites such as Mo gård
additional: Registration opens in November. Entry fees are non-refundable and cannot be transferred. Those who register by the deadlines receive a buff and running socks, distributed on race day. It is possible to pre-order a race pack with energy products. Elite athletes can register by email for separate start groups. Buses to the race are arranged from Oslo and Gardermoen. The time limit is 1 hour and 40 minutes. Registration for 2027 opens in November; information about the entry fee has not yet been published.

name: Saaremaa Kolme Päeva Jooks
description: Saaremaa Three-Day Run is a traditional running competition held in the village of Iide. The competition consists of three stages, where participants can enjoy Saaremaa’s beautiful nature and varied terrain. The competition is open to different age groups and offers a friendly, supportive atmosphere for all running enthusiasts. Participants are provided with electronic timing, reusable race bibs and drinking cups, and a sweet treat and a drink after the run.

name: Bėgimas Graužikai-Kelmė
description: The Graužikai–Kelmė Run is a traditional race in Kelmė District held in memory of Vaidotas Rimkus. The event takes place in October and aims to promote running and athletics in Lithuania, encourage a healthy lifestyle, and increase physical activity among local residents. It attracts runners of all ages, who can choose from several distances, including the 8 km main race. Participants are awarded cups, medals, and commemorative prizes.

name: TeutoMarsch
location: Grundschule Hohne, Lengerich-Hohne, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany
description: The Teutomarsch is a unique hiking and running experience through the Teutoburg Forest and surrounding area. Organized by Turnverein Hohne von 1911 e.V. in Lengerich, the Teutomarsch offers two routes designed to delight participants. The event is very popular, and starting places fill up quickly. The exact route is still being finalized, but promises to be a fantastic and unique course. Participants must be at least 16 years old, and dogs are allowed on a leash.
course_highlights: A unique route through the Teutoburg Forest and surrounding area
Two different routes for a special experience
A nature experience in the Lengerich-Hohne region
additional: Registration for the 2026 Teutomarsch sold out within 30 minutes, with 500 starting places. There is a waiting list. Participants consent to being photographed and filmed and to the publication of the resulting images and footage. Entry fees are non-refundable. Minimum age: 16. Dogs are allowed on a leash. The organizer accepts no liability for personal injury, property damage, or loss or theft. Trail running, no timekeeping, refreshment stations along the route, start and finish at Grundschule Hohne, participant limit: 500.

name: Prignitzer Moormeile
description: The Prignitzer Moormeile in Bad Wilsnack is a traditional race taking place for the 26th time on October 17, 2026. The event offers various distances from 1 km to 12.4 km, running through the Wilsnack forests, the Kurpark, and around the Karthanehalle. The races are suitable for children, young people, and adults, and are part of the Prignitz Cup and the Brandenburg Cup. The event is known for its family-friendly atmosphere, good on-course refreshments, and professional timing.

name: Coconaut Pomerania ULTRA Trail
description: Coconaut Pomerania ULTRA Trail is a trail running series held on the hilly trails of Pomerania and Kashubia, with the event base at KJ Barłomino. The event offers five distances: 100 km, 65 km, 42 km, 21 km and 11 km, providing a range of challenges for trail runners. The race showcases the beauty of the Kashubian landscape and regional attractions, and participants can look forward to excellent aid stations along the route. The event is supported by the #AktywnaWieś program and organized by the Pomerania Sports Association.

35 Orla Pięść

name: Täby Halvmarathon
description: Täby Half Marathon is a fast, easy-to-run half marathon in scenic surroundings, starting and finishing at Näsby Castle. The course offers coastal views along the shores of Värtan, a scenic loop around Lake Rönninge, and a finish back by the sea with views towards Bogesundlandet. The course is officially measured and the race is organized by Täby IS Friidrott. It is ideal for runners looking to end the season on a fast and beautiful course. The race has been very popular in previous years, with limited places, so the organizers encourage early registration.

name: Täljemilen
description: Enhörna IF presents Täljemilen—perhaps autumn’s fastest officially measured 10K, at Geneta Sportfält in Södertälje. The course runs entirely on cycle paths and footpaths and is fully paved, making it very fast and suitable for those chasing a personal best. Water is available at 5 km and at the finish. Instead of medals, the organizer donates a sum to the Swedish Childhood Cancer Fund for every registered runner. Prizes are awarded to the top 3 in both the women’s and men’s categories, and there is also a draw for approximately 20 prizes.

name: Skövdeloppet
description: Skövdeloppet makes a comeback in 2026 with a new, city-adjacent course that mainly follows walking and cycling paths through several of Skövde’s residential areas. Race day is October 18, and the races are designed as easy-to-run urban courses suitable for both recreational and competitive runners. Three distances are offered (21.1 km, 10 km and 5 km), with a shared start and finish at Lillegårdens Fritidsområde.

name: Gjesdal Trailrun
location: Gjesdal IL athletics facility, Solås, Ålgård, Gjesdal, Norway

description: Gjesdal Trailrun is a true trail race held in beautiful natural surroundings in Ålgård, starting from Gjesdal IL’s athletics facility at Solås. The race mainly follows trails in the terrain northeast of the facility, climbing Kodlifjellet and Håfjellet. It suits both those looking for an enjoyable mountain hike and those who want to compete. Three distances are offered: 10 km, 6 km, and a 1.3 km children’s race. The course follows regular hiking trails that can be challenging, with rocky and slippery sections, so good trail shoes are recommended.
course_highlights: Trail race on paths in the terrain northeast of Gjesdal IL’s athletics facility
The main course climbs Kodlifjellet and Håfjellet
Challenging sections with rocks and slippery areas
additional: Race bib collection opens at 10:00 at the Gjesdal IL clubhouse. The children’s race starts at 11:30. Both timed and untimed starts are available for the 6 km and 10 km distances. The 10 km has a time limit, with participants required to pass Kodlifjellet within approximately 35 minutes and the junction between the 6 km and 10 km courses within 40 minutes. The online registration fee of NOK 20, plus any NFIF one-time licence, is additional. Previous editions have featured 10 km, 6 km, and a 1 km children’s race. Good trail shoes with good grip are recommended. The 2027 distances have not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Neskollen Frontyard 2027

description: Neskollen Frontyard 2027 is a unique race organized by Hvam IL, where participants run 3 km laps that must be completed faster and faster. The race combines competition with a family-friendly, social atmosphere, with indoor breaks at Nes Arena where snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza are served, included in the price. Frontyard challenges both running capacity and tactics, and prizes are awarded to the best woman, the best man, and the fastest overall time after 15 laps. The start and finish are at Nes Arena, with convenient facilities such as toilets and parking right outside.
course_highlights: 3 km laps that must be run faster with each lap
Start and finish at Nes Arena, with indoor breaks
The course consists of approximately 700 meters of gravel, with the rest on asphalt
additional: Snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza are included in the price. The start, finish, and breaks are indoors at Nes Arena, with 12 toilets and parking right outside. The course consists of approximately 700 meters of gravel, with the rest on asphalt. Remember to wear your race bib visibly on the outside of your clothing. The children's race starts at approximately 10:01. Previous editions have served snacks, drinks, fruit, and pizza during breaks at Nes Arena.

name: Krusensterni jooks
description: The Krusenstern Run is a traditional running race that starts at the Purila bus stop and finishes at Hagudi Manor. The race is 4.2 km long and is suitable for schoolchildren, pensioners and adults. The top men and women are awarded prizes, with special prizes also awarded to veteran athletes, the youngest and oldest finishers, and the largest family. Participants take part at their own risk, and all finishers are offered water, a treat and hot tea.

name: Botanic Five Kaunas
location: Botanical Garden of Vytautas Magnus University, Kaunas, Lithuania

name: Oldenburg Marathon
price_range: 35 Euro für Sportshirt (genaue Startgebühr nicht spezifiziert)
description: The Oldenburg Marathon on October 25, 2026, offers runners a varied programme featuring a marathon, half marathon, half-marathon relay, 10 km city run, 5 km run and children’s mile run. The course goes through Oldenburg and Wardenburg and is known for its good refreshments and friendly atmosphere. The event welcomes runners of all abilities and also offers a public race series with additional competitions during the year. Participants receive high-quality long-sleeved shirts, and extensive services are available on site.
course_highlights: Refreshment stations every 5 km on courses of 10 km or longer, with water, sports drinks and fruit
Showers in the sports hall at Graf Anton Günther School, approximately 300 m from the start/finish area
Changing facilities and baggage drop-off on Level 1 of the Schlosshöfe car park
additional: Race packs will be handed out on October 11 from 11 a.m. at the Schlosshöfe. On race day, collection opens at 7 a.m. for marathon runners and at 8 a.m. for everyone else. Group registration is available. After the race, extensive refreshments will be provided, including drinks, fruit, coffee, tea, pastries and non-alcoholic wheat beer. Physiotherapy students will offer free massages. Portable toilets and changing facilities are available. Multiple race distances, start in Wardenburg, road closures in the city centre, finisher medals, online registration available

name: 20. Müggelsee-Halbmarathon
description: The Müggelsee Half Marathon is a scenic race in southeast Berlin that runs entirely around the Großer Müggelsee. The event offers three distances: a half marathon, 10 kilometers, and 5 kilometers, each laid out as either an out-and-back route or a loop. The course passes through the historic Spreetunnel and offers idyllic views of Berlin’s largest lake and the surrounding Müggelberge. The race is suitable for all runners, whether they are aiming for personal bests or simply want to enjoy the community and nature. The start and finish are at Müggelseeperle, and the race takes place on October 18, 2026.

name: 52.Maraton Dębno 2026
organizer: Ośrodek Sportu i Rekreacji w Dębnie
description: The 52nd Dębno Marathon is the oldest and one of the fastest marathons in Poland, taking place on October 18, 2026. The 42.195 km course, certified by the Polish Athletic Association (PZLA), runs through the streets of Dębno and the surrounding area, making it ideal for personal bests. The event has a rich tradition dating back to 1966 and attracts both amateur and professional runners from Poland and abroad. Participants can expect professional organization, numerous refreshment stations, and enthusiastic support from spectators. The marathon is also an opportunity for the running community to come together and a celebration of sport for the whole family.

name: XVII Półmaraton Ziemi Puckiej
description: The 17th Puck Land Half Marathon is a well-known running event in Pomerania, returning in 2026 in a new edition under the STONE TRI & RUN banner. The event takes place on a refreshed course in an autumn setting, making it an ideal way to wrap up the running season. It features a half marathon, a 5 km race, and a 5 km Nordic walking event, all with individual starts. It’s a great opportunity to enjoy the beautiful Kashubian countryside and experience the sporting atmosphere of the Puck Running Triad.

name: 40. Bieg Barbórkowy o Lampkę Górniczą – Sztafeta Międzyzakładowa
Necon Vinterkarusell 27-28 løp 1 (18. okt)
description: Necon Winter Series is a winter running series consisting of 8 races held at Fana Stadium in Bergen from November to April. The races have a mass start and offer two distances, 5 km and 10 km. Participants can choose their distance during the race at the turnaround point. The start and finish are at Fana Stadium, and the races follow varied terrain, with intermediate times available along the way. The series is suitable for both recreational and experienced runners looking for a social and challenging winter series.
course_highlights: Mass start for the 5 km and 10 km, with the option to choose a distance during the race
The course starts at Fana Stadium, with turnarounds at Sandsli and Plantasjen in Kokstad
Intermediate times are recorded at 2.5 km, 5 km and 7.5 km for the different distances
additional: Start and finish at Fana Stadium from 18:45. Start waves are based on expected finish times to avoid crossing Grimseidvegen. Wave 0 starts at 18:45 for 10 km runners expecting to finish in over 55 min. Wave 1 starts at 19:00 for 5 km runners expecting to finish in under 22:30 min and 10 km runners expecting to finish in under 45 min. Waves 2–4 start at 2-minute intervals, based on expected finish times. Participants register for the 5 km when signing up; the distance is chosen automatically during the race at the turnaround point.

name: Pukinmaki Run Helsinki 18.10.2026
description: Pukinmäki Run is an annual running event held in the Pukinmäki district of Helsinki, offering distances of 1 km for children, 5 km, 10 km and a half marathon. The course is flat and fast, mainly on asphalt and outdoor trails, and loops around the boundaries of Pukinmäki. The event is open to runners of all ages and abilities, offering a chance to enjoy exercise and beautiful nature together with others. The event hub is located at Pukinmäki Sports Park, and refreshments and snacks are available.

name: Emili jookseb
description: Emili Runs is a cheerful school community running event held in Kadriorg Park in autumn, with students, teachers and parents taking part. The focus is on the joy of movement and supporting one another, not on speed. This traditional event fosters a sense of togetherness and offers the community enjoyable moments of exercise in the fresh air. The first run took place amid golden leaves and was an inspiring start to the school holiday.

name: Älvsjöloppet night trail
location: Gamla Älvsjö IP, Älvsjö, Stockholm, Sweden
price_range: 250 kr; gratis för medlemmar i OK Älvsjö-Örby
description: Älvsjöloppet Night Trail is an exciting 5 km evening race through hilly terrain in Älvsjöskogen, with 150 metres of elevation gain. The start and finish are at Gamla Älvsjö IP, about a 15-minute walk from Älvsjö station. The course is marked with reflective markers and requires a bright headlamp, preferably at least 1,000 lumens, as well as good trail shoes to handle the terrain. After the finish, all runners are offered a sausage and a drink in a friendly atmosphere. The race is organised by OK Älvsjö Örby and is open to everyone, with free entry for club members.
course_highlights: 5 km reflective-marked course through hilly terrain, with 150 m of elevation gain
Start and finish at Gamla Älvsjö IP, near Älvsjö station
Requires a bright headlamp and trail shoes with good grip
additional: Race bibs and timing chips are handed out from 18.15 to 18.45. The chip must be returned at the finish. Toilets and changing rooms are available at the venue. Parking is available in the area and at Herr Stens väg 2, but walking, cycling or running to the start is recommended. Live results and the results list are available at alvsjoloppet.se. Sausages and drinks are offered to all runners after the finish; no other refreshments are available. The start and finish are at Gamla Älvsjö IP. The organiser's published information applies to 2026 and does not give confirmed details for 2027. For 2026, a headlamp of at least 1,000 lumens and trail shoes, preferably with metal studs, are recommended.

name: Ambla SK SV suusatajate seeriajooks+kepikõnd
description: Ambla SK SV Skiers’ Series Run + Nordic Walking is a multi-stage running and Nordic walking series held at Kangrumägi in Järva County. The competition consists of five stages: the first four are time trials, and the final stage is a mass-start run. The results of the best four stages count toward the series standings, and prizes are awarded by age group. The competition is intended for runners using ski poles, which can be borrowed if needed. Special prizes are awarded to those who complete the series.
course_highlights: Five stages: the first four are time trials, and the final stage is a mass-start run
Held at Kangrumägi in Järva County
Only runners using ski poles are included in the competition standings
additional: Only runners using ski poles are included in the competition standings. Ski poles can be borrowed if needed. Every runner or Nordic walker who completes all five stages receives a special prize. Age groups range from age 6 to 55+. Points are awarded as follows: 1st place 30 points, 2nd place 27 points, 3rd place 25 points, and so on. In the event of a tie, the placing in the final stage decides. The fifth stage is scheduled for 8 November 2026, starting at 12:00. The best four stage results count toward the series standings.

name: 3. Holstre-Polli ööjooks
location: Holstre-Polli Sports Centre, Holstre, Viljandi County, Estonia
description: The 3rd Holstre-Polli Night Run takes place on the health and ski trails of Holstre-Polli Sports Centre in Viljandi County. This night run gives participants the chance to experience the wilderness and tranquillity surrounding the sports centre. The event is part of Holstre-Polli Sports Centre’s sports event series and is suitable for both experienced runners and recreational runners. Participants can enjoy a unique night-running experience amid beautiful nature.

name: Yxbacken Extreme Challenge by E2C
description: Yxbacken Extreme Challenge by E2C is one of Östergötland’s most unique and challenging running races, held at the foot of Pernilla Wiberg’s home slope in Yxbacken, Norrköping. The race challenges participants with five laps up a hill with 100 metres of elevation gain over 350 metres, for a total distance of approximately 7 kilometres. Whether you run fast or take it easy, everyone is welcome to take part, and the most important thing is to make it to the top. New this year is also a relay, adding an extra dimension to the race. Children can take part for free in the Lilla Yxbackenloppet by E2C, making it a family-friendly running festival.
course_highlights: Five laps up Yxbacken, with 100 metres of elevation gain over 350 metres per lap
Approximately 7 kilometres in a unique race setting in Östergötland
Start at the foot of Pernilla Wiberg’s home slope
additional: Race bibs can be collected at XXL on Friday 23 October from 14:00 to 18:00, or at the start and finish area no later than one hour before the start. The bib includes a timing chip, which must be used to record your time. All participants who cross the finish line receive a medal sponsored by Energi & Inneklimat. Companies can rent a partner tent at the race venue for team spirit and exposure through Rent a Tent. E2C was title partner for the fourth year in the 2024 edition.

name: VSM terräng

late_fee.price: 530 kr för seniorer och veteraner, 430 kr för juniorer och ungdomar

description: The Swedish Cross Country Championships are organised by Västerås FK and the Swedish Athletics Federation at Rocklunda IP in Västerås. The course is 2 km long and consists mostly of grass, with some other surfaces, including fast-running grass and gravel paths. The competition includes several categories, including seniors, youth, masters and para-athletes, with individual races and team competitions. The event also offers the option of pre-booked lunch and good accommodation options close to the venue.
course_highlights: 2 km course consisting mostly of grass, with some other surfaces
Fast-running grass and a 2–3-metre-wide gravel path, crossed four times per lap
Hay-bale obstacles on parts of the course
additional: Race numbers must be collected at the start/finish area at least 60 minutes before the start. Access to the start area opens 10 minutes before the start and closes 2 minutes before. Water is available at the lap point and finish, with Dextrosol at the finish. Changing rooms and showers are available at Expandia Arena. Free parking and local buses are available. Clubs may set up their own tents in the designated area. Pre-booked lunch is served at Good Morning Hotels near the venue. Doping tests may be conducted during the competition weekend. The 2026 event took place at Rocklunda IP in Västerås. The organiser’s website states that Västerås FK handed over hosting duties for the 2027 Swedish Cross Country Championships to Mora.

name: Linghem Dark Halfyard (Ultra) Trail
description: Welcome to the second edition of Linghem Dark Halfyard (Ultra) Trail, a unique and exciting running event in the autumn darkness of Kråksångsskogen. The race consists of 13 laps on a 3.5 km loop, with a maximum of 30 minutes allowed for each lap. After the sixth lap, runners change direction, adding an extra dimension to the competition. This is a small-scale race with a limited number of places, and a headlamp is mandatory because almost the entire race takes place in the dark. All participants who complete at least one lap receive a beautiful wooden medal, and the winners receive unique winner’s medals.
course_highlights: 13 laps on a 3.5 km loop, with a maximum of 30 minutes per lap
Running direction changes after the sixth lap
The course is marked with reflective markers and trail tape; the surface is mostly trails, with approximately 700 metres of gravel
additional: Energy is served during laps 7 and 8 (pizza from a local pizzeria), along with sweets, bananas, crisps, coffee, hot broth, sports drink and water. Facilities are very limited, with self-service energy, a warm fire and approximately 25 sq m of covered shelter. Toilets are outdoors in the forest. Maximum 70 places. Each lap starts every 30 minutes, and anyone who completes a lap faster can rest for the remaining time before the next lap starts. A headlamp and mobile phone are listed as mandatory equipment. The race website lists 70 places.

name: Halloween Night Trail
location: Friluftscentrum Karlsnäs, Ronneby, Blekinge County, Sweden
description: Halloween Night Trail is an exciting trail race in the dark in the Karlsnäs area north of Ronneby, with distances of 2 km, 5 km and 10 km. The race offers a unique Halloween atmosphere, with themed features such as Zombie Hill, Count Dracula’s lair and the Bat Cave along the course. The venue is at Friluftscentrum Karlsnäs, where the finish is indoors. After the race, grilled hamburgers and drinks are served and included in the entry fee. The race is organised by Ronneby Orienteering Club, which has extensive experience organising major orienteering competitions.
course_highlights: Run along small trails and through terrain, with reflectors showing the way in the dark
Themed features such as Zombie Hill, the Cemetery, Count Dracula’s lair and the Bat Cave
The finish area is indoors at Karlsnäs outdoor recreation centre
additional: Electronic timing for 5 km and 10 km; no timing for 2 km. Race bibs and timing chips can be collected from 17:00 at the venue. Freshly grilled hamburgers and drinks are served after the race and are included in the entry fee. The prize-giving is provisionally scheduled for 20:45. Shoes with good grip and a headlamp are recommended. Parents may run with children in the 2 km race without registering. A specially designed medal is given to all participants. The entry fee includes a hamburger and a drink. Electronic timing is available for the 5 km and 10 km distances, but not the 2 km. The finish area is indoors.

description: Rosa Sløyfe-løpet Oslo is an annual race held in support of the Pink Ribbon campaign. On Saturday, the event offers a short untimed course from Nedre Foss gård to Nydalen. On Sunday, participants can choose between timed 5 km and 10 km races, starting and finishing at Rådhusplassen. The course passes through some of Oslo’s most iconic areas, including Aker Brygge, Tjuvholmen and Akershus Fortress, offering an urban and atmospheric experience. The event is for everyone, whether you want to race for a time, run with colleagues or simply be part of the sea of pink.
course_highlights: Course through Aker Brygge, Tjuvholmen and Akershus Fortress
Start and finish at Rådhusplassen in central Oslo
Urban, atmospheric course with beautiful views
additional: Saturday’s short course is untimed and suitable for anyone looking for a more relaxed experience. The race packet includes a race bib, neck warmer, bag and medal. Pacers will be available for Sunday’s 5 km and 10 km races at different paces to help participants maintain a steady speed. Race bibs can be collected in advance or from two hours before the start on race day. Participants are insured through a licence provided by the Norwegian Athletics Federation, and half of the entry fee goes directly to the Pink Ribbon campaign. Timing is available for the 5 km and 10 km. The free Mini Run, approximately 400 metres, is for children aged 3 to 9. The participant package includes a race bib, neck warmer, bag and medal.

description: Bergen Marathon will be held for the 40th time on Saturday, October 23, 2027, with the start and finish at Fana Stadium in Bergen. The race is part of Maratonkarusellen, which offers both full and half marathons, and aims to ensure that all participants enjoy themselves despite the challenges of the race. Maratonkarusellen works with BFG Bergen Running Club and places great emphasis on the quality of its events. The minimum age for the marathon is 18.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Fana Stadium
Events include both full and half marathons
Organized in collaboration with BFG Bergen Running Club
additional: Kondis members receive a NOK 50 discount. A year-round license from the Norwegian Athletics Federation can be provided to avoid the one-time license fee. Participants without a license must purchase a one-time license. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. The event offers a half marathon and a marathon. The minimum age for the marathon is 18. Listed prices apply to the 2026 edition and may change before the 2027 race.

tiers.label: tier_1

description: Backyard Sandefjord is a unique ultrarun being held for the 14th time in 2027. The race consists of a gently rolling loop of approximately 6.7 km, run on the hour every hour, with a maximum of 12 loops in total. Participants must start each loop to continue, and the last runner to start the final loop is declared the winner. The event has a social atmosphere and a low barrier to entry, with facilities including snacks, hot drinks and places to rest in the hall. Everyone who completes 12 loops receives a cup, and those who reach the ultradistance receive a Norwegian-made wooden medal.
course_highlights: Gently rolling loop of approx. 6.7 km
The course is marked with yellow arrow signs, red marker flags and white arrows on asphalt
Maximum of 12 loops, totalling 80.4 km if completed
additional: Bringing your own cup, headlamp and reflective vest is mandatory. Bib collection is Friday 17:00–18:30 and Saturday 08:30–09:30. Support is allowed outdoors only. Snacks, coffee, sweet tea, broth, cold/hot water and hot dogs are offered after the 7th loop. Participants must bring their own chair; there is no room for sun loungers. Enter through the large gate at the back of the hall; parking is available. Start and finish at Runarhallen, Klavenesveien 20. Maximum 350 participants. Bringing your own cup, headlamp and reflective vest is mandatory. Snacks, coffee, sweet tea, broth and water are offered.

name: Fredrikstad Multiconsult Maraton 2027
description: The Fredrikstad Multiconsult Marathon takes place in Fredrikstad and consists of three identical 14 km laps, followed by an extra 195-metre finishing section so that the kilometre markers are in the same place on each lap. The course starts and finishes at FIF-huset and includes asphalt, gravel and forest roads in Fredrikstadmarka. There are aid stations along the route with water, squash and sports drink, as well as cola and bananas on the final laps. The race has been held since 2001 and offers a varied, scenic course with marshals at important intersections.
course_highlights: The course consists of three 14 km laps, plus an extra 195 metres to ensure the kilometre markers are in the same place on each lap
The first half is on asphalt; the rest is on gravel and forest roads in Fredrikstadmarka
Three aid stations per lap with a range of drinks and food
additional: An early start at 10:00 is available for runners who expect to take more than 5 hours. The race office and bib collection open at 09:00 on race day at FIF-huset. Parking is at Stjernehallen, about a 5-minute walk from the start/finish. Changing rooms and toilets are available at FIF-huset. There are no pacers during the race. Online registration is open until 1 hour before the start. There are three aid stations per lap. The race office, changing rooms and toilets are at FIF-huset; parking is at Stjernehallen.

description: Snipsøyrvatnet Rundt is one of Sunnmøre’s most traditional recreational races, organised by Hareid IL. The race goes around Snipsøyrvatnet, starting at Ward1 in Bjåstad, and marks the beginning of the autumn season. Participants register at Hareid Clubhouse before the race and can warm up with a 3 km jog to the start area. The race is open to both seniors and juniors, with a friendly and inclusive atmosphere.
course_highlights: The race goes around Snipsøyrvatnet
Start and finish at Ward1 in Bjåstad
A 3 km warm-up jog from registration to the start
additional: Registration takes place at Hareid Clubhouse from 12:00 to 13:45. Participants must make their own way from registration to the start area, either with a 3 km warm-up jog or by car. Changing facilities are available at Hareid Clubhouse. A one-time licence from the Norwegian Athletics Federation is an additional cost for those without an annual licence for road running. Parking is available at Ward1, Bigset Bedehus or Kulturoasen. Start time is 14:00; participants must make their own way approximately 3 km from registration to the start.
