name: Yddingeloppet
description: Yddingeloppet is one of Skåne’s largest cross-country races, held in the beautiful and challenging terrain of Bokskogen, Torup, outside Malmö. The race always takes place on the last Sunday in October, starting and finishing at Torups Friluftsgård. There are recreational 6 km and 12 km races, as well as a 6 km walk/power walk, and competitive classes for different ages, including veterans’ classes. All participants receive a race bib with a timing chip and a medal at the finish. Prizes are awarded to the top finishers in the competitive classes, and winners in the veterans’ classes have their prizes sent to them.
course_highlights: Cross-country race in autumn-coloured Bokskogen, Torup
Two distances: 6 km and 12 km
Start and finish at Torups Friluftsgård
additional: Race bibs with timing chips are provided to all entrants except those taking part in the walk and power walk. Bibs can be collected at the race office during the week before the race or on race day from 8:30 a.m. until one hour before the start. Prize-giving for places 1–3 in the women’s and men’s 6 km and 12 km competitive classes is at approximately 12:30 p.m. The start and finish area has parking and good public transport connections via buses 150 and 148. Carpooling is recommended. The race has previously been held in late October. The date and practical information for 2027 have not been confirmed in the available information.

name: Sjögarpslunken 2026
description: Sjögarpslunken is a long-running running race celebrating its 50th anniversary in 2026. The race is organized by Boxholm-Ekeby Ski Club and takes place at Boxholm ski stadium. It is a popular event for runners of all ages and abilities, with a scenic and challenging course. More information and registration will be available closer to race day.
course_highlights: Scenic route around the Sjögarp area
Challenging 14 km course with a course profile available
The race takes place at Boxholm ski stadium
additional: The race celebrates its 50th anniversary in 2026. Links to the invitation, race information, start list and preliminary results from previous years are available. A course profile and map are available for runners. The race celebrates its 50th anniversary in 2026. The gathering is scheduled for 09:30.

name: Hindås Trail
description: Hindås Trail is a running festival held on beautiful recreational trails in Hindås. Participants can choose between a 1 km race for children and 5 km or 15 km races for adults. It is a competition for those who want to run fast, and an enjoyable run for those who prioritise the experience. At the finish, participants are served coffee and chocolate biscuits, and hot dogs and an enhanced fika are also available for purchase. All proceeds go directly to the popular skiing activities in Hindås.
course_highlights: Beautiful recreational trails in Hindås
A 1 km children’s race on an easier course
A choice of 5 km or 15 km distances
additional: At the finish, participants are served coffee and chocolate biscuits. Hot dogs and an enhanced fika are available to buy at a good price. All proceeds from Hindås Trail go directly to the skiing activities. Coffee and chocolate biscuits are included after finishing. Hot dogs and an enhanced fika have been available for purchase. The proceeds go to Hindås Ski Club’s skiing activities.

name: Löfstad Slott Trail
description: Löfstad Castle Trail is an atmospheric trail race held in the autumn darkness around the historic Löfstad Castle. The race offers a unique running experience as participants run through the castle park, along forest trails and over unmarked terrain lit by headlamps. The event consists of two races: the Little Twilight Race for children in the park and Löfstad’s Darkest, a 7-kilometre night race for adults. Löfstad Castle Trail combines nature, history and community in a beautiful and challenging setting.
course_highlights: 7 km night race on gravel roads, trails and unmarked forest terrain
The course is marked with reflectors and course tape
Little Twilight Race: 1,000 metres in the park, with no timing
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 15:00 at the castle courtyard. Löfstad’s Darkest starts at 17:00 and requires a headlamp and trail shoes. The Little Twilight Race is a children’s race with no timing, and all participants receive a prize. The joint awards ceremony takes place after the races. On-site registration is available. Parking is available up to 500 metres from the castle. A headlamp is mandatory for the 7 km race, and trail shoes are recommended. The children’s race is untimed. The start and finish are at Löfstad Castle.

name: Ottestad løpsfestival
description: Ottestad Running Festival is organized by Ottestad Idrettslag and consists of three races: HOKA Ottestad Rundt over 17 kilometers, the Spenst Run over 5 kilometers, and the Sport1 Sprint for children, with distances of 400 meters, 1 km, and 1.8 km. The race starts and finishes at Ottestad Idrettspark, which has excellent facilities, including a café, refreshments, changing rooms, and showers. The course follows Ottestadstien, a scenic hiking trail through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland, with beautiful views of Mjøsa. The event is family-friendly and offers both timed and recreational races.
course_highlights: The course follows Ottestadstien through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland
Fantastic views of Mjøsa during the race
Start and finish at Ottestad Idrettspark, with a café and changing-room facilities
additional: The HOKA Sprint is a separate 430-meter segment on the 17 km course where participants can compete to be the fastest on Strava and win HOKA shoes. The segment has its own refreshment station, music, and spectators. A one-time race license is an additional cost for those without an annual license, and athletes up to age 12 are covered by NIF's child sports insurance. The 5 km and 17 km races can be run with or without timing. Listed prices apply to 2026, and a one-time race license is an additional cost where applicable.

name: Norgestesten 2027 3
description: Norgestesten is an efficient and inclusive running event held at Jessheim Athletics Stadium. The event offers distances ranging from an 800-metre children’s race to a half marathon, all with a mass start on a flat, fast 3,146-metre loop course. Many experienced pacers help participants find the right pace, and the event emphasizes convenient logistics, with parking and the train station nearby. Proceeds support sports for children and young people, and race bibs can be collected via self-service from 09:00 on race day.
course_highlights: Flat 3,146-metre loop course
Mass start for all distances
Many experienced pacers available
additional: The children’s race starts at 09:30 and is approximately 800 metres. Race bibs can be collected via self-service from 09:00 in the start area. Toilets are available at Jessheim Athletics Stadium and in the ice rink and multipurpose hall. A table for participants’ own drinks is provided at the start, along with water and sports drink along the course. The half-marathon cut-off is 2 hours and 30 minutes. The race is organized by volunteers, and proceeds support sports for children and young people. Information about dates and distances relates to different editions; the 2027 edition has not been confirmed in the sources.

name: Sønderjysk Crossløb 2026/27 - Cup tilmelding alle løb
Pärnu Rannajooks
description: Pärnu Beach Run is the season-ending race and final event in the Pärnu Two Bridges Club’s three-event series. It takes place at Pärnu Beach Stadium. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km distances, which can be completed by running or walking with or without Nordic walking poles. The course runs through the beautiful Pärnu beach area, offering natural scenery and architectural landmarks characteristic of the city, including the seaside promenade. The event is suitable for recreational and experienced runners alike and offers an enjoyable sporting experience.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km distances, available for running or walking with or without Nordic walking poles
Course through Pärnu’s beach area, with beautiful natural scenery and architectural landmarks
Seaside promenade with views of the sea
additional: The distance options are 5 km and 10 km, which can be completed by running or walking with or without Nordic walking poles. The race is part of the Pärnu Two Bridges Club’s three-event series. Children’s races and virtual race distances are also planned. The event includes virtual races and children’s races and takes place at Pärnu Beach Stadium, offering a chance to enjoy sport and nature together.

name: Bėgimas „Aplink Lietuvą“
description: The “Around Lithuania” Run is a traditional running event held in Rumšiškės, on the grounds of the Lithuanian Open-Air Museum. The event offers a range of distances, from a 300 m children’s race to the 21.098 km half marathon, which is the main event and counts toward the Lithuanian Running Cup standings. Participants start according to age-group handicap rules, and the event program includes registration, starts for different distances, and awards. It is a great opportunity to spend time actively outdoors and compete with running enthusiasts from all over Lithuania.
course_highlights: Distances range from a 300 m children’s race to a 21.098 km half marathon
Starts follow age-group handicap rules
Location: Lithuanian Open-Air Museum in Rumšiškės
additional: Event program: 09:00 registration and race number distribution, 10:45 competition opening, starts for different distances from 11:00 to 13:00, awards from 14:00. The main distance is 21.098 km, consisting of 4 laps. The age-group handicap system allows less competitive participants to start earlier. The event takes place in Rumšiškės, with online registration available. The program includes starts, awards, and special groups.

name: Volkswaldlauf des MTV Borstel-Sangenstedt
description: The MTV Borstel-Sangenstedt Volkswaldlauf takes place on 25 October 2026 in Winsen-Borstel. The event offers distances ranging from short children’s races to a challenging 20.3 km course, making it ideal for families as well as runners looking for a longer distance. The start and finish are at the Am Habichtshorst sports ground on Heidlandsweg, which serves as the central meeting point. The race is part of the Sparkassen Heidjer Cup and promises a varied route through natural surroundings.
course_highlights: Distances from 0.5 km to 20.3 km
Start and finish at the Am Habichtshorst sports ground
Event as part of the Sparkassen Heidjer Cup
additional: The event is aimed at families and runners of all ages. Typical October weather is around 14 °C, with a low of 6 °C and mostly cloudy skies. The Am Habichtshorst sports ground is the central meeting point for runners. Distances: 0.5 km to 20.3 km, including children’s races; central meeting point at the Am Habichtshorst sports ground; October weather: approx. 14°C, 6°C low, 40mm of precipitation, cloudy

name: 35. Ricklinger Volkslauf / Ricklinger Volkslauf
location: Meisenwinkel 9, Hannover-Ricklingen, Hannover, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Ricklingen Volkslauf is a local race day in Hannover-Ricklingen, organized by TuS Ricklingen. It offers flat races for adults over approximately 5.5 to 5.7 km, as well as walking and Nordic walking over the same distance. The main race is the 10 km Lothar-Mayer-Lauf. There is also a 400 m Bambini race for the youngest participants and a 1 km students’ race, allowing families and club runners to take part together, with participants grouped by age category.
course_highlights: Flat courses in Hannover-Ricklingen
Races for adults and children, plus walking and Nordic walking
Finish at Meisenwinkel 9 in Hannover-Ricklingen
additional: Running and walking events are grouped by distance and age category. There is a 400 m Bambini race and a 1 km students’ race. All races finish at the same location. The event takes place in Hannover-Ricklingen, with the start and finish at Meisenwinkel 9. It offers a family-friendly atmosphere with a range of events, including walking and children’s races.

name: 44. Zerbster Rolandlauf
description: The 44th Zerbst Roland Run is a traditional fun run in Zerbst, Saxony-Anhalt, starting and finishing at the Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn Stadium. The event takes place on a Sunday in October and is organized by the athletics department of TSV Rot-Weiß Zerbst. Various distances are offered for all age groups, from short children’s races to 10 kilometers for adults. The course is a flat 5-kilometer loop on paved and mixed surfaces that also passes through the stadium. Winners receive special 3D medals, and certificates are awarded to the top three in each category.
course_highlights: Flat 5 km loop on paved and mixed surfaces
Course passes through the Friedrich-Ludwig-Jahn Stadium
The 10 km race consists of two laps of the 5 km course
additional: Separate categories for children, teenagers, adults, and seniors. Winners receive special 3D medals, and certificates are awarded to the top three in each category. Typical October weather: around 14 °C, mostly cloudy, with about 40 mm of precipitation. The race also supports Anhalt Hospice Zerbst and is organized as a community fun run with medals and certificates.

name: Gütersloher DJK Halbmarathon
description: The Gütersloh DJK Half Marathon is an established running event in Gütersloh, taking place on 25 October 2026. The event offers a half marathon as well as 5 km and 10 km road races. The courses are officially measured by the DLV and are therefore eligible for rankings. The event is known for its friendly atmosphere, with awards for the fastest runners in various age categories and overall standings.
course_highlights: DLV-measured half-marathon course to IAAF/AIMS standards
5 km and 10 km road races as additional events
Awards for places 1–6 in the overall standings
additional: Certificates can be downloaded from the timekeeper’s website, www.timeteam-jung.de. Awards ceremonies will take place in the tent as soon as possible after the races. Parking is available at Hauptschule Nord, Ahornallee. DJK Gütersloh accepts no liability for accidents, theft or other damage. Measurement to DLV/IAAF/AIMS standards, online registration, parking at Hauptschule Nord, disclaimer of liability, certificates via www.timeteam-jung.de

name: VR Bank Westküsten Herbstlauf Schafstedt
description: The VR Bank Westküsten Autumn Run Schafstedt is an autumn running event in Schafstedt, Schleswig-Holstein, taking place for the 38th time in 2026. Distances include 3 km, 5 km and 10 km runs, as well as a 5 km walking route. The event welcomes adults and younger participants and fosters a family-friendly atmosphere with children’s and youth races. The routes pass through the autumn landscape in the fresh air and offer an alternative to city runs.
course_highlights: The 3 km route is flat
The 5 km run and 5 km walk include some hills
All races finish at the same finish line
additional: Children’s and youth races are part of the event. Typical October weather in Schafstedt is around 14 °C during the day and 6 °C at night, mostly cloudy, with an average of 40 mm of precipitation. The event also includes walking options and is aimed at families and young people. October weather is generally mild, with temperatures around 6–14 °C, creating ideal conditions for an autumn run.

name: 16 Nocna Ściema
description: Nocna Ściema is a unique night road race in Koszalin, offering three distances: 7 km, a half marathon, and a marathon. The course runs through the city streets, with the start and finish at the ZOS “Bałtyk” Stadium. The race has official PZLA certification, ensuring accurate course measurement and the possibility of setting records. The event has a one-of-a-kind atmosphere, with a laser start at 2:00 a.m. highlighting its unique nocturnal character. Participants can expect excellent organization, attractive prizes, and keepsakes.
course_highlights: PZLA-certified course, confirming accurate measurement
A loop of approximately 7 km, completed multiple times depending on the distance
Start and finish at the ZOS “Bałtyk” Stadium in Koszalin
additional: The race starts at 2:00 a.m. with a laser start. The race office for children and young people is located at the Koszalin University of Technology Sports Hall. The course runs through the streets of Koszalin, with views of exhibits at the aviation museum. After each distance, children receive gifts and prizes directly at the stadium. The course is undulating, and runners can rest at the stadium, which the loop passes through.

name: Sopot Półmaraton
description: PKO Sopot Half Marathon is an annual running event held in the seaside city of Sopot, attracting runners from across Poland and abroad. The half marathon course runs through the city’s picturesque streets, offering exceptional views and the atmosphere of running to the rhythm of the city. The finish line is at ERGO Arena, adding a distinctive character and sporting spirit to the event. It is also an opportunity for families to celebrate sport together, with numerous accompanying races for different age groups and ability levels.
course_highlights: A seaside course through the streets of Sopot
Finish line at ERGO Arena—a unique place to cross the finish
The atmosphere of running to the rhythm of the city, attracting runners and spectators
additional: The event also includes accompanying races such as the Half Marathon Relay, the 5 km Run, and races for children and juniors. The race pack includes a medal and other merchandise. The finish at ERGO Arena provides a unique atmosphere and comfort for participants. The organizer also offers the “Run, Be Ready” training plan for those preparing for the race.

name: XIV Bieg Nadwiślański Szlakiem Doliny D... (Tczew)
description: The Bieg Nadwiślański Szlakiem Dolnej Doliny Wisły is an annual running event held in Tczew County. The event features two races: a PZLA-certified marathon of 42.195 km and a half marathon of 21.097 km. The routes pass through the scenic Vistula Valley, over a mix of asphalt and gravel surfaces, with traffic restricted during the race. The start and finish are located in Tczew, and the event attracts runners from various regions, offering professional organization and clearly marked routes.
course_highlights: A PZLA-certified 42.195 km marathon through Tczew and nearby towns
A 21.097 km half marathon on an asphalt-and-gravel route
The course is marked with road markings and signs at 1 km intervals; traffic is restricted during the race
additional: The participant limit is 400 paid entrants. The marathon starts at 09:00 at the School Complex of Construction and Clothing in Tczew; the half marathon starts at 11:00 at the Primary School in Małe Walichnowy. The start line closes 15 minutes after the start. The marathon course is PZLA-certified; the half marathon course is not. The course is marked with road markings and signs at 1 km intervals.

name: 63 Bieg Republiki Ostrowskiej
location: Ostrów Wielkopolski, Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland

name: II Jesienny Bieg Charytatywny Artbud Group – Biegniemy dla Rodzin Zastępczych
XIV Pętla Krosowa Grodziskiego Klubu Biegacza
Botaniczna Piątka Przelewice – edycja jesienna 2026
location: Ogród Dendrologiczny w Przelewicach, Przelewice, Poland

name: Kullamannen by UTMB
description: Kullamannen by UTMB is an adventure race along the rocky shores of Kullaberg and the Bjäre Peninsula on Sweden’s southwest coast. The races range from 22 km to 100 miles and offer challenging terrain through rocky hills, beech forests, and coastal trails. This is a tough and scenic trail-running experience that attracts adventurous runners from around the world. The races are part of the UTMB World Series and offer a unique combination of technical trails and spectacular views.
course_highlights: Technical singletrack on Kullaberg
Passage through 15 nature reserves and two hills (Ultra 100 Miles)
Coastal trails and beech forests along the Bjäre Peninsula
additional: The start and finish for Ultra 100 Miles and Sprint Ultra are in Höganäs, with bib pickup in Båstad. Drop bags are provided and can be collected at specific aid stations and after the finish. It is possible to transfer a registration to a shorter distance up to three weeks before the race. Minimum age varies by race, and parental consent is required for minors taking part in North Shore 20K. The event also includes an extensive schedule of activities during the week before the races. The race lineup includes, among others, 20K, 50K, 100K, and 100 miles. For the 100-mile race, bib pickup takes place at the EXPO in Båstad.

name: Kullamannen 100 miles
description: Kullamannen 100 miles is an extremely challenging A+ 100-mile race that takes you through 15 scenic nature reserves and two mountains in Skåne. The race starts in Höganäs and the course includes technical singletrack on Kullaberg, one of Sweden’s most popular nature reserves. After 66 kilometres, runners can refuel with hot soup before continuing north towards Ängelholm and Torekov, with the finish in Båstad. The race is known for its high DNF rate of 40–60% and the tough weather conditions in November, with Scandinavian coastal winds and long hours of darkness.
course_highlights: Passes through 15 nature reserves and two mountains
Technical singletrack on Kullaberg Mountain
Starts in Höganäs and finishes in Båstad, with a chance to refuel after 66 km
additional: The race starts in Höganäs, with buses departing from Båstad. Race bibs must be collected in person at the Expo in Båstad. Drop bags are provided and can be collected at the Båstad Aid Station and after the finish. Drop bags must be collected within two hours after the race ends. Bib collection by proxy is not permitted. The race is part of the UTMB World Series. Bibs must be collected in person at the EXPO in Båstad, with valid ID and a QR code. Participants receive an official UTMB World Series drop bag.

name: Walking Dead Ultra 100 Miles
description: Walking Dead Ultra 100 Miles is a challenging ultramarathon held in Paradiset Nature Reserve in Huddinge. The race offers a unique terrain experience, with scenic views and technical trails that test both endurance and mental strength. It is a well-regarded event for experienced ultrarunners seeking a long-distance challenge in a beautiful setting.
course_highlights: Running in Paradiset Nature Reserve with varied terrain
Technical trails and scenic views
A challenging 100-mile distance
additional: The race also offers 100 km and 65 km distances. According to the available race information, drop bags and toilets are available, along with water, tea, coffee and broth at Torpet Paradiset.

name: Finalloppet Göteborg

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: Parvelbanan, ca 250 m, anmälan endast på plats tävlingsdagen. 40 kr

description: Finalloppet is western Sweden’s largest cross-country race. It has been organised by Göteborgs Skidklubb since 1968 and is held at Skatås Motionscentrum in Gothenburg. The event offers several distances (19 km, 10 km, 5.3 km, 2.3 km and 1.9 km, as well as Paraloppet and Parvelbanan) for both competitive and recreational runners. The courses alternate between technical trail sections and wider forest roads, and are marked with clear arrows and kilometre markers. The organiser brings the finish area and services together at the event venue at Skatås and provides water stations, medical care and a sweep crew on all courses.
course_highlights: The 19 km course has an advanced trail section of approximately 2,500 metres
The 10 km course includes a trail section just over 500 metres long that is often wet, muddy and rocky
The courses are marked with orange arrows and coloured kilometre markers; the leading groups are guided by a cyclist
additional: Registration is handled via RaceID (payment by card, Swish or Google Pay and Mobile BankID). You can register several people at the same time and buy gift cards via RaceID. The organiser offers Startklar insurance as an optional add-on, which reimburses the entry fee in the event of illness, injury or pregnancy. The event venue is at Skatås Motionscentrum, with finish and service tents, a medical tent at the finish, and medical staff at certain water stations (Ugglemossen and Svarttjärn). The sweep crew sets off after the last start for each course and is responsible for runners still on the course. Donate 50 kronor to Jontefonden when registering; a GPX file is available to download for the 19 km course.

name: Jätten Bule-löpet
description: Welcome to the 57th Jätten Bule Run on 31 October 2026 at Bulevallen in Österbymo. The race offers an enchanting forest setting, with trails and gravel roads winding through the area. There are recreational race classes for 10 km, 5 km and 2.4 km, where everyone can enjoy a challenging run surrounded by beautiful scenery. IFK Österbymo warmly welcomes all runners to a well-organised event with timing and excellent service.
course_highlights: The 10 km course runs along floodlit trails, forest paths and gravel roads across hilly terrain
The final 4 km take you through an enchanting forest on winding trails with both climbs and descents
The 5 km course is a miniature version of the 10 km course, marked in blue, while the 2.4 km course follows the floodlit trail
additional: Race bibs can be collected from 09:00 at the IFK Österbymo clubhouse by the start area. Timing is chip-based. Changing rooms are available in the clubhouse. Refreshments, including coffee and hamburgers, are available at the start area. Payment by Swish or cash. Bulis will lead a warm-up at approximately 10:00 before the children’s race starts. Start and finish at Bulevallen, Idrottsvägen, Österbymo.

name: Repovesi Trail 2026
description: Repovesi Trail 2026 is a trail running event held in Repovesi National Park on Saturday, 31 October 2026. The event offers three challenging distances: 10 km, 21 km and 42 km, taking runners through stunning natural scenery among rugged cliffs and forest views. The routes are clearly marked and feature varied terrain, offering a challenge for experienced runners and new adventurers alike. The event centre is at the Lapinsalmi car park, a short distance from the start of the route.
course_highlights: The routes follow the established trails of Repovesi National Park
Climbs, rugged cliffs and stunning forest views
The 21 km main route is run twice for the 42 km distance; the 10 km route takes a shortcut from the main route
additional: The event centre is at the Lapinsalmi car park, address Riippusillantie 55, 47900 Vuohijärvi. The race has a limit of 100 participants per distance, 300 in total. The finish closes at 18:00. Parking is available near the event centre. Runners must use their own cup at drink stations. Baba Foods smoothies, Maxim sports drink, sweets, crisps, bananas and raisins are available at the finish. After the race, a buffet meal is served at Restaurant Prinssi, with continuous bus transport to the car park. Route provisions include marking and aid stations; the event is environmentally friendly and offers prizes to participants.

name: Pohjoisbaanan maili 2026
description: Pohjoisbaanan Mile 2026 is a traditional mile race held on Pohjoisbaanan in Käpylä, Helsinki, on October 31. The race gives runners the chance to test their pace over one mile (1.609 km). The start is on the pedestrian and cycle path near Käpylä railway station, and the event is open to all running enthusiasts. The event is organized by Helsingin Juoksijat ry, and participation is free for members. Welcome to enjoy a fast-paced, community-minded running event!
course_highlights: The distance is exactly one mile, or 1.609 km
The start is on the pedestrian and cycle path near Käpylä railway station
The event takes place on Pohjoisbaanan in Käpylä, Helsinki
additional: Participation is free for members of Helsingin Juoksijat ry. The start location is marked by a Helsingin Juoksijat flag. The event lasts about an hour, from 11:00 to 12:00. The event starts at 10:00, and no information is available about specific course features or registration procedures. Helsingin Juoksijat also offers a variety of running training and community events throughout the year.

name: Komia Ilkan Polku
location: Ilmajoella Kyrkösjärven läheisyydessä, Ilmajoki, South Ostrobothnia, Finland
description: KOMIA Ilkan Polku is a varied and challenging trail-running event held in Ilmajoki near Kyrkösjärvi. The event offers several distances, including a 39 km marathon, a 20 km half marathon, a 10 km sprint, and the children’s Halloween Run. The route follows a variety of trails and village roads, with approximately 300 metres of elevation gain. The event centre is at Luontokeskus Käpälikkö on the shore of Kyrkösjärvi, where runners can enjoy beautiful natural scenery and challenging sections. The event is also family-friendly and encourages participants to dress in a Halloween theme.
course_highlights: Varied trails along the Ilkan Polku nature trail
Approximately 300 metres of total elevation gain
The route also includes approximately 3 km of village roads and gravel roads
additional: The event has mass starts, bag storage, and bag transport from the start to the finish area. The café serves coffee, sweets, sausages, and drinks. First-aid points are located along the route and at the finish. Changing facilities, showers, and toilets are available in the changing rooms at Kyrkösjärvi beach. Littering in nature is prohibited. The children’s Halloween Run is free and encourages participants to dress up in costume. The event includes various categories, the route, timing, prizes, a café, soup, bag storage, toilets at Kyrkösjärvi beach, a recommendation to have insurance, first aid, and the opportunity to test running shoes.

name: Sandflugtsløbet 2026
distance_verbose: Halvmarathon, 15 km, 14 km, 10 km, 7 km, 5 km, 2 km

name: 26. Dresden-Marathon / DRESDEN-MARATHON
description: The DRESDEN-MARATHON has been held regularly in late October since 1999. It offers a flat, fast course through the Saxon state capital, passing its famous sights. The route goes through the historic Old Town, including Brühl’s Terrace, the Semper Opera House and other Baroque buildings, as well as the lively Neustadt district. More than 300 musicians and numerous bands create a special atmosphere along the course. The second half of the marathon runs through the Blasewitz district, with views of the palaces on the Loschwitz Elbe slope and the villas along Goetheallee, before returning to the Old Town along the Elbe.
course_highlights: Flat, fast course through Dresden’s historic Old Town and Neustadt district
Illuminated Waldschlößchen Tunnel and bridge, and the Großer Garten
Atmosphere created by more than 300 musicians and bands along the course
additional: More than 300 musicians and numerous bands create an atmosphere along the course. There is a marathon expo, race-pack collection and a SPARKASSEN pacemaker service. After the race, medal engraving, a photo service, showers, changing rooms and toilets, as well as award ceremonies, are available. The evening before the race, an anniversary party takes place in the marquee behind Heinz Steyer Stadium (€25 admission; limited capacity). Several race distances, online registration, health questionnaire, event on 24 and 25 October 2026

name: 34. Mündener Altstadtlauf
description: The 34th Mündener Altstadtlauf takes place on October 31, 2026, in Hann. Münden and offers suitable distances for runners of different age groups and ability levels. The event includes Bambini and schoolchildren’s races, as well as 5 km and 10 km races for recreational and competitive runners. The course is measured by the Lower Saxony Athletics Association and is therefore eligible for record times. In addition to individual rankings, there are group and team rankings, making the race particularly appealing to teams. The organizing team places great importance on professional delivery and continually improving the event.
course_highlights: Course measured by the athletics association and eligible for record times
500 m Bambini course and 1,000 m schoolchildren’s race for young runners
5 km course with a group ranking and 10 km course with a team ranking (at least one woman per team)
additional: The 5 km course offers a so-called combined ranking for groups. The 10 km course has a team ranking for teams of three, including at least one woman. Around 40 volunteers help with setup and dismantling and secure the race routes. Various local institutions, including the fire department, police, and city administration, are involved. Commentator Frank Neumann hosts the event. Courses for Bambini, schoolchildren, 5 km, and 10 km; team and group rankings; courses measured to be eligible for record times

name: 6. Halloween Run
description: The Halloween Run Bremen 2026 takes place on October 31 at Werdersee in Bremen and offers runners a spooky running experience with various distances from 1 km to the marathon. The courses are measured in accordance with German Athletics Association rules and are eligible for record lists, underscoring the competitive nature of the event. Alongside the sporting event, participants can look forward to a spooky atmosphere with costumes, lights and fog, as well as a spectacular fireworks display to close the event. The event is open to all age groups and ability levels, and includes relay races and a children’s run.
course_highlights: 8.333 km loop, measured by the German Athletics Association and eligible for record lists
Distances from 1 km to the marathon (42.195 km) in a spooky atmosphere
Start and finish area at Werdersee, with fireworks from 18:00
additional: Relay races for men’s, women’s and mixed teams with RFID bibs. Costumes are expressly encouraged, but regular sportswear is also allowed. The award ceremony takes place immediately after the Spooky Run and later for the other distances. Fireworks from 18:00 bring the event to a close. The start and finish area is between the Finnbahn at Werdersee and the Grillwiese/DLRG lifeguard station. Several running distances, including the marathon, take place on measured loops; costumes are encouraged; the event concludes with fireworks.

name: Bredstedt-Cross
description: The 39th Bredstedt Cross takes place on 31 October 2026 at Sportpark Bredstedt and is hosted by Bredstedter TSV. The event offers cross-country races for a wide range of ages, from children and young people to senior competitors and numerous masters categories. There are short and long cross-country races for men and women, as well as separate age categories from M6/W6 to M75/W75, including youth and U18/U20. The event is listed as category 6.5.1, an event held away from a stadium, and offers a varied competition format for all age groups.
course_highlights: Cross-country races for children, youth, senior competitors and masters
Short and long cross-country races for men and women
Age categories from M6/W6 to M75/W75, as well as youth and U18/U20
additional: The entry deadline is 28 October 2026; online registration is open until 23:59. The event is listed as category 6.5.1, an event held away from a stadium. No detailed course distances or other practical information are provided on the page. The entry deadline is 28 October 2026; October weather is typically around 14°C with about 40 mm of precipitation, making the cross-country race a challenging, nature-oriented experience.

name: Kreismeisterschaft und 3. Halloween-Crosslauf im Örtzetal zu Munster
location: Sportpark Osterberg, Munster, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The District Championships and 3rd Halloween Cross-Country Run in the Örtzetal in Munster is a cross-country event taking place on October 31, 2026, at Sportpark Osterberg in Munster. The event combines the District Cross-Country Championships with the third Halloween Cross-Country Run and is open to children, young people, open categories and masters. Distances range from 500 metres to 10 kilometres, offering a local, club-oriented atmosphere rather than the feel of a major city race. The race takes place in the autumnal Örtzetal region and is a popular seasonal event organised by Eintracht Munster.
course_highlights: Cross-country running in the Örtzetal on varied terrain
Distances from 500 m to 10 km for different age and ability categories
Event at Sportpark Osterberg in Munster
additional: The event was postponed due to bad weather and incorporates the District Championships into the Halloween Cross-Country Run. Typical October weather is around 14 °C, with mostly cloudy skies and an average of 40 mm of precipitation. The event uses a cross-country race format, has a local character, is open to children, young people, adults and masters, and takes place on Halloween with weather-dependent adjustments.

name: Nordhessische Crosslaufmeisterschaften
description: The North Hesse Cross-Country Championships are a regional club and regional cross-country championship held in various locations across North Hesse. The event is aimed primarily at club runners from the region competing for regional and district titles. Course distances range from short youth races of 1.2 km to longer senior races of 8 km. The races take place on cross-country terrain, not on closed roads, and are organized by various athletics districts and clubs.
course_highlights: Cross-country terrain rather than a road race
Distances from 1.2 km to 8 km
Held at sports facilities in various locations across North Hesse
additional: The event is geared strongly toward club runners. Depending on the course, runners are advised to choose suitable shoes carefully, such as spikes. Results are published as web and PDF listings. Typical October weather is cool and mostly cloudy, with a daytime high of about 14°C and a low of 6°C. October weather: about 14°C, low of 6°C, 40 mm of precipitation, cloudy; races take place at sports facilities in the region, online registration is possible, and results are published as web and PDF listings.

name: Botaniczna Piątka – Bydgoszcz, edycja jesienna
location: Botanical Garden of the Kazimierz Wielki University, Bydgoszcz, Poland

name: Höstmilen
description: Höstmilen is a trail race in the Kolmården forests outside Åby, north of Norrköping, taking place on 1 November 2026. The course follows trails between Sörsjön and Lillsjön and offers scenic, challenging terrain for both competitive runners and recreational participants. The event is organised by OK Kolmården and has three main race options: the classic 10.6 km, Höstfemman 5.2 km, and races for children and young people.
course_highlights: Trail race on paths between Sörsjön and Lillsjön
Höstmilen 10.6 km (Sörsjön → Lillsjön) and Höstfemman 5.2 km (start/finish at Lillsjön)
Running through the scenic, hilly terrain of the Kolmården forests
additional: Online registration closes on 29 October at 23:00; after that, it is possible to register on 31 October from 11:00 to 14:00 at XXL and at the start area on 1 November. For the classic Höstmilen, a bus runs from Jurslaskolan to the start at Sörsjön. The race information sheet will be published approximately one week before the event. The adult races have just two prize categories: Men and Women. A complete list of registered participants will be published on the “Registered” page. Distances and competition formats are 10.6 km, 5.2 km and children’s races (1.4 or 2.0 km); team, company and school competitions. The Höstmilen race information sheet and registration are available via hostmilen.nu.

name: Perseløpet 5 km, 10 km, halvmaraton
description: Perseløpet is a race focused on fast times, held at Ås school in Eidsvoll. The race takes place on a flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop, where participants can set out their own bottles and gels on their personal nutrition table. Seven distances are offered, from 3 km to 100 km, including 5 km, 10 km and the half marathon. Race numbers are collected from a self-service station at the school, and the venue has good facilities, including changing rooms, toilets and free parking. The race has a friendly atmosphere, with personal records celebrated by the ringing of a bell at the finish area.
course_highlights: Flat, accurately measured 2,633-metre loop
Participants’ own nutrition tables along the course
Good venue facilities, including changing rooms, toilets and free parking
additional: Race numbers are collected from a self-service station about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. The race uses a lap-time calculator to plan split times. At selected races, the 9th grade class at Feiring school staffs an official drinks station to raise money for their school trip. The weather forecast is updated four times a day using satellite data for the area around Ås school. Public transport to the venue is available by train and bus, with real-time departures. Race numbers are collected from a self-service station at the school from about two hours before the start. Free parking, changing rooms and toilets are available at the venue. Registration is through RaceDays.

name: HA Ottestad løpsfestival 2027
description: HA Ottestad Running Festival is an annual event held at Ottestad Idrettspark, with the start and finish in the same place. The festival consists of three races: HOKA Ottestad Rundt (17 km), the Spenst Race (5 km), and the Sport1 Sprint for children, with distances of 400 m, 1 km, and 1.8 km. The course follows Ottestadstien, a scenic walking trail winding through a cultural landscape of wooded areas and farmland, with splendid views over Lake Mjøsa. The event offers good facilities, including a café, food and refreshments, changing rooms, and showers in the clubhouse.
course_highlights: The course follows Ottestadstien through a cultural landscape of woodland and farmland
Fantastic views over Lake Mjøsa
Start and finish at Ottestad Idrettspark, with good facilities
additional: The HOKA Sprint is a separate 430 m segment on the 17 km course where participants can compete to be the fastest on Strava and win HOKA shoes. There is music, spectators, and a dedicated drinks station at the sprint segment. A one-day race license is an additional cost for those who do not have an annual license. Athletes up to age 12 are covered by NIF’s child sports insurance. The festival features HOKA Ottestad Rundt (17 km), the Spenst Race (5 km), and the Sport1 Sprint for children. The 17 km and 5 km races can be run with or without timing. The start and finish are at Ottestad Idrettspark, which has a café, food and refreshments, and changing rooms with showers.

name: REINPAULI XXIV MAASTIKUJOOKS
location: Ebavere, Väike-Maarja Parish, Lääne-Viru County, Estonia

name: Birkhahnlauf
location: Schneeren, Neustadt am Rübenberge, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Birkhahnlauf in Schneeren is a traditional race that has been held annually on the last Sunday in October for over 50 years. The event offers distances for all age groups, from short children’s races starting at 500 metres to challenging 5 km and 10 km races for adults. The routes run through the pine forest on firm forest paths with a slightly sandy surface and no significant elevation gain, making the race a special experience surrounded by nature. New this year is a 2.3 km distance for age group U12 and above. The friendly atmosphere and promptly held award ceremonies with certificates and medals round off the event.
course_highlights: Routes through the pine forest on firm forest paths
Distances from 500 m to 10.2 km for all age groups
Kilometre markers on the 5.1 km and 10.2 km routes, with no significant elevation gain
additional: Start times: children’s 500 m at 10:30, 1,000 m at 10:45, 2.3 km at 11:10, and 5.1 km and 10.2 km at 11:40. Award ceremonies take place promptly after the respective races. Parking is available nearby and signposted. Online registration is preferred from 01.08.2026; the entry fee must be paid on site no later than 20 minutes before the race starts. Forest race, distances from 0.5 km to 10 km, children’s races, online registration from 01.08.2026, start on 25.10.2026

name: Halloween-Run-Bremen
description: The Halloween Run Bremen 2026 takes place on October 31 and offers runners a spooky race experience around Werdersee. With five different distances, from 1 km to the 42.195 km marathon, there is something for every ability level. The courses are measured in accordance with German Athletics Association rules and are eligible for record lists, underscoring the competitive nature of the event. Alongside the sporting event, participants can look forward to a spooky atmosphere with costumes, lights and fog, as well as an awards ceremony and a closing fireworks display.
course_highlights: 8.333 km loop course, measured by the German Athletics Association and eligible for record lists
Distances from 1 km (Spuklauf) to the marathon (Splatterthon), with a spooky atmosphere
Start and finish area at Werdersee, between the Finnbahn and the barbecue area
additional: The awards ceremony for the Spuklauf takes place immediately after the finish; awards for the other distances are presented later. A spectacular fireworks display at 18:00 rounds off the event. There are also relay competitions for the marathon (5-person relay). The race bib with RFID chip serves as the relay baton and must be brought by the team. Costumes are expressly encouraged but are not compulsory. Participants can register online. There are various distances and relay options; the event takes place at night and offers a spooky atmosphere.

name: 19. Bothfelder Waldlauf
location: Bezirkssportplatz Bothfeld, Hannover, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Bothfelder Waldlauf is a DLV-approved public race organized by TuS Bothfeld 04 in Hanover. The races start and finish at the Bothfeld district sports ground and follow a loop through the beautiful Bothfelder Wald on forest trails and well-maintained forest roads. The race is part of the Hannover Region Running Pass and offers changing and shower facilities in the finish area. Affordable food, drinks, and free hot tea are available. The event is open to runners of all age groups, including Bambinis, with short-distance races.
course_highlights: Loop through the Bothfelder Wald
Forest trails and well-maintained forest roads
Start and finish at the Bothfeld district sports ground
additional: Late entries on race day can be made online up to 60 minutes before the respective race, subject to availability. The late-entry fee is €2 in addition to the entry fee. The children’s race award ceremonies take place approximately 60 minutes after the races; ceremonies for the longer races follow immediately after the finish. On-site certificate printing is available. The 5 km walk starts at the same time as the 10 km main race. Changing and shower facilities are available. Public transport is available via tram line 13, and parking is available nearby. The registration deadline is October 30, 2026; the event takes place in typical November weather in Hanover; the event is outside the official stadium calendar.

name: 28. Tangerpokallauf
description: The 28th Tanger Cup Run in Demker is the oldest running event organized by SC Demker '95 and is part of the Elbe-Ohre Cup. The course runs through the autumnal Tanger lowlands between Demker and Weißewarte, past Deutsches Eck, under the Stendal–Magdeburg railway line, and through the Süppling woodland. Distances offered are 1.2 km for children and young people, and 5.4 km and 12.0 km for older young people and adults. The terrain is mostly flat, with gentle rises formed by the dikes surrounding Demker.
course_highlights: Flat course through the Tanger lowlands between Demker and Weißewarte
Runs along the Tanger and past Deutsches Eck
Passes through the Süppling woodland
additional: Distances: 1.2 km (children/young people), 5.4 km and 12.0 km (older young people/adults). The terrain is flat throughout, with the dikes as the only rises. The course passes under the Stendal–Magdeburg railway line. The event takes place on November 1, 2026. Information is also provided about registration, results, photos, and accommodation in Demker.

name: LG Alsternord Herbstwaldlauf 2026
description: The LG Alsternord Autumn Forest Run is a local autumn race through the forest in Norderstedt, north of Hamburg. Organized by LG Alsternord Hamburg e.V., the race starts at 11:00 a.m. at the Rantzauer Forst-Thingplatz. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km routes, including a cross-country option. The race takes place away from city streets in the Rantzauer Forst area and also offers walking and hiking events. With a modest field of usually 101 to 300 runners, the event has more of a club-run feel than that of a major race.
course_highlights: Run through the autumnal Rantzauer Forst, away from city streets
5 km, 10 km and cross-country options
Modest field with a club-run atmosphere
additional: Results are published via race result; public start lists, photos, reports and historical rankings are available. In addition to the races, there are walking and hiking events, including a 5 km walk. Typical November weather is around 7 °C, with rainy days. The event takes place in typical November weather, around 7°C and with rainy conditions. It is open to runners and walkers of all ages, with a modest participant count of between 101 and 300.

name: Tiergarten-Cross
description: The Tiergarten Cross in Schleswig is a local cross-country race taking place on November 1, 2026. The event offers two main distances, 4.4 km and 8.8 km, which start one after the other so the fields are separate. The course is undulating and demands constant changes of pace, making the race varied. In addition to the main races, there are also children’s and youth races, making the event family-friendly and diverse.
course_highlights: Finishes in Tiergarten Schleswig, the most distinctive point on the course
Undulating course with constant small changes of pace
Separate start times for the 4.4 km and 8.8 km distances
additional: The event also includes children’s and youth races. Typical November weather in Schleswig is cool, with daytime highs of around 7 °C, and rainy on most days. The event takes place in Tiergarten Schleswig, is weather-dependent (November is usually rainy), and offers a family-friendly atmosphere with various race categories.

name: Landehof 4-Årstider Höstloppet 2026
description: Landehof 4 Seasons Autumn Race 2026 is an orienteering event held at Landehofstugan, Landvetter, on November 3. The race offers a challenging autumn setting with darkness, rain, wind and slippery roots, providing an authentic autumn experience in the forest. Participants can enjoy an exciting, traditional orienteering experience in beautiful surroundings. Start lists and live results will be published well in advance of and during race day.
course_highlights: Orienteering in an autumn setting with darkness and slippery roots
Challenging terrain in the forest around Landehofstugan
Traditional autumn race with a long history and a strong sense of community
additional: The start list will be published from Friday, October 30, and updated until the registration deadline. Live results and the results list will be available. Register by logging in with your personal identity number on OK Landehof's registration page. QR codes are available to easily share the invitation and registration details with colleagues or training partners. Start and gathering point at Landehofstugan in Landvetter. A headlamp is recommended. Registration is open until November 1, 2026.

name: MartinCrossen Trail Run
description: MartinCrossen Trail Run is a trail race starting and finishing at Voksenjordet in Oslo, inspired by the Martincrossen ski race and Martin Johnsrud Sundby. The race offers a unique course with challenging technical terrain, particularly on the longest distance, which ends with a tough finish. The event takes place in the evening in November, and the darkness and use of headlamps on the 3 km and 8 km distances make for a special experience. The race is inclusive, with categories for children, young people, para athletes, recreational runners and competitive runners. There will also be a show with pyrotechnics, flames, lights and music in the spirit of Martincrossen.
course_highlights: Trail running on challenging technical terrain
Start and finish at Voksenjordet
Evening race, with headlamps required on the 3 km and 8 km distances
additional: The 500-metre children’s race for ages 3–5 and the para category are free and do not require registration. Companions for para participants are free; contact mari@roail.no. Medals for all participants. A show with pyrotechnics, flames, lights and music. A limited number of race bibs are available for late registration, which opens on 2 November at 12:00. The sources describe the 2026 edition, listed as taking place on 4 November 2026, and do not confirm the date or registration details for 2027.

name: Frikarusellen 2026/27 alle løp
location: Espeland idrettsplass, Espeland, Arna, Bergen, Norway
price_range: 65-450 kr, avhengig av alder og påmelding

tiers.label: tier_1
tiers.description: 15 år og eldre: 450 kr for alle løpene

tiers.label: tier_3
tiers.description: IL Fri-medlemmer: 100 kr for alle løpene (bruk rabattkode)

tiers.label: tier_4
tiers.description: 15 år og eldre: 80 kr for enkeltløp

description: Frikarusellen 2026/27 takes place at Espeland sports grounds in Arna and consists of six races on a certified 5 km course. The course starts north of Londalskrysset, runs via Gamle Haukeland station and returns along the same route, finishing inside the sports grounds. The races are suitable for both young people and adults, with separate prices for members and age groups. The event has a long tradition and offers easy registration through EQ Timing, with race bibs distributed on race day.
course_highlights: Certified 5 km course (first measured in 2000, revised in 2018)
Starts north of Londalskrysset and returns via Gamle Haukeland station
Finishes inside Espeland sports grounds
additional: Race bibs can be collected at Espelandshallen on race day between 18:00 and 18:55. Registration is open until 18:55 on race day. A licence fee is additional for participants over 13 without an annual licence. There is a fee of NOK 50 for forgetting your race bib if you have registered for all the races. Results are published at www.eqtiming.no. The series consists of six races: 14.10.2026, 04.11.2026, 25.11.2026, 27.01.2027, 17.02.2027 and 10.03.2027. Registration is open until 18:55 on race day; race bibs can be collected at Espelandshallen from 18:00 to 18:55. A licence fee is additional for participants over 13 without an annual licence.

name: Energiruset
organizer: IF Göta Karlstad och Karlstads Energi
description: Energiruset is an evening race in Mariebergsskogen, organised in collaboration between IF Göta and Karlstads Energi. The race takes place on Thursday, 5 November 2026, and is family-friendly, with a choice of distances of 2 km and 5 km. The 5 km distance has a competitive category for those who want to test themselves; much of the course runs through woodland, and some sections are unlit. After finishing, all participants are treated to a hot dog by the organisers.
course_highlights: The course runs through Mariebergsskogen, including woodland.
Some sections of the course are unlit; a headlamp is recommended.
Distances: 2 km and 5 km; the 5 km has a competitive category.
additional: Date and location: Mariebergsskogen, Thursday, 5 November 2026. You can buy a headlamp when registering. Practical information (chip collection and exact start times) will be published on the organiser’s website. A previous race briefing is available as a PDF: https://ifgota.se/files/PM_ER_2025.pdf. After the race, IF Göta and Karlstads Energi will treat participants to a hot dog. The course will be open during the evening for non-competitive participants, who can start within a specified time window. The start times are tentatively around 18:00.

name: Ledlenser Nightrun Bergen
location: Fløysletten, Fløibanen Upper Station, Bergen, Norway
description: Ledlenser Nightrun Bergen is a unique trail race held in the dark, where all participants run with headlamps. The race offers an exciting experience along Bergen’s forest trails at night, with reflective markers along the course to help runners. Separate men’s and women’s categories are held across several age groups, and all participants receive a medal. The race has a sociable atmosphere, with luggage storage available and prizes for the top finishers.
course_highlights: Trail race through dark forest trails
The course is marked with reflective markers
Headlamps are required
additional: Ledlenser provides a limited number of headlamps for testing and loan during the race, available on a first-come, first-served basis. Self-service luggage storage is available in the start area. There are separate men’s and women’s categories for ages under 25, 25–39, 40–54, and over 55. All participants receive a medal and can enter a draw for spot prizes. A headlamp is required; reflective markers along the course help you find your way. Race numbers can be collected at Löplabbet Bergen, Strandkaien 6, November 1–3, 10:00–19:00, or at the race venue from 17:00 on race day. Self-service luggage storage is available in the start area.

name: Nightrun Oslo
description: Ledlenser Nightrun Oslo is an exciting night race held at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann. The race offers an atmospheric experience, with headlamps lighting the trail and reflectors along the course helping participants find their way to the finish. There are separate men’s and women’s categories in several age groups, and all participants receive a medal and the chance to win great prize-draw prizes. The event has a friendly social atmosphere, with self-service baggage storage and awards for the top runners.
course_highlights: The course passes through scenic surroundings at Sognsvann
Headlamps light the trail in the dark
Reflectors along the course provide visibility and help runners find their way
additional: Ledlenser provides a limited number of headlamps for testing and borrowing during the race, on a first-come, first-served basis. Self-service baggage storage is available in the start area, and the baggage tag from your race bib must be attached to your bag. There are separate men’s and women’s categories for the age groups under 25, 25–39, 40–54 and over 55. The top three men and women overall receive prizes. The start and finish are at the Norwegian School of Sport Sciences at Sognsvann. Race bibs can be collected at Löplabbet Oslo, Pilestredet 7, or at the race venue on race day. All participants receive a medal, and a limited number of headlamps are available to borrow.

name: Samnanger Vinterkarusell - 1. løp
description: Samnanger Winter Series is a social and inclusive running series organised by Samnanger IL Running Group, with races held approximately every other Friday at Nesodden throughout the winter. Participants can choose between 2 km and 5 km courses, with the 5 km course officially measured by NFIF. The races suit all levels, from beginners to experienced runners, and focus on the joy of running and community. The start and finish are at Nesodden, and participants are encouraged to wear reflective gear because of the winter darkness. The Winter Series is a great opportunity to stay in shape and take part in a welcoming running community.
course_highlights: Race at Nesodden, with the start and finish at the same place
Choose between 2 km and 5 km courses; the 5 km course is officially measured by NFIF
Races are held approximately every other Friday during the winter at 19:00
additional: The running group is informal, free, and open to all levels. Wearing a reflective vest is recommended because of the winter darkness. The Winter Series is held approximately every other Friday at 19:00 at Nesodden.

name: Jämjöhalvan och Jämjöhallenstafetten
location: Jämjö, Karlskrona Municipality, Blekinge County, Sweden
price_range: Jämjöhalvan 21,1 km: 300 kr (4/6-2/10) eller 400 kr (3/10-2/11); Jämjöhalvan 10 km: 250 kr (4/6-2/10) eller 350 kr (3/10-2/11); Jämjöhalvan 5 km: 200 kr (4/6-2/10) eller 300 kr (3/10-2/11); Barnlopp 50 kr; Jämjöhallenstafetten: 600 kr per lag (4/6-2/11).
description: Jämjöhalvan is a mass-participation race organized by Team Blekinge LF, with distances ranging from a children’s race to a half marathon, as well as a relay (Jämjöhallenstafetten). The half marathon and other races take place on a fast, spectator-friendly loop course around Jämjö and can also be used as qualifying races for events such as Göteborgsvarvet. The event centre and finish are at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum, and in 2026 the Swedish Veterans Championships in the half marathon will be held alongside the race. Runners of all abilities are welcome—the event emphasizes running community and clearly marked laps.
course_highlights: Loop course: 4 laps for the half marathon, 2 laps for 10 km, 1 lap for 5 km
Fast, spectator-friendly course around Jämjö
Distances are officially measured (measured 25 Sep 2021), and course marshals are stationed along the route
additional: The start, finish and event centre are at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum. Start locations vary by distance. The half marathon and Jämjöhallenstafetten start at 10:30, the 10 km at 10:40, the 5 km at 10:45 and the children’s race (500 m) at 12:45. Runners must keep to the right and pass on the left; runners who are not running at a fast pace are asked to keep right. In the relay, teams hand over a baton in the exchange area near the lap point; late registration is not available for Jämjöhallenstafetten. Late registration for other distances is open on race day from 08:00 to 10:00 at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum. Payment is accepted in cash or via Swish. Start times: 21.1 km and Jämjöhallenstafetten 10:30, 10 km 10:40, 5 km 10:45, 5 km youth class (ages 12–16) 10:45, children’s race 12:45. Start locations vary by distance. There is no late registration for Jämjöhallenstafetten. The start and finish are at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum. The course is a loop with water stations every 5 km, in cooperation with Umara. Changing facilities and showers are available at Jämjö Kunskapscentrum from approximately 09:00. Free open training sessions are held on 17 September and 15 October before race day.

name: Skanneloppet
price_range: Fram till 7 oktober: 17,3 km 200 kr; 7,6 km 150 kr; 3,9 km 100 kr. 8 oktober – 24 oktober: 17,3 km 300 kr; 7,6 km 200 kr; 3,9 km 150 kr. 25 oktober – 5 november: 17,3 km 400 kr; 7,6 km 300 kr; 3,9 km 250 kr.
description: Skanneloppet is organized by IS Skanne and takes place on Saturday, November 7, 2026, starting and finishing at Tingvalla amusement palace in Åstorp. The race is run individually, with approximately ten runners starting per minute, and offers three courses for both elite runners and recreational runners. The courses are hilly and run mostly on gravel roads, with some asphalt and trails, and the race is suitable for both young and old. Registration information and start lists are published on the organizer’s website.
course_highlights: Three distances: Red 17.3 km, Blue 7.6 km, and Green 3.9 km
Hilly terrain—mostly gravel roads with some asphalt and trails; particularly hilly at the beginning
Aid stations are marked on the map (yellow circles)
additional: Bib pickup from 08:00 on race day. Check your bib number in the start list inside Tingvalla and collect it yourself. No on-site registration. There are no showers or changing rooms on site (toilets are available). Medical assistance is available at the finish, and a defibrillator is available. Maximum running time is until approximately 12:30. Those who register before October 24 will have their name printed on their bib. All finishers receive a commemorative plaque; commemorative medals are awarded after completing 5, 10, 20, 30, and 40 races. Start times are between 10:00 and 11:05, with approximately 10 runners starting per minute. Start and finish: Tingvalla, Vramsvägen 9, Åstorp. No on-site registration. Showers and changing facilities are unavailable; toilets are available. Start lists and results are published on the IS Skanne website. Bibs for the 17.3 km race can be collected on site from 08:00 on race day.

images.alt_text: IS Skanne-logotyp från inbjudan till Skanneloppet.
Löpare vid start och mål för Skanneloppet i Åstorp.

name: Höstrusket
description: Höstrusket is a trail and road race in Norra Djurgården, Stockholm, taking place on 7 November 2026. Choose from 10 km, half marathon (21.1 km) or marathon (42.195 km), with the start and finish at Fisksjöängsvägen. The race is suitable for both beginners and experienced runners, and features encouraging pacers, well-stocked aid stations and an atmospheric end to the running season in the Royal National City Park. The event is organised by Marathongruppen together with local athletics clubs, and the surplus goes back to sport.
course_highlights: Start and finish at Fisksjöängsvägen in Norra Djurgården (approx. 800 m from Ropsten metro station)
Certified courses, mostly on asphalt with some gravel; 10 km: +103.9 m, marathon: total elevation gain +439 m
Well-stocked aid stations and lap support, as well as clearly marked kilometre signs
additional: Start/finish at Fisksjöäng (approx. 800 m from Ropsten metro station). Bib collection, pacer tent, food and coffee sales, bag drop for warm-up clothes and toilets at the event area. Changing and shower facilities are available at a nearby venue for a fee, a few hundred metres away. Chip timing by RaceTimer; pacers are available for several finish times (lists by distance). Cut-off times: 10 km 2:00, half marathon 2:30, marathon 5:30 (cut-off at the final lap point at 13:40). Minimum ages: 10 km from age 15 (age 13 when accompanied by a guardian); half marathon and marathon from age 17. Some aids and vehicles (poles, inline skates, strollers, bicycles, handcycles and racing wheelchairs) are not permitted; special conditions apply for guides and wheelchair users. The surplus goes back to sport. Registration is open.

name: Nyårsloppet
description:
For the 43rd time, Vallentuna Friidrott invites everyone—from elite athletes to recreational runners and children—to take part in a winter race on the streets and squares in central Vallentuna. Participants and spectators may be met with challenging ice, slushy snow, wonderfully crisp winter weather or a fast asphalt course.
Nyårsloppet is a great way to get a little active before the New Year’s meal and the year’s reflections. And as some people say: “What you do on New Year’s Eve sets the tone for the rest of the year!” So take the opportunity to get active, bring a friend and run or jog around the course.

name: Craft Idre Fjällmaraton
description:
Become unbeatable
We believe everyone has the right to feel unbeatable at some point. Not in relation to anyone else, but in relation to yourself. Unbeatable because you achieved something you didn’t think was possible. Because you dared to do something you didn’t think you could. Because you ventured into unknown territory and won. You won over that little voice telling you that you can’t.

name: Kroppefjäll Trailrun

tiers.description: 900 meter: 0 kr för de allra minsta

tiers.description: 10,5 km: 350 kr för ungdom under 18 år

description: Kroppefjäll Trailrun is an evening race at Kroppefjäll B&B in Dals Rostock, offering runners three main distance options (42 km, 21 km and 10.5 km) in two-person teams, as well as a children’s race around the pond. The course is technical terrain with plenty of singletrack and natural trails, and the race has a relaxed, adventurous atmosphere with no official timing. After the finish, participants can use the large sauna and take a refreshing dip in the pond. Accommodation can also be booked at Kroppefjäll B&B with discounts. The organisers welcome both experienced trail runners and younger participants (Lilla KTR) in a friendly setting.
course_highlights: Approx. 60% singletrack/off-trail, 35% gravel road/forest road and 5% oil-gravel road
Race format: trail running in two-person teams
Lilla KTR: children’s race around the pond (approx. 900 m), with the option to run 1–3 laps
additional: Bus to the start from Kroppefjäll B&B; GPX file for 21 km; bring your own fluids; bib pickup in the days before the race or the evening before; accommodation discounts via Trailrun1/Trailrun2; the Lilla KTR race takes place on 7 November at 18:00; registration deadline: 4/11.

name: Iron Backbone Ultra
description: Iron Backbone Ultra is a trail adventure in Kristinehamn built around the Järnleden and offers three distances (15, 30 and 50 km). The race takes place on varied and characterful terrain—deep forests, bogs, small lakes, pastures and old trails—putting both mental toughness and the joy of running to the test. The start and finish are at Hultets friluftsgård, and the 15 km course partly leaves the Järnleden. The organiser, Topp & Dröm, welcomes both experienced trail runners and those who want to try trail running for the first time.
course_highlights: The course largely follows the Järnleden through varied terrain (forests, bogs, lakes, pastures and old trails)
Start and finish at Hultets friluftsgård, Kristinehamn
The 15 km course partly leaves the Järnleden
additional: Three distances are offered: 15 km, 30 km and 50 km; start and finish at Hultets friluftsgård; from 1 October, places are limited to ensure a specially designed medal for every participant; organiser: Topp & Dröm (contact person Lasse / telephone 073-853 75 21), and the information pages have sections on aid stations and equipment. Start times: 30 km and 50 km at 17:00; 15 km at 17:30. No cups are provided at the aid stations; bring your own cup. Start and finish at Hultets friluftsgård, Kristinehamn. Entry fees are updated over time, and from 1 October, places are limited to secure a specially designed medal for every participant.

name: Nyårsloppet Vallentuna
description:
The New Year’s Race is a perfect way to get active during the days between Christmas and New Year. For the 42nd time, Vallentuna Friidrott is inviting runners to take part on New Year’s Eve, with everyone from elite athletes to those who prefer a more relaxed pace. A winter race can mean challenging conditions or fast asphalt—we never know until race day. Keep an eye on the weather forecast and read our information. Statistically, conditions have been favourable for running in most years, as the results from previous years show.

Above all, the New Year’s Race is a lovely way to get together to round off the old year and have something to talk about at the celebrations later in the day.

You’re welcome too—we’ll see you there!
additional: Please remember that the New Year’s Race is a winter race, and conditions can vary from year to year. In some years, spiked shoes may be recommended.

name: Österlen Spring Trail
description: Österlen Spring Trail was founded in 2015 and can be described as a recreational race where nature, camaraderie and the experience take centre stage, while performance and time are secondary. The race offers all runners, regardless of ability, a fantastic opportunity to take part in one of three distances: 60 km (Simris Alg Ultra), 30 km (Duo Trail) and 22 km (Teleservice trail). It takes place amid the beautiful natural surroundings of Christinehof Castle in Andrarum, Skåne County, and has 500 metres of elevation gain.

images.alt_text: Löpare springer på stig i Österlens vackra natur.
Löpare springer på en strand under Österlen Spring Trail med en grönskande kulle i bakgrunden.
Karta som visar banan för ÖST 13km, en del av Österlen Spring Trail, med start och mål markerade.
Österlen Spring Trail logotyp med fågel och texten ÖST.

name: Nora Marathon
description:
A hilly marathon, most of which is run on asphalt, but also includes gravel roads.
You run four laps.
If you choose the half marathon, you run two laps, and if you choose the quarter marathon, you run one.

name: STHLM Trail Marathon
description:
A warm welcome to the second edition of STHLM TRAIL MARATHON
All races take place on a very scenic course, approximately 15 km long. Each lap will offer you nearly 500 metres of elevation gain. Expect beautiful views and challenging running, mostly over hilly terrain and mostly on trails, sometimes off-trail, but also on a couple of gentler sections where you can stretch out and run for a few hundred metres.

New for 2026
• Be on the start line as early as April! This time we’re holding the event in early spring, so mark 18 April in your calendar now.
• Kids Trail, a free race for our younger runners (born in 2014 or later).
• Hjärnloppet, a virtual race lasting 18 days, where the entire entry fee goes directly to Hjärnfonden and vital research into epilepsy.
• Course preview runs. On two occasions, we’ll run through the first and second parts of the course.
• Virtual running sessions in the Heyey app to help you stay in shape all the way to the start line in April.

What’s not new for 2026
• The course, a challenging and very scenic route in the area around Lake Flaten.
• Sprint and Ultra, two trail races that challenge you a little extra.
• Grit, the ultimate test, which we don’t think anyone can complete. If you prove us wrong, you’ll win both honour and fame, as well as some prize money.
additional: All information on the organiser’s website

name: Billingen Trail
description:
We invite you to enjoy running on Billingen. This year, the start and finish will be at the Stadium in the Billingen Recreation Area.
The long course is just over 47 km with approximately 930 metres of elevation gain. It goes all the way around northern Billingen, along beautiful trails by the edge of the mountain. As a runner, you’ll experience varied terrain, including deciduous forest, mountain ravines, meadows and spruce forest, as well as beautiful views across the landscape from several places. The surface varies from easy-to-run sections and approximately 6 km of asphalt to some more challenging parts.

The middle-distance course, 21 km, follows the northern section of the Billinge Trail and has approximately 500 metres of elevation gain. The course includes a mix of trails, meadows and roads.

Our shortest distance, 12 km, has just over 200 metres of elevation gain and follows trails of varying difficulty, with some short sections on roads.

Information about the courses and markings may change.

Start:

47 km, 10:00, Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.
21 km, 10:45, Björnasäter, Lerdala. Bus departs from the Billingen Recreation Area at 10:05.
12 km, 11:30, Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.

Finish:

At the Stadium, Billingen Recreation Area, Skövde.

All finishers cross the finish line at the stadium.

name: Isaberg500
description:
Isaberg 500 is the race we love running ourselves and the foundation of the entire trail weekend. It’s a perfect mix of trails, hills, sweat and tears that brings to mind spectacular races in both the Swedish mountains and the Alps. Isaberg 500 also features switchbacks, long, enjoyable downhill stretches and fantastic views. In between, you can enjoy winding trails through enchanting forests. Isaberg 500 includes at least 500 metres of elevation gain and is perfect for anyone training for a mountain marathon or similar race.

NEW FOR 2025!
When Isaberg500 started, Jättestigen was a big talking point. A few years later, it was closed due to the risk of landslides. In 2025, Jättestigen returns as part of Isaberg500, but under a new name — Jättetrappan...

Isaberg500 is a race in the Outnorth Trail Tour 2025.
course_highlights: Trail race with varied trails and hills, with a technical character reminiscent of races in the mountains and the Alps
Multisport around the Isaberg summit: kayaking, mountain biking and trail running — Solo and Duo categories
Isaberg Gravel: a circuit of approximately 45 km, starting and finishing in Åsenhöga; Elite/up to age 50: 3 laps, older riders/sport recreation: 2 laps, recreational: 1 lap
additional: Contact GI by mobile at +46 703 815 118 or email at gimulti@gmail.com. Organisers: GI Folkestad and Martin Jepson. Guided rides for cycling groups can be booked; the organisers have ready-made routes that can be adapted to the group’s needs. Main distance: approximately 10.5 km (Distans Trailtour); Kids Trail: approximately 2 km with approximately 150 metres of elevation gain; start time: Sunday at 12:00; location: Isaberg/Anderstorp; contact: niklas@isabergtrail.se.

description: Dammekärr Dirt Dash is a trail-running series in Dammekärr organised by the orienteering club OK Alehof. The competition consists of three races with combined scoring, and participants can choose to run one, two or all three races. The courses run through hilly forest terrain and come in three different distances: 1.5 km, 3.5 km and 7.0 km. The short course follows the floodlit trail, while the longer courses require a headlamp. After the finish, runners can enjoy a hot sauna and refreshments in the club cabin, creating a pleasant and social atmosphere.

name: Backyard Ulötra Sölvesborg
description:
What is Backyard Ultra?
Backyard Ultra takes place on a marked 6,706-metre loop, and each participant has one hour to complete it. A new start takes place at the top of every hour, and as long as you can complete the loop within an hour, you remain in the race. You win by being the most enduring and ultimately getting to run one final lap alone! A fun race and concept with a very welcoming, community-minded atmosphere, where many participants set their distance records!

name: Fredsloppet
description: Fredsloppet 2026 is a peace and solidarity race held at several locations in Sweden, including Stockholm, between 15 August and 18 October 2026. The event is more than a running race; it is an expression of peace, justice and solidarity, supporting Palestinian and Cuban organisations. Participants can choose from different distances, including 5 km and 10 km, as well as walking categories and mini peace races for children. The event encourages people to organise their own Fredsloppet races, and the surplus goes to peace and solidarity work.

additional: 75% of the proceeds go to Palestinian aid, and the event celebrates its 40th anniversary in 2026. Participants can register via fredsloppet.se. The event includes water stations, medals and the option to register on the day.
