name: Ultra Caballo Blanco Suecia
description:
Only the 100-mile race starts on Friday (08:00); the 100 km and 50-mile races start on Saturday (06:00).
All three races have their own routes (they have nothing in common with CBMR, which takes place on the same day). The 50-mile and 100-mile races have some staffed aid stations, which are also shared with the 100 km race, which has its own stations as well. The 100-mile race is virtually entirely unsupported, apart from a few unmanned water stations. You also pass a well-stocked country store and a church with water and toilets.
All three races offer the option of a drop bag.
The courses are completely unmarked, so you navigate using a downloaded GPX file...
additional:
We don’t have paper cups, so bring a cup!
Hot food, drinks, coffee and cake are served after the finish.

The entry fee includes 120:-, which is sent to a children’s race in Urique, Mexico!

name: Caballo Blanco Memorial Run (CBMR)
description:
This is the route that Caballo Blanco (aka Micah True) and I ran on 2011-09-26, when he was visiting Sweden at my invitation. In spring 2012, we received the news that he had died. We then organised a memorial race on 2012-09-22. It became a tradition, and eventually the race offered 1, 2 or 4 laps of the route, which is approximately 11 km and has approximately 150 metres of elevation gain.
See also Ultra Caballo Blanco Suecia — an ultra race held at the same time.
An article I wrote quite a while ago, when we introduced the 50-mile race:
https://redsports.se/CBM/TheStory.html
additional:
The 4-lap race starts at 12:00, while the 1- and 2-lap races start at 15:00.
Please note that you must bring your own cup/mug.
The entry fee includes drinks, energy products, and a hot meal with coffee and cake after the race.

name: Bräkneåns Dalgång 25 K
description:
A technical trail race through the Bräkneån valley, starting at Hoby Ekebacke. The course is partly technical but also includes sections of asphalt.
The course has a total elevation gain of approximately 400 metres.
The generous time limit is 5 hours, allowing a maximum average pace of 12 min/km.
The finish is at Hoby Eckebacke.

The course will be clearly marked, and a GPX file will also be available for you to download to your watch or phone.
An aid station with food and drink will be available halfway, as well as at the start and finish.

Everyone who completes the race within the time limit will receive a lovely medal from RawCut studio.
additional:
Start and finish at Ekebacken Bräkne-hoby

Women’s/men’s category

name: Hoby Backyard Ultra 24 H
description:
Hoby Backyard Ultra 24H. Start and finish at Ekebacken in Bräkne-Hoby on Saturday, 26/9 at 10:00.
The course is the same as before, with varied terrain and approximately 60 metres of elevation gain.
The course has been officially measured using a measuring wheel and is 6,706 metres long.
Each lap starts on the hour. To complete the lap and continue to the next one, each lap must be completed within 1 hour.

Energy, drinks, sports drinks, and hot meals will be served to all participants throughout the race.

Everyone who completes at least 1 lap within the time limit will receive a stylish medal from RawCut Studio.

All participants can take shelter under the roof inside Rotundan at Ekebacken throughout the race.

Medically trained race staff will be on site throughout the race.

Welcome to another fantastic running festival!
additional:
Start and finish at Ekebacken in Bräkne-Hoby.

Women’s and men’s categories.

name: Vildmarksleden 100 miles
description:
The first edition of Vildmarksleden 100 Miles, with an exclusive limit of just 25 places.

An out-and-back trail race taking you from Hoby Ekebacke to Eringsboda and then back to Hoby Ekebacke.

The course follows selected sections of Vildmarksleden and includes technical trails, gravel roads and asphalt. Approximately 1,850 metres of elevation gain.

One drop box, transported by the organizer to the turnaround point (50 miles) in Eringsboda. Opportunities to refill fluids and energy supplies at several points along the course.

A GPX file on a watch or mobile phone is mandatory.

Participation is entirely at your own risk. Participants are responsible for having the knowledge and equipment required to complete the race.
additional:
Start and finish at Ekebacken, Bräkne-Hoby
Men’s and women’s categories

name: GUM - Gotland Ultramarathon
description:
One of Sweden’s most beautiful ultramarathons. The race starts at 9:00 at Hallshuk in northern Gotland, and the course heads south along the coast, with the sea on your right all the way to Visby. The route is approximately 50 km, with very varied terrain.

There is also a Half-GUM (28 km), starting at 11:00 in Lickershamn.

name: XC-race Linköping
description: Linköping XC-race is an annual cross-country race organised by Linköpings OK in Vidingsjön, Linköping. The race offers a marked 5 km loop through varied terrain, including trails and marshland, and is open to both recreational runners and competitive classes. Participants can choose between 5 km, 10 km for men and women, and a 5 km recreational class. The 10 km races cover two laps. The event is known for its challenging, muddy terrain, and the start and finish are at Vidingsjö Motionscentrum.

name: Västerås Marathon
description:
NEW RACE 2026

Västerås Marathon offers three distances — 42 km, 21 km and 10 km — on a flat, fast course through the heart of the city and along the beautiful shores of Lake Mälaren. The course is a loop course, with 10 km per lap.
Experience the joy of running in a well-organised race for all levels.

The race is for everyone who enjoys running, from beginners to elite athletes. All ages and paces are welcome, and generous time limits will be set for completing the race.

A warm welcome!

name: Kilterrängen
description: Are you among those who prefer trails to asphalt? Whether you’re a curious beginner, a recreational runner, or an elite runner, Kilterrängen is for you. Starting and finishing at Frykstahöjden in Kil, this 16 km trail race ends with a few tough kilometres full of hills, including the notorious ski slope. The course is just as suitable for running at full speed as for jogging, walking with poles, or hiking. You can also choose to run 6 km, with the same tough finish as the longer course.

name: Oskarshamn backyard 6h 2026
description:
A Backyard race lasting under 6 hours.

One 6.7 km lap every hour for 5 hours. In the 6th hour, one 8.7 km lap. 42.195 km in total. If you complete the race, you will have covered a marathon! The first to finish the final lap wins.

name: Löparfesten
description:
The running festival offers several different races, with something for everyone!

Whether you’re looking to set a personal best in the half marathon or prefer a walk with good friends, there’s a great race to choose from!

EKO ½Maran is for experienced runners, FORMTOPPEN Milen is a wonderful challenge, and the slightly shorter Here We Go 5an is for happy recreational runners or those who prefer to run fast but short. For those who want to take it a little easier, perhaps bring walking poles or a stroller, or simply enjoy nature, there’s Here We Go 5an – Promenad!

There are also races for younger participants—Papricaloppet—for everyone up to 12 years old! We also have Rulleruset for everyone with a disability! At Rulleruset, you can choose between a shorter 1.4 km race and a slightly longer 5 km race!

As we said, there’s something for everyone!

name: Å-stadsloppet
description:
Å-stadsloppet runs through both Örebro’s neighborhoods and scenic areas such as Rynningeviken and Wadköping.

The 5, 10 and 21.1 km courses have all been officially measured by federation course measurer Bertil Sundin.

name: Uppsala Marathon
description:
UPPSALA MARATHON
17 OCTOBER 2026
Through centuries of history – one step at a time
MARATHON • HALF MARATHON • MARATHON RELAY
Celebrate 10 years with us!
Challenge yourself and experience one of Sweden’s most popular races in beautiful autumnal Uppsala. Run the marathon or half marathon, or gather family, friends or colleagues and take part in the marathon relay.
Uppsala Marathon is turning 10!
Over 42,195 metres, the course takes you through some of Uppsala’s most historic, scenic and remarkable surroundings. From the castle and Carolina Hill to the River Fyris, the city centre and leafy green spaces – a unique combination of running, history, culture and a festive atmosphere.
Whether you’re an experienced marathon runner or taking part for the first time, you’re warmly welcome to help write the next chapter in the race’s history.
All participants are invited to enjoy a post-run gathering, and all finishers receive a technical T-shirt and this year’s exclusive 10th-anniversary medal.
More information and registration:

Along mountain trails, paths, boardwalks and gravel roads, nature will challenge you on your way to the finish and the After Run at Experiumtorget in Lindvallen. name: Änglamilen
description: Änglamilen is a long-established fun run in the heart of Ängelholm. Participants experience the town, the sea and the forest all in the same 10 kilometres. The 5 km race begins with a lovely run through the park in the charming Hembygdsparken. After approximately 2.7 km, the course crosses the Rönne River and continues along the beautiful riverside path in Nybroskogen. Finally, the course turns back across the river, with a sprint to the finish at Tullakrok. The 10 km course starts the same way as the 5 km route, but turns north after about a kilometre. Runners are treated to beautiful views over Skälderviken and its harbour, with Kullaberg visible in the background. After approximately 7.7 km, the courses join again, and runners can enjoy the beautiful riverside path in Nybroskogen.

name: Refleksløpet Kristiansand
description: The Reflective Run in Kristiansand invites you to a magical evening run with headlamps on Thursday, November 13. The start and finish are at Fant Olsen in Baneheia, with registration opening at 16:30. Participants can start from 17:00, while the mass start with timing is at 18:00. The course is 4.1 km long and follows the outer edge of Baneheia, marked with reflective markers. Participants must bring a headlamp, and mulled juice and porridge will be served after the finish.

name: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Maraton
description: Fagerstrand Backyard Ultra Marathon 2026 is organized by Fagerstrand IF at Myklerud, Fagerstrand. This unique race starts on Saturday, November 7 at 09:00 and follows a simple but demanding format: a new 6.7 km lap starts every hour. The race continues on a “last man standing” basis until only one runner remains, or is decided on lap 12 if several runners are still competing. Participants can choose their strategy: run fast for a longer break or take it easier to conserve energy. There will be a banquet for runners and their companions.

description: Grimstadvatnet Rundt is a 7.8 km road race run mainly on asphalt, with a relatively flat course. The race is part of the Hareid Winter Series, which consists of four races held on the first Saturday in November, December, January and February. The first race in the series was held in 1981, and awards are presented after the fourth and final race in February. To qualify for an award, runners must complete at least three of the four races. Scores are based on the three best races, with bonus points for completing all four.

name: Refleksløpet Arendal, Fossbekk
description: Welcome to the Refleksløpet in Arendal, an atmospheric race in the dark held at Fossbekk in Arendal. The race offers two distances: a short 4.8 km course and a long 7.8 km course, as well as the option to walk without timing. The race starts early in the evening, and participants are encouraged to wear a headlamp for a safe and magical experience. This is a social event where friends, family and running buddies can get together for a fun and active evening.

additional: The race office opens at 16:30 for registration and bib collection. The long course starts at 18:00, the short course at 18:05, and walkers without timing can start at 17:00. The first 30 people to register will have the chance to win a Mizuno bag. Registering before race day is recommended to avoid stress. Participants receive a 15% discount on headlamps at Brekke sport's physical store. The long course starts at 18:00 and the short course at 18:05. Walkers without timing can start at 17:00. The race office opens at 16:30, and a headlamp is recommended.

There is also a free run for children, along with fun arts and crafts and play activities.

The race takes place in Nuuksio National Park and attracts runners from Finland and around the world. Participants can choose from different distances, including 42 km and 70 km, and enjoy superb courses, wild forest, and excellent organization. Join us on September 5, 2026!

name: Orimattilan Kymppi
description: The most significant village event to develop in Kuivanto is Kuivannon Kymppi. As a celebration of physical activity, it brings villagers together in late autumn to exercise and organize a sporting event. This outdoor and sporting event, initiated by local residents, was first held in 1981, when 24 participants completed the course. The event has grown into a significant international gathering, with more than 500 participants from countries including Russia, Estonia, Sweden, England and Kenya. Through cooperation between the City of Orimattila and local village associations, the event has been carried forward one year at a time.

The course is designed to be both challenging and enjoyable for runners of all levels. The event is aimed especially at fitness enthusiasts and running fans, and offers an excellent opportunity to enjoy the outdoors and good company. Participants can run or walk, and anyone who wants a time will be timed.

The start and finish are on Keskuskatu, in front of the more than 100-year-old Elävien Kuvien cinema.

The race continues until only one runner remains, but unfortunately the organizers will have to end the race after 36 laps if no winner has emerged after just over 240 km of running.

name: 55. Pirkan Hölkkä 5.10.2025
description:
A jewel of the running season, the icing on the cake: this long-distance running event, held mainly on trails, takes place every year on the first Sunday in October.

The 33-kilometre route from Valkeakoski to Tampere runs along a varied mix of fitness trails, forest roads and trails. Around five kilometres of the route are on asphalt. In addition to the running categories, you can take part in a walking category, which is not timed. The event is organised jointly by Tampereen Taivaltajat ry and Valkeakosken Retkeilijät ry.

Pirkan Hölkkä dates back to 1970. The route has largely remained as it is today. In recent years, the average number of participants has been around 1,000–1,500.
additional:
You can choose from the age categories Women’s Open, N40, N50, Men’s Open, M40, M50 and M60. The start is at the Sahara sports field in Valkeakoski (Tallikatu 11), where the starting gun will sound at 9:30 on Sunday morning. Late registration at the start is available from 8:00 to 9:00.

The event uses gun time, measured from the starting gun until you cross the finish line. At the start, you can choose a position near the start line according to your target time.

The first 3 km of the race are on streets. For the next 3 km, the route follows the fitness trail in the recreational area as far as Leppäjärventie. After that, the route to Rutajärvi (11 km from the start) consists of varied forest trails and a short section of gravel road. The 3.5 km stretch between Rutajärvi and Vähä-Kausjärvi is on forest roads. Of the 5 km between Vähä-Kausjärvi and Taivalpirtti, the first part is on forest roads, followed by forest trails; after crossing Savontie, the route returns to gravel roads.
From Taivalpirtti onward, the route alternates between gravel roads and forest trails until it reaches the recreational trail around Suolijärvi. The final 3 km follow a gravel-surfaced recreational trail between Hervanta and Koivistonkylä. This section still has a few climbs that will test Finnish grit.

The Pirkan Hölkkä route is marked with blue flagging tape, directional arrows and kilometre signs. The organisers have aimed to include as many forest trails as possible. There are six refreshment stations along the route.

The finish is in Nirva, Tampere, in the grounds of Tampere Adult Education Centre (Kurssikeskuksenkatu 11). Paid bus transport to the start is available from the finish area and Tampere city centre, both in the morning before the start and in the afternoon after you finish. You can include transport and the soup lunch sold at the finish area in your entry fee by selecting these add-ons in our online store.

name: Pirkan Kieppi 5.10.2025
description:
The jewel of the running season and the icing on the cake, Pirkan Hölkkä is a long-distance running event held mostly on trails. It takes place every year on the first Sunday in October. Together with TU38, we are organizing the much-requested shorter distance, the 14 km Pirkan Kieppi.

Pirkan Kieppi starts at the Pirkan Hölkkä finish area, in the courtyard of TAKK’s Nirva campus, at 11:30. On-site late registration is open from 10:00 to 11:00.
additional:
The route continues via Lahdesjärvi to Vuores, where it winds through the beautiful scenery of this neighbourhood. It then joins the traditional Pirkan Hölkkä route at the Vormisto aid station, from where runners continue to the finish together with the full-distance participants.

Pirkan Kieppi has two open categories, women (N) and men (M). Timing is based on gun time, from the starting gun to crossing the finish line. At the start, you can choose a spot near the start line according to your target time.

name: Guldfeber Aarhus — Golden Fever #1
description:
Gold Fever — Denmark’s first SplitRace tournament. A free running game in the streets of Aarhus: 12 segments (0.4–1.9 km) are mapped around the city, and 7 of them form a hidden “golden chain” — nobody knows which ones, or in what order. Find them. Run them. Chase the times.

No mass start and no entry fee: run whenever you want, as often as you want, throughout 17 October – 1 November. The app measures your times via GPS. You earn points for each golden segment based on how close you are to the fastest time — women are scored against the fastest woman, men against the fastest man. Extra points go to the first runners to unlock a golden segment — and the tournament’s biggest bonus goes to the first to complete the whole chain in the correct order.

This is the first edition — a pilot for a maximum of 30 runners. Your feedback will shape the game.

(EN: A free city-wide running game in Aarhus. 12 segments, 7 of them secretly form a golden chain — find them and beat the clock. No mass start: run anytime 17 Oct – 1 Nov. Free entry, GPS timing in the SplitRace app. First edition, 30 pilot spots.)
additional: No start line and no start groups — all segments are on public, lit routes around Aarhus, and you can run them whenever you want during the event window. Participation requires the free SplitRace app (iOS / Android) — download it via splitrace.app, join the “Guldfeber Aarhus” tournament, and all 12 segments will appear on your map. Limited to the first 30 runners. Open streets: follow normal traffic rules. Questions? Write to support@splitrace.app or Instagram https://www.instagram.com/split_race/

- A convenient, compact event centre close to Tallinn.

- Of course, there’ll also be a hot sauna and, for the bolder participants, a hot tub.
- You can also take part with your whole work team to boost team spirit and health.
- Together, we’re helping improve public health in Estonia.

The Sportland pop-up shop will be open all day, so you can top up your running gear if you’ve forgotten something at home or want the best functional gear for the course. Every finisher will receive a great medal, a GRAM drink and a Nicks bar. Winners will receive Sportland credit, a sapling and gifts from our partners. The season’s best in each age group and the season’s best team will also be recognised.

Want to enjoy a private sauna with your group? Rent the Iglusaun by the pond! Would you like to stay overnight in Kõrvemaa? Check availability at Kuuse Elamusmajad.
course_highlights: 100% of the course runs through a stunning nature reserve
Trail running in unspoilt nature, with a mix of climbs and descents
Routes suitable for beginners and experienced runners alike
additional:
Register online at iseteenindus.sportlandkorvemaa.ee or through the Sportos platform, where Stebby is also available as a payment method.

The event takes place on Sunday, 27.09.2026. On race day, you can register at the start venue from 10.00. Registration closes 30 minutes before the start.

Seniors (aged 60+) and young people (aged up to 17) receive a 50% discount on the main distances when registering in advance. The discount is applied automatically during registration based on year of birth. The minimum discounted price is 15 EUR; the discount will not reduce the price below this amount. The discount does not apply to youth races, which already have a special price of 15 EUR. Only one discount can be used at a time; the system always applies the larger discount.

A 10% discount applies when registering at least 5 people together. A 20% discount applies when registering at least 10 people together. If you are registering from the same company, club or group of friends, be sure to enter your team name, as we will award the best team to take part in the series at the end of the season.

name: Swedbanki Tallinna Maraton
description:
Swedbank Tallinn Marathon and Tallinn Autumn Run invite you to register!

Estonia’s largest running and movement festival, the Swedbank Tallinn Marathon, takes place from September 11 to 13. The programme of this event, which brings together thousands of active people, includes the classic marathon (42.195 km) and marathon relay, half marathon (21.1 km), Tallinn Autumn Run (10 km), Nike Youth Run (5 km), Welcome Run and Limpa Kids’ Runs.

The Tallinn Marathon’s event centre and start-finish area are located on the edge of Tallinn’s Old Town, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The course runs along streets and cycle and pedestrian paths, passing interesting places and offering a colourful overview of Estonia’s capital.

Over the years, more than 340,000 active people have taken part in the Tallinn Marathon across its various distances. The record for international participants at Estonia’s largest sporting event by number of participants was set in 2025, when runners came from as many as 93 countries.

Take this opportunity to be part of Estonia’s most spectacular movement event!

Although heavy rain accompanied the runners, it did not dampen the festive atmosphere—the awards ceremony was held inside the Panoteriai church.

You can choose from the following distances: running—a marathon, half marathon, 7 km, 3 km, and 400 m (children’s race); Nordic walking—a half marathon and 7 km. Every participant who completes their distance will receive a wonderfully beautiful, one-of-a-kind medal!

name: Bėgimas Kaune
description: The annual pink ribbon charity run in Kaunas supports breast cancer prevention. It is a short, recreational and fun running course—a joyful, positive celebration of sport decorated with pink costumes, paint, balloons and ribbons. During PINK RUN, both men and women can show their support and love for the women closest to them: their mother, daughter, sister, wife or best friend.

The most enduring runners are invited to set off on an adventure through the hills and valleys of Ąžuolynas Park! From a true test of endurance to active entertainment, there’s something for everyone among the different race distances and obstacle courses—whether you’re a thrill-seeker or an enthusiast of active recreation. This year, the run attracted a record number of participants and was held at the KTU Student Campus and in Ąžuolynas Park.

description: The renewed and unique representative Šiauliai Run 2024 will take place on September 22 at 12:00. THE BIG START. The project’s main goal is to promote physical activity and sport by encouraging an active, fulfilling way to spend leisure time, fostering community spirit and a healthy lifestyle. The run will follow the city’s central streets, passing places significant to Šiauliai’s history. It is for people of all ages, from recreational runners to professionals. The program includes a 700 m children’s run, a 1236 m run commemorating the date of the Battle of the Sun, and 5 km and 10 km runs.

After each lap, the remaining time can be used for rest and food. Every hour, you will return to the starting line and run another lap until only one runner remains. The Lithuanian record is 22 laps, and the world record is 108 laps.

Support the fight against breast cancer by taking part in runs of various distances for both professionals and amateurs. Pink Run with Antėja is more than a run; it is a message that we love them.

The fastest woman was Aurika Balsytė, who is from Kelmė District. There was also a 1.8 km race, in which Lukas Mikavičius performed best, and a 200 m race for young children.

name: 14. Sollingquerung
description: The Solling Crossing is a unique run from Dassel to Bad Karlshafen, taking place on November 7, 2026. The course is run exclusively by GPS, as it is not marked, making the event particularly challenging and exciting. The field is limited to 100 participants, creating a friendly atmosphere. The start is at 9:00 a.m., after runners are taken by bus from Dassel to Bad Karlshafen at 7:45 a.m. A tip for runners: anyone who completes the marathon distance at the Solling Run on June 6, 2026, is guaranteed a starting place in the Solling Crossing.
course_highlights: Course from Bad Karlshafen to Dassel
No course markings; GPS navigation only
Aid stations along the course
additional: Start at 9:00 a.m. after the 7:45 a.m. bus ride from Dassel to Bad Karlshafen. Field limited to 100 participants. No course markings; GPS navigation only. Tip: A starting place is guaranteed to participants in the Solling Run marathon on June 6, 2026. The course is unmarked, GPS navigation is required, November weather may bring rain and temperatures of around 2–7°C, no on-site entries are possible, and the event sells out quickly.

name: 6. Weserbergland Backyard Ultra
description: The Weserbergland Backyard Ultra Run is a unique ultrarunning event in Höxter, North Rhine-Westphalia, held every year in November. Participants run a lap of about 6.7 kilometers every hour until only one runner remains. The race stands out for its distinctive challenge and the camaraderie among runners. The event is known for its demanding course and the impressive performances of participants, who often run for many hours and cover many kilometers.
course_highlights: A course of approximately 6.7 km per lap
A loop course with challenging climbs on the Heiligenberg
A run through varied terrain in the Weserbergland
additional: The race traditionally starts at 10 a.m. Registration usually fills up quickly, and the field often reaches capacity early. There is currently no waiting list. The event is organized by TuS Lütmarsen e. V. Participant numbers are limited to ensure the quality and safety of the event. It is one of Germany's last major Backyard events of the year, with typical November weather and long nights. Registration opens on 1 May 2026.

name: Pokallauf
description: The “Rund um Marienberg” Cup Race is a traditional running event held in the Marienberg region. Competitions are held in classic and freestyle technique, with distances of 5 km and 10 km, each run on a 2.5 km loop. The event offers runners of various age groups and ability levels a sporting challenge in a scenic setting. Due to the current snow conditions, technical and course adjustments may affect how the competition is run.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km distances on a 2.5 km loop
Classic technique for U6–U9; freestyle technique from U10
New 10 km distance from H21
additional: The event is organized by ATSV Gebirge/Gelobtland e.V. The event announcement will not be updated. Competition technique depends on age group: U6–U9 use classic technique with a mass start; U10 and older use freestyle technique with a mass start. Depending on snow conditions, the route may vary, with adjustments to technique and distance. It is a popular event for runners seeking nature and a challenge.

name: SCC Cross Country
description: The SCC Cross Country is a forest race in Berlin at the Julius-Hirsch-Sportanlage in Westend. Two clearly defined cross-country routes are offered: 4 km for U16 through adults and 9 km for U18 through adults; both races start in the morning. The event is deliberately straightforward and is aimed at club runners, young athletes and adults who want to run short off-road loops, setting it apart from the city’s major road races. The course follows paved and unpaved forest paths, where rhythm, sure footing and a fast finish matter more than scenic views. Awards go to the top three in each age and gender category, and there is a prize for the fastest final lap for men and women.
course_highlights: Forest race on paved and unpaved forest paths
Two routes: 4 km for U16 through adults, 9 km for U18 through adults
Focus on rhythm, sure footing and a fast finish
additional: Entry is free for SCC members. Late registration is available shortly before the start for an additional fee. An archive of results is available to document the race. The event takes place at the Julius-Hirsch-Sportanlage on Harbigstraße in Westend, Berlin-Charlottenburg. Typical November weather is around 7 °C, with rainy days. Forest race on paved and unpaved forest paths, entry fee for non-members, late registration for an additional fee, November weather around 7 °C, rainy.

name: Schkölener Stadtparklauf
description: The Schkölen Stadtparklauf is a long-standing running event in Schkölen, Thuringia, taking place on November 7, 2026. Organized by TSV 1885 Schkölen and SSV Friedrich-Schiller-Gymnasium Eisenberg, the event offers various distances for children, teenagers, and young adults. The routes run through the town park and include short and long loops, combined according to age group. The event emphasizes clear age-group divisions and is aimed particularly at young runners.
course_highlights: Distances from 0.6 km to 5 km, tailored to age groups
Loops through the town park, combining short and long loops
Age groups determined by calendar year for fair competitions
additional: Age groups are determined by calendar year; for example, a 6-year-old runner in 2025 belongs to age group 6. Participants are asked to enter the correct age group when registering late. Various running distances, age-group divisions, registration with the correct age, looped running on the sports field

name: Sparkassen-LüneCross
description: The Sparkassen-LüneCross is an exciting and challenging cross-country running event set amid nature and the city of Lüneburg. The varied course follows sandy, root-covered trails, meadows, forest paths and gravel tracks, testing endurance, strength and running technique. Main races are offered over 4 km and 8 km, along with shorter distances for children and young people and 8 km relay races. Alongside the sporting challenge, the focus is on the enjoyment of running and community, with a school competition and a convivial awards ceremony afterwards.
course_highlights: Varied terrain with sandy, root-covered trails
Routes through meadows, forest paths and gravel tracks
8 km relay races can be run by teams of 3 to 6 runners
additional: There is a school competition with prizes for schools with the highest participation rate. Food and refreshments are available, followed by an awards ceremony and a convivial get-together. Relay teams of 3 to 6 runners can be formed from family, colleagues, teammates or friends. The route passes through natural surroundings, including forest paths, meadows, sand and gravel. Registration is required; family and group participation is possible.

name: Lauf Winterlaufserie 2026/2027
description: The 1st Winter Running Series 2026/2027 in Beverstedt-Wellen is a winter running series connected with the traditional Rund um Wellen event. It is organized by the local running club, which also runs the historic Wellen Marathon, one of the oldest marathons in Germany. The event offers a welcoming, family atmosphere, various distance options, and strong local support from volunteers, sponsors, and the local fire brigade. The organizers aim to preserve the event’s well-established challenge and familiar character.
course_highlights: Part of the long-standing Rund um Wellen event, with four distances
Rural, family-friendly atmosphere, organized by a local club
Strong local support from volunteers and the fire brigade
additional: Typical November weather: average 7 °C (minimum 2 °C) with frequent rain (45 mm of precipitation). Start location: Beverstedt-Wellen. Terrain: mixed. Registration: not specified. Further notes: Part of the Rund um Wellen event, with local support and volunteers involved.

name: 50. Hermann-Löns-Park-Lauf
location: Hermann-Löns-Park, Hannover-Wülferode, Hannover, Lower Saxony, Germany
description: The Hermann-Löns-Park Run in Hannover-Kirchrode is a traditional road and fun run held annually in early November. The event offers various distances from 400 m to 10 km, officially measured and approved by the German Athletics Association. It is known for its family-friendly atmosphere, volunteer support, and professional timekeeping. Runners can enjoy a raffle and refreshments in the finish area, making it a popular event in the region.
course_highlights: Officially measured 5 km and 10 km courses in accordance with German Athletics Association standards
Run through Hermann-Löns-Park in Hannover-Kirchrode
Various distances from 400 m to 10 km for all age groups
additional: Late entries are possible on site on Saturday from 14:00 to 16:00 and on Sunday from 9:00 until 45 minutes before the start. Race numbers can be collected on both days. Electronic timekeeping is used, with results recorded via race number. Spikes are not allowed and may lead to disqualification. The event takes place in all weather conditions. A €2 deposit for the race number is payable at registration. Courses from 1.5 km to 10 km, marathon relay, registration and results online

name: Braunschweiger Speed5
description: Braunschweiger Speed5 is the fastest fun run in the city of Braunschweig, organised by Polizeisportverein Braunschweig and Braunschweiger Laufclub. The running event on November 8, 2026, offers exciting races for recreational and competitive runners of all ages, including an 800 m children’s race, a 1-mile schoolchildren’s race and a measured 5 km race. The event features professional chip timing, a clear cutoff time for the fast 5 km race, and a friendly atmosphere with refreshments at the finish and music. Awards ceremonies recognise the top female and male runners in various age groups and main races.
course_highlights: Measured 5 km course with a 22-minute cutoff in the fast race
800 m children’s race and 1-mile schoolchildren’s race
Professional chip timing and awards for top finishers
additional: Race bib collection starts at 09:15 on the grounds of Polizeisportverein. Refreshments are available for runners at the finish, with musical entertainment by DJ Carlito. Paramedics will be on site for safety. A pacemaker will be available in the slower 5 km race to help runners achieve times under 20 minutes. Certificates can be accessed online or on site after the race. Course: measured 5 km, children’s and schoolchildren’s races. Registration via RaceResults. Parking is available along Georg-Westermann-Allee and Ebertallee. The event takes place in Prinzenpark.

name: Hohen Neuendorfer Herbstlauf
description: The Hohen Neuendorf Autumn Run is a traditional running event that has been held in Hohen Neuendorf since 1900 and is considered the birthplace of cross-country running in Germany. The run attracts numerous participants from the region and beyond each year and offers distances for all age groups, from a children’s run to longer distances. The event brings generations together and is supported by many volunteers and local partners. It traditionally takes place in November and is a fixture on the regional sporting calendar.
course_highlights: Traditional cross-country run with a history dating back to 1900
Participants spanning generations, from age 3 to over 90
Support from local clubs and reservists along the course
additional: The run includes various distances, including a 400-metre children’s run and a 5.5 km course. The event is supported by many volunteers, including the Roter Adler Reservists from Lehnitz. The Autumn Run is one of the largest running events in the Oberhavel district and attracts participants from various regions. It takes place at the Rudolf Harbig sports ground and is weather-dependent. Registration is via MyRacepartner. The event is known for its historical significance in cross-country running in Germany and promotes a sense of community through sport.

name: Lop dwasch dörn Wildenloh
location: Wildenloh bei Oldenburg, Landkreis Oldenburg, Niedersachsen, Germany
description: Lop dwasch dörn Wildenloh is a traditional cross-country run held in early November on the beautiful fitness trail in Wildenloh, west of Oldenburg. The name means “Run across Wildenloh” and reflects the event’s rustic character: it takes place in the forest, without showers. The event is organised by the sports club Team Laufrausch e.V., which creates a friendly, nature-oriented running atmosphere.
course_highlights: Cross-country run on the local fitness trail in Wildenloh
Rustic forest course without showers
Traditional event with regional character
additional: The run takes place on a rustic forest course without showers. Several distances are offered (short course: 1600m, middle course: 3200m), and results from previous years are available. The event is organised by the sports club Team Laufrausch e.V. The run is held annually in November. There are no showers on site, results are published, and categories include children and adults.

name: Mausebergecrosslauf
description: The Mauseberge Cross-Country Run is an autumn cross-country race held in the Mauseberge Forest near Husum in northern Germany. The course follows natural forest trails over uneven terrain, with mud and several climbs. The event is organized by the athletics department of Husumer Sportverein and is a long-standing fixture on the regional race calendar.
course_highlights: Natural forest trails in the Mauseberge Forest
Uneven, muddy terrain
Several climbs
additional: The start is in Husum, and the venue can be reached by car. Typical November weather averages 7 °C (minimum 2 °C), with frequent rain (about 45 mm of precipitation). The race takes place in November in typical autumn weather, with temperatures around 2–7 °C and rain. Registration with the organizer is recommended. Places are available for various distances, including 1 km, 3.35 km, 5 km, 6.67 km, and 8.33 km.

name: Quickborn Run über 5 km und 10 km
description: The Quickborn Run is organized by TuS Holstein Quickborn and will be held for the 47th time in 2026. There are two race distances, 5 km and 10 km, starting in Quickborn on November 8. Childcare is available for families with young children, allowing parents to take part as well. The event offers changing facilities, free parking and a free timing chip on loan. The races are open to young people aged 12 and 14 and up, respectively, and follow the rules of the German Athletics Regulations.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km race routes
Start and finish at Dietrich-Bonhoeffer-Gymnasium in Quickborn
Free timing chip on loan
additional: Start times: 10:00 a.m. for the 5 km race, 11:00 a.m. for the 10 km race. Race pack collection from 8:00 to 10:30 a.m. at Dietrich-Bonhoeffer-Gymnasium. Changing facilities in the sports hall. Free parking at the sports hall and in the AKN station parking garage. Participation from age 12 for the 5 km and age 14 for the 10 km. Registration opens on 1.7.2026 via the Race Result portal. Late registration is possible on the day of the event, but participant numbers are limited, particularly for the 5 km race. Distances: 5 km and 10 km; minimum ages: 12 for the 5 km and 14 for the 10 km; limited places; parking at the sports hall and AKN station parking garage.

name: Süderelbe Halbmarathon durch das Alte Land
price_range: 20 Euro Halbmarathon, 18 Euro 10 km, 5 Euro Kinderlauf
description: The 50th Süderelbe Half Marathon through the Altes Land takes place on November 8, 2026. The course starts at the CU Arena at Neugraben S-Bahn station, runs through the Altes Land to Neuenfelde, and returns to the start. In addition to the half marathon, there are 10 km and 5 km races, a 5 km walking event, and a 1.2 km children’s race. The event is organized by Hausbruch-Neugrabener Turnerschaft von 1911 e.V. and offers a varied program for runners of all ages.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the CU Arena, Neugraben S-Bahn station
Course through the scenic Altes Land to Neuenfelde
Return to the starting point along the same route
additional: The program includes 10 km and 5 km races, a 5 km walking event, and a 1.2 km children’s race. The organizer is Hausbruch-Neugrabener Turnerschaft von 1911 e.V., with office hours Mon–Fri 09:00–11:00 and Mon–Thu 16:00–18:00. The event features a course through the Altes Land, various race distances, a children’s race, a walking event, a course closing time of 12:30, parking at the P+R car park at Neugraben S-Bahn station, race-number pickup on the day of the event, refreshments along the course, and medals and certificates for participants.

name: Wernigeröder Armeleuteberglauf
description: The Wernigeröder Armeleuteberglauf is a challenging trail race in November that starts and finishes at Haus Blume in Wernigerode. The route takes runners to the Kaiserturm and offers a varied challenge, with narrow forest paths, muddy sections and steep climbs. In addition to the main races over 5.4 km and 10 km, there are also children’s races over 1 km and 2.1 km. The event is organized by Harz-Gebirgslauf 1978 e.V. Wernigerode and, with around 160 participants, is a popular local tradition that also includes a pasta party on the evening before the race.
course_highlights: Trail race on narrow forest paths
Steep climbs to the Kaiserturm
Muddy and fast downhill sections
additional: The event has four distances: 1 km and 2.1 km for children, and 5.4 km and 10 km for the main races, which start together later in the morning. A pasta party on the evening before the race is a small local tradition. Trail character with challenging climbs; registration by email; pasta party on Saturday evening at Waldgasthaus Armeleuteberg.

name: Stadtparkstaffelmarathon
description:
All information about the 2024 Stadtpark Relay Marathon organized by the marathon department of FC St. Pauli von 1910 e.V.

Date: Sunday, 04 October 2026, 10:00 a.m. (finish cutoff: 3:00 p.m.)

Start / finish: “Jahnkampfbahn” (stadium), Stadtpark, Linnering 3, 22299 Hamburg

Course and format: Relay race, 5 participants per team—women’s, men’s, mixed (at least 2 women). Each team member runs two laps of 4.2 km each on paths in the western part of Stadtpark (around the planetarium). Course marshals will be present. A detailed course map can be viewed at the end of the page.

Registration: by email to staffelmarathon@marathon.fcstpauli.com

Registration deadline: 20.09.2026

Required information: First and last names of all relay team members, the relay team’s name, and whether the team is a women’s, men’s, or mixed team.

name: Marceliński Bieg Jesienny 2026
description: Marceliński Autumn Run 2026 is a cross-country race organized in Poznań by running enthusiasts from the Biegi.Wlkp. group. The event takes place on scenic courses that showcase the location’s aesthetic appeal. Since 2014, the organizers have focused on promoting cross-country running in Wielkopolska, offering participants a unique running experience in beautiful natural surroundings.
course_highlights: A cross-country race on scenic routes in Poznań
Courses that showcase the location’s aesthetic appeal
Organized by experienced running enthusiasts from Wielkopolska
additional: The race route is available on Garmin Connect. Race packs can be collected using an authorization form template. Cross-country race, event in Marceliński Forest, November 8, 2026, puzzle-piece medals, forest routes

name: Poznański Bieg Niepodległości – Kocham Polskę!
location: Strzeszyn, Poznań, Greater Poland Voivodeship, Poland
price_range: 20 zł za koszulkę techniczną, wpisowe na stronie nie jest wyraźnie podane
description: The Poznań Independence Run – I Love Poland! is a cross-country race held in picturesque locations in Poznań, particularly in Strzeszyn near Malibu Beach. The event is part of the activities of a group of running enthusiasts who have been promoting cross-country running in Greater Poland since 2014, with an emphasis on attractive courses and the sporting character of the event. The race has a patriotic dimension and takes place on 11 November, combining sport with a celebration of Poland’s independence. Runners are invited to take part in a range of distances amid beautiful natural surroundings.
course_highlights: Cross-country course around Strzeszyn and Malibu Beach
Picturesque green areas of Poznań
A patriotic race held on 11 November
additional: The organiser is a group of running enthusiasts from Greater Poland, active since 2014 and specialising in cross-country races. The race takes place in the green areas of Strzeszyn, near Malibu Beach. The event has a patriotic character and is part of the Poznań Running Triad. Participant limit: 750; picturesque courses; cross-country races.

name: 9 Olsztyński Bieg Niepodległości
location: Centrum Rekreacyjno-Sportowe Ukiel, Olsztyn, Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship, Poland
description: The Olsztyn Independence Run is an annual patriotic sporting event held in Olsztyn, combining the joy of running with celebrations of Independence Day. The event is open to everyone, from experienced runners to families with children. The races take place at the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre and include 5 km and 10 km runs, Nordic walking, and children’s races of up to 400 metres. The atmosphere is lively despite the autumn weather, and places are limited, with online registration open until 6 November.
course_highlights: The 5 km and 10 km routes run through the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre grounds and along nearby streets: Sielska, Schumana and Kapitańska
The event combines sporting competition with patriotic celebrations
Nordic walking and children’s races of up to 400 metres are also available
additional: The start and finish are located at the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre. The event takes place on 11 November, and registration is open online until 6 November. Participants can choose from the 5 km and 10 km runs, Nordic walking, and children’s races of up to 400 m. Traffic disruptions should be expected along the race route. Traffic disruptions along the route; start at 9:00; registration until 6 November; event at the Ukiel Recreation and Sports Centre and on Sielska, Schumana and Kapitańska streets.

name: Gdyński Bieg Niepodległości
description: The Gdynia Independence Run is an annual running event held in Gdynia and part of the 2026 Gdynia Grand Prix. The 10 km main race attracts runners of all ages, and there are also races for children and young people. The event combines sport and recreation, with participants able to expect professional organization and an atmosphere celebrating Poland’s independence. Photos and video footage are taken during the event for the organizers’ promotional purposes.
course_highlights: 10 km main race
Races for children and young people
Part of the 2026 Gdynia Grand Prix
additional: Photos and video footage will be taken during the event to promote events organized by GCS and the Municipality of the City of Gdynia. Registration until October 28, 2026; results, photo galleries, and information about event partners are available.

name: II Bieg Legionów Polskich
description: The 2nd Polish Legions Run commemorates the anniversary of Poland regaining its independence and offers two distances: 5 km and 10 km. The starts take place in scenic coastal locations: Władysławowo, Rozewie and Jastrzębia Góra. The organizer provides transport from Jastrzębia Góra to the start locations and opens the race office on the day before and on race day. The course is available online, allowing participants to familiarize themselves with the route before the start.
course_highlights: The course passes through Władysławowo, Rozewie and Jastrzębia Góra
The 10 km race starts by the General Haller monument on Morska Street in Władysławowo
The 5 km race starts by the bust of Marshal Piłsudski on Garnizonowa Street in Rozewie
additional: Transport from Jastrzębia Góra to the start locations is provided. The race office is open on 10 November 2025 from 14:30 to 15:30 at OSiR Władysławowo, and on 11 November 2025 from 10:20 to 10:50 in Jastrzębia Góra. The course is available online at https://www.traseo.pl/trasa/bieg-legionow-polskich. Registration runs from 22 September to 5 November 2025; the event takes place on routes with moderate elevation gain, starting in Władysławowo and Rozewie.

name: XXXVIII Goleniowska Mila Niepodległości o Puchar Burmistrza Gminy Goleniów
description: The 38th Goleniów Independence Mile is an annual one-mile race held to celebrate Independence Day in Goleniów. The event offers an opportunity to celebrate Poland’s independence together through sport, promoting a healthy lifestyle and the local community. The race takes place in Goleniów and is open to everyone, regardless of age or experience level.
course_highlights: A one-mile race
Held to celebrate Independence Day
Supports the local community and promotes physical activity
additional: The race takes place on 11 November 2026 in Goleniów and is part of the region’s Independence Day celebrations.

name: 20 Gminne Biegi z okazji Święta Niepodległości
1. Prusicki Bieg Niepodległości
location: Prusice, Trzebnica County, Lower Silesian Voivodeship, Poland

name: III KÓRNICKI BIEG ZAMOYSKIEGO
location: Kórnickie Centrum Rekreacji i Sportu OAZA
organizer: Kórnickie Centrum Rekreacji i Sportu OAZA
description:
Edition celebrating the “Year of Kórnik Heritage”

Date: Sunday, 27 September 2026, at 10:00

Venue: Kórnickie Centrum Rekreacji i Sportu OAZA – Błonie.

The course follows the charming promenade along Lake Kórnickie, then speeds through the streets of Bnin before the final section leads into the quiet, picturesque Zwierzyniec Experimental Forest. This is a run with varied terrain: from paved routes to dirt trails surrounded by woodland.

Start/Finish: ul. Błonie, 62-035 Kórnik

10 km race

Entries will be accepted online only until 31 August 2026.

Participation in the “Bieg Zamoyskiego” is paid:
- Basic package – 80zł
- Extended package with a T-shirt – 130zł

Runner limit: 400
